description: Walt Disney's pioneering animation showcase, set to classical music conducted by Leopold Stokowski and introducing stereophonic Fantasound, debuted in New York on November 13, 1940.

title: ISRO PSLV-C30 Launches Astrosat India First Dedicated Multi-Wavelength Space Observatory
description: ISRO launched Astrosat aboard PSLV-C30 on September 28, 2015 from Sriharikota alongside six international customer satellites, providing simultaneous multi-wavelength astronomical observations.

title: President Bill Clinton Arrives in New Delhi on First US Presidential Visit to India in Decades
description: US President Bill Clinton touched down in New Delhi on March 21, 2000 for a historic five-day state visit that fundamentally transformed bilateral relations with Prime Minister Vajpayee.

title: ISRO PSLV-C3 Launches TES Satellite Providing Sub-Metre Resolution Imagery
description: ISRO launched the Technology Experiment Satellite from Sriharikota on September 21, 2001 aboard PSLV-C3, demonstrating high-resolution panchromatic imaging sensors for defence and mapping.

title: ISRO PSLV-C6 Injects Cartosat-1 and HAMSAT into Sun-Synchronous Polar Orbit
description: ISRO's PSLV-C6 launched Cartosat-1 stereoscopic mapping satellite and HAMSAT micro-satellite on May 5, 2005 from the newly commissioned Second Launch Pad at Sriharikota.

title: ISRO GSLV-F04 Launches INSAT-4CR Communications Satellite from Sriharikota
description: ISRO successfully launched the 2,130 kg INSAT-4CR high-power broadcasting satellite into geosynchronous transfer orbit aboard GSLV-F04 on September 2, 2007.

title: United Kingdom Votes in Referendum to Leave European Union with 52 Percent Voting Leave
description: British voters decided by 51.89 percent to 48.11 percent on June 23, 2016 to exit the European Union, prompting Prime Minister David Cameron to announce his immediate resignation.

title: Donald Trump Elected 45th President of United States Defeating Hillary Clinton
description: Republican nominee Donald Trump captured 304 electoral votes on November 8, 2016, defeating former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton in one of the biggest upsets in US political history.

title: Russian Ambassador to Turkey Andrei Karlov Assassinated at Art Exhibition in Ankara
description: Off-duty Turkish police officer Mevlut Mert Altintas shot Russian envoy Andrei Karlov in the back during an art gallery speech on December 19, 2016, shouting slogans about Aleppo.

title: Michael Curtiz Romantic Drama Casablanca Premieres at Hollywood Theater in New York
description: Starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman as star-crossed lovers Rick and Ilsa, Warner Bros' classic drama Casablanca premiered in New York City on November 26, 1942.

title: Antoine de Saint-Exupery Novella The Little Prince First Published in New York City
description: Reynal & Hitchcock published French aviator Antoine de Saint-Exupery's poetic novella The Little Prince in both English and French in New York City on April 6, 1943.

title: Ernest Hemingway Pulitzer-Winning Novella The Old Man and the Sea Published in Life Magazine
description: Life magazine published Ernest Hemingway's full 27,000-word tale of Cuban fisherman Santiago and his titanic struggle with a giant marlin on September 1, 1952, selling five million copies.

title: JRR Tolkien The Two Towers Published as Second Volume of The Lord of the Rings
description: George Allen & Unwin published the middle volume of JRR Tolkien's epic masterwork in Britain on November 11, 1954, chronicling the breaking of the fellowship and the Battle of Helm's Deep.

title: JRR Tolkien The Return of the King Published Completing The Lord of the Rings Trilogy
description: The concluding installment of JRR Tolkien's fantasy trilogy was published in the United Kingdom on October 20, 1955, culminating in the destruction of the One Ring in Mount Doom.

title: Lerner and Loewe Musical My Fair Lady Premieres at Mark Hellinger Theatre on Broadway
description: Starring Rex Harrison as Professor Henry Higgins and Julie Andrews as Eliza Doolittle, the adaptation of Pygmalion opened on Broadway on March 15, 1956 to universal critical acclaim.

title: Leonard Bernstein and Stephen Sondheim Musical West Side Story Premieres on Broadway
description: The groundbreaking musical setting Romeo and Juliet in Hell's Kitchen opened at the Winter Garden Theatre on September 26, 1957, with choreography by Jerome Robbins.

title: Rodgers and Hammerstein Musical The Sound of Music Premieres at Lunt-Fontanne Theatre
description: Mary Martin starred as Maria von Trapp in the original Broadway production of Rodgers and Hammerstein's final musical collaboration, opening in New York on November 16, 1959.

title: The Beatles Release Debut Single Love Me Do on Parlophone Records in UK
description: Recorded at Abbey Road Studios with producer George Martin, The Beatles released their first official UK single Love Me Do backed with P.S. I Love You on October 5, 1962.

title: Robert Wise Musical Film The Sound of Music Starring Julie Andrews Premieres in New York
description: Robert Wise's cinematic adaptation of the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical premiered at the Rivoli Theatre on March 2, 1965, becoming the highest-grossing film of its era.

title: Jim Morrison Lead Singer of The Doors Passes Away in Paris at Age 27
description: Charismatic rock icon and poet Jim Morrison was found dead in a bathtub at his apartment in Le Marais Paris on July 3, 1971, joining the tragic 27 Club.

title: Francis Ford Coppola Epic Crime Film The Godfather Premieres at Loew State Theatre in NYC
description: Starring Marlon Brando and Al Pacino in Mario Puzo's Mafia epic, Francis Ford Coppola's The Godfather premiered in New York on March 15, 1972, redefining cinema history.

title: Record 944mm Monsoonal Downpour Causes Catastrophic Flooding Across Mumbai
description: A historic meteorological cloudburst dumped 944 millimeters of rain on Mumbai in twenty-four hours on July 26, 2005, paralyzing the financial capital and claiming over one thousand lives.

title: Two Bombs Detonate Aboard Samjhauta Express Train at Diwana Near Panipat
description: Two improvised suitcase explosive devices exploded aboard the Delhi-to-Attari Samjhauta Express on February 18, 2007 at Diwana station, killing sixty-eight passengers.

title: Sri Lankan Cricket Team Bus Attacked by Gunmen in Lahore En Route to Match
description: Twelve masked terrorists opened fire with rifles and rocket launchers on the Sri Lankan cricket team convoy at Liberty Roundabout in Lahore on March 3, 2009, injuring six players.

title: United Progressive Alliance Wins Decisive Mandate in 15th Lok Sabha General Elections
description: The Indian National Congress-led UPA coalition secured 262 seats in general election results announced on May 16, 2009, returning Dr. Manmohan Singh to power for a second term.

title: Massive Northern and Eastern Electricity Grid Failure Leaves 620 Million Without Power
description: Cascading transmission overdraws triggered the collapse of the Northern, Eastern, and North-Eastern power grids on July 30, 2012, causing the largest blackout in human history across twenty-two states.

title: Hurricane Harvey Makes Landfall in Texas Causing Unprecedented Catastrophic Flooding
description: Category 4 Hurricane Harvey stalled over southeast Texas on August 25, 2017, dropping over sixty inches of rain and flooding hundreds of thousands of homes in greater Houston.

title: Category 5 Hurricane Maria Makes Devastating Direct Landfall Across Island of Puerto Rico
description: Packing 155 mph sustained winds, Hurricane Maria tore across Puerto Rico on September 20, 2017, completely destroying the electrical grid and leaving millions without power for months.

title: XXIII Olympic Winter Games Officially Open in Pyeongchang South Korea
description: The 2018 Winter Olympics opened at Pyeongchang Olympic Stadium on February 9, 2018, featuring North and South Korean athletes marching together under a unified Korean flag.

title: Francis Ford Coppola The Godfather Part II Premieres in New York City
description: Continuing the saga of the Corleone family through parallel timelines of Michael and young Vito, Coppola's masterwork premiered on December 12, 1974, winning six Academy Awards.

title: Queen Release Operatic Rock Masterpiece Single Bohemian Rhapsody in United Kingdom
description: Freddie Mercury's revolutionary six-minute suite combining ballad, operatic passage, and hard rock was released on October 31, 1975, topping the UK charts for nine consecutive weeks.

title: John G Avildsen Sports Drama Rocky Starring Sylvester Stallone Premieres in New York
description: Sylvester Stallone's Oscar-winning underdog boxing drama about Philadelphia fighter Rocky Balboa premiered in New York City on November 21, 1976, spawning a global media franchise.

title: The Empire Strikes Back Second Star Wars Film Directed by Irvin Kershner Premieres

description: Starring Harrison Ford as globe-trotting archaeologist Indiana Jones, Raiders of the Lost Ark was released in North America on June 12, 1981, becoming an instant cultural phenomenon.

title: Robert Zemeckis Sci-Fi Comedy Back to the Future Starring Michael J Fox Releases
description: Featuring a time-traveling DeLorean powered by a flux capacitor, Back to the Future opened in American theatres on July 3, 1985, topping the box office for eleven weeks.

title: James Cameron Sci-Fi Action Film Aliens Starring Sigourney Weaver Opens in Theatres
description: James Cameron's acclaimed sequel to Ridley Scott's sci-fi thriller opened in North American cinemas on July 18, 1986, earning Sigourney Weaver an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress.

title: Jonathan Demme Psychological Horror The Silence of the Lambs Premieres in US Theatres
description: Starring Jodie Foster as FBI trainee Clarice Starling and Anthony Hopkins as Dr. Hannibal Lecter, the psychological thriller opened on February 14, 1991, winning the Big Five Oscars.

title: Nirvana Release Breakthrough Grunge Album Nevermind Featuring Smells Like Teen Spirit
description: Produced by Butch Vig, Kurt Cobain and Nirvana released Nevermind on September 24, 1991, unseating Michael Jackson on the charts and bringing Pacific Northwest grunge to the global mainstream.

title: Steven Spielberg Holocaust Drama Schindler List Premieres in Washington DC
description: Filmed in black and white and starring Liam Neeson, Steven Spielberg's harrowing Holocaust masterpiece premiered on November 30, 1993, going on to win seven Academy Awards including Best Picture.

title: Walt Disney Animated Epic The Lion King Premieres in Theatres Grossing Over 700 Million
description: Featuring songs by Elton John and Tim Rice, Walt Disney Feature Animation's The Lion King debuted in wide release on June 23, 1994, becoming the highest-grossing hand-drawn animated film.

title: NBC Premieres Legendary Television Sitcom Friends Starring Ensemble Cast
description: Created by David Crane and Marta Kauffman, the pilot episode of Friends aired on NBC on September 22, 1994, beginning a ten-season run that became a worldwide television phenomenon.

title: Nanda Devi Glacier Burst Triggers Catastrophic Flash Flood in Chamoli Uttarakhand
description: A hanging glacier detachment on Ronti Peak unleashed rock and ice down Rishiganga valley on February 7, 2021, destroying two hydroelectric projects and killing over two hundred workers.

title: Mi-17V5 Helicopter Crash in Coonoor Kills Chief of Defence Staff General Bipin Rawat

title: Punjabi Music Artist Sidhu Moosewala Shot Dead in Mansa District of Punjab
description: Shubhdeep Singh Sidhu, celebrated globally for revolutionary Punjabi hip hop music, was ambushed and fatally shot in Jawaharke village on May 29, 2022, sparking international mourning.

description: A historic British-era pedestrian suspension bridge reopened days earlier collapsed under hundreds of visitors on October 30, 2022, pitching crowds into the Machchhu River and claiming 141 lives.

description: Two men breached security inside the Lok Sabha chamber during Zero Hour on December 13, 2023, jumping from the gallery and opening color smoke canisters on the 2001 attack anniversary.

title: Wild Boars Junior Association Football Team Trapped Inside Flooded Tham Luang Cave in Thailand
description: Twelve boys and their assistant coach became trapped inside the Tham Luang Nang Non cave system on June 23, 2018 when sudden heavy monsoon downpours flooded the subterranean exit tunnels.

title: Magnitude 7.5 Sulawesi Earthquake and Tsunami Devastate Palu Indonesia Killing 4300
description: A strike-slip earthquake triggered massive soil liquefaction and a destructive localized tsunami in Palu Bay on September 28, 2018, sweeping away coastal communities in Central Sulawesi.

description: National Thowheeth Jama'ath suicide bombers attacked St. Anthony's Shrine, St. Sebastian's, and Colombo luxury hotels on April 21, 2019, killing 269 worshippers and guests.

title: Quentin Tarantino Pulp Fiction Opens in North American Theatres Across 1338 Screens
description: Starring John Travolta and Samuel L. Jackson in nonlinear interconnected crime vignettes, Quentin Tarantino's Cannes-winning Pulp Fiction opened widely on October 14, 1994 to critical ecstasy.

title: James Cameron Epic Romantic Disaster Film Titanic Starring DiCaprio and Winslet Releases
description: James Cameron's monumental 200-million-dollar recreation of the 1912 maritime disaster opened on December 19, 1997, becoming the first film to surpass one billion dollars at the box office.

title: Peter Jackson The Lord of the Rings The Two Towers Opens in Theatres Worldwide
description: Peter Jackson's second Middle-earth installment premiered internationally on December 18, 2002, featuring the groundbreaking photorealistic CGI character Gollum and the Battle of Helm's Deep.

title: Peter Jackson The Lord of the Rings The Return of the King Premieres in Theatres
description: The epic fantasy conclusion The Return of the King had its world premiere in Wellington on December 17, 2003, concluding the cinematic trilogy with unanimous acclaim and record ticket sales.

title: The Lord of the Rings The Return of the King Sweeps All Eleven Academy Award Nominations
description: At the 76th Academy Awards in Hollywood on February 29, 2004, The Return of the King tied Ben-Hur and Titanic by winning all eleven Oscars it was nominated for, including Best Picture.

title: Sears Tower in Chicago Completed Becoming World Tallest Building at 1451 Feet
description: Architect Bruce Graham and structural engineer Fazlur Khan's bundled-tube skyscraper was topped out in Chicago on May 3, 1974, holding the title of world's tallest building for twenty-four years.

title: Petronas Twin Towers in Kuala Lumpur Formally Surpass Sears Tower as World Tallest
description: Architect Cesar Pelli's twin 88-floor Islamic-inspired towers in Kuala Lumpur were certified as the tallest buildings on Earth on August 31, 1998, connected by a skybridge on floors 41 and 42.

title: London Eye Observation Wheel Opens to General Paying Public on South Bank
description: Designed by Marks Barfield Architects, the 135-meter cantilevered observation wheel on the River Thames welcomed its first public ticket holders on March 9, 2000, becoming a British icon.

title: Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant Unit 3 Shut Down Completely Decommissioning Site
description: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma ordered the permanent shutdown of Chernobyl's last operational reactor Unit 3 on December 15, 2000, ending power generation at the infamous disaster plant.

title: Fourteen-Year-Old Leonard Thompson Receives First Injection of Insulin for Diabetes
description: Dying from juvenile diabetes at Toronto General Hospital, Leonard Thompson was administered an improved extract of purified bovine insulin on January 11, 1922, making a remarkable recovery.

title: ISRO PSLV-C10 Successfully Launches Israeli TecSAR Synthetic Aperture Radar Satellite
description: ISRO's PSLV-C10 successfully injected the 300 kg Israeli TecSAR synthetic aperture radar spacecraft into an accurate low Earth orbit from Sriharikota on January 21, 2008.

title: ISRO PSLV-C14 Launches Oceansat-2 Along with Six European Nanosatellites
description: ISRO's PSLV-C14 launched Oceansat-2 along with four German and two Swiss nanosatellites on September 23, 2009, providing vital ocean color and surface wind vector data.

title: ISRO PSLV-C15 Successfully Injects Cartosat-2B and Four Auxiliary Satellites
description: ISRO launched Cartosat-2B alongside Indian ALSAT-2A and three university nanosatellites on July 12, 2010 from Sriharikota, enhancing national high-resolution cadastral mapping.

title: ISRO PSLV-C17 Places GSAT-12 Communications Satellite into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit
description: ISRO's PSLV-XL C17 successfully launched the 1,410 kg GSAT-12 communications satellite into transfer orbit on July 15, 2011 to augment transponder capacity for healthcare and tele-education.

title: Italy Defeats England on Penalties at Wembley Stadium to Win UEFA Euro 2020 Championship
description: Following a 1-1 draw after extra time, Italy goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma saved two penalties at Wembley on July 11, 2021 to secure Italy's second European Championship triumph.

title: Final US Military Transport Aircraft Departs Kabul Airport Ending Twenty-Year War in Afghanistan
description: A C-17 Globemaster III carrying Major General Chris Donahue lifted off from Hamid Karzai International Airport at 23:59 local time on August 30, 2021, concluding America's longest military engagement.

title: Jonas Salk Announces Successful Vaccine Against Polio in National Radio Broadcast
description: Dr. Jonas Salk revealed the breakthrough results of his injectable polio vaccine trials during a CBS nationwide radio broadcast on March 26, 1953, bringing hope to terrified families.

title: Ali Maow Maalin in Somalia Contracts World Last Documented Natural Smallpox Case
description: Hospital cook Ali Maow Maalin in Merca Somalia developed smallpox rash on October 26, 1977, recovered fully, and became celebrated in medical history as the final naturally occurring smallpox patient.

title: Abraham Lincoln Inaugurated as 16th President of United States as Civil War Looms
description: Abraham Lincoln took the presidential oath on the East Portico of the Capitol on March 4, 1861, appealing to 'the better angels of our nature' to preserve the union as seven southern states seceded.

title: Abraham Lincoln Succumbs to Gunshot Wound Andrew Johnson Sworn in as President
description: President Lincoln passed away at 7:22 AM on April 15, 1865 at the Petersen House across from Ford's Theatre, with Vice President Andrew Johnson taking the oath in his hotel parlor.

title: Global Outage Knocks Offline Meta Platforms Facebook Instagram and WhatsApp for Hours
description: A routine Border Gateway Protocol configuration error severed Meta's data centers on October 4, 2021, cutting off Facebook, WhatsApp, and Instagram for 3.5 billion users for six hours.

title: Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai Submarine Volcano Explodes in Massive Atmospheric Blast
description: A colossal underwater volcanic eruption on January 15, 2022 generated atmospheric shockwaves that circled the planet multiple times and triggered Pacific-wide tsunamis.

title: Nazi German Troops March into Undefended French Capital Paris
description: Wehrmacht infantry units occupied the French capital on June 14, 1940 after Paris was declared an open city, raising the swastika flag over the Eiffel Tower and Arc de Triomphe.

title: Soviet Union Detonates 50-Megaton Tsar Bomba World Largest Thermonuclear Weapon at Novaya Zemlya
description: A Tu-95V bomber dropped the RDS-220 Tsar Bomba over Mityushikha Bay on October 30, 1961, creating an atmospheric fireball visible 600 miles away with an explosive yield of fifty megatons.

title: May 68 Student Protests and General Strike Bring French Economy to Standstill
description: Tens of thousands of students clashed with riot police in the Latin Quarter on May 10, 1968, sparking a general strike of eleven million workers that brought Charles de Gaulle's government to crisis.

title: Cinema Rex Arson Fire in Abadan Iran Kills Over 420 Civilians Catalysing Revolution
description: Four militants locked the doors and poured aviation fuel into Cinema Rex during a screening on August 20, 1978, incinerating over 420 patrons and galvanizing public fury against the Shah.

title: Mexico Finance Secretary Jesus Silva Herzog Informs Creditors Nation Cannot Service Foreign Debt
description: Mexican finance officials informed international banks on August 12, 1982 that Mexico was unable to service its 80-billion-dollar foreign debt, triggering the Latin American debt crisis.

title: ISRO PSLV-C20 Injects SARAL Indo-French Oceanographic Satellite into Polar Orbit
description: ISRO launched the 407 kg Indo-French SARAL ocean altimetry satellite and six co-passenger satellites into sun-synchronous orbit on February 25, 2013 from Sriharikota.

title: ISRO PSLV-C22 Launches IRNSS-1A First Dedicated Satellite of NavIC Constellation
description: ISRO's PSLV-XL C22 launched IRNSS-1A on July 1, 2013, inaugurating the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System designed to provide independent positioning services across South Asia.

description: ISRO accomplished a historic technological milestone on January 5, 2014 as GSLV-D5 with an indigenous cryogenic engine successfully placed the GSAT-14 communications satellite into orbit.

title: ISRO PSLV-C24 Launches IRNSS-1B Second Navigation Satellite from Sriharikota
description: ISRO successfully launched the 1,432 kg IRNSS-1B navigation satellite aboard PSLV-C24 on April 4, 2014 into sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre.

title: ISRO PSLV-C23 Launches French SPOT-7 Earth Observation Satellite into Sun-Synchronous Orbit
description: With Prime Minister Narendra Modi witnessing the launch, PSLV-C23 launched the 714 kg French SPOT-7 satellite and four commercial spacecraft from Sriharikota on June 30, 2014.

title: Russian Black Sea Fleet Flagship Guided Missile Cruiser Moskva Sinks Following Missile Strike
description: The 12,000-ton Project 1164 Slava-class cruiser Moskva suffered catastrophic munitions detonations from Ukrainian Neptune anti-ship missiles on April 14, 2022, sinking while being towed.

title: Charles III Formally Proclaimed King of the United Kingdom at St James Palace Accession Council
description: The Accession Council met at St. James's Palace on September 10, 2022 in the first televised proclamation in British history, formally confirming Charles III as sovereign of the United Kingdom.

title: Subsea Explosions Rupture Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 Natural Gas Pipelines in Baltic Sea
description: Series of underwater detonations damaged three out of four strings of the Nord Stream pipeline near Bornholm Island on September 26, 2022, causing unprecedented methane boiling on the sea surface.

title: Haitian Dictator Jean-Claude Baby Doc Duvalier Flees Port-au-Prince Ending 28-Year Family Rule
description: President-for-life Jean-Claude Duvalier fled into French exile aboard a US military cargo plane on February 7, 1986 amidst escalating nationwide popular rebellions across Haiti.

description: West German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and East German Prime Minister Hans Modrow walked through the opened gates on December 22, 1989 in freezing rain before 100,000 cheering citizens.

description: Witness George Holliday filmed four LAPD officers striking motorist Rodney King over fifty times with batons on March 3, 1991, broadcasting police brutality to a shocked nation.

description: Guides Rob Hall and Scott Fischer were among eight mountaineers who died in the Death Zone on May 10, 1996 when a blinding blizzard trapped summit teams on the upper slopes of Everest.

description: Sheriff deputies discovered thirty-nine members of Marshall Applewhite's UFO cult dead in identical black clothing and Nike sneakers on March 26, 1997, having taken phenobarbital.

title: Pakistan Conducts Chagai-I Underground Nuclear Tests in Balochistan Becoming Nuclear Power
description: Under Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, Pakistan detonated five nuclear devices in the Ras Koh Hills on May 28, 1998, responding directly to India's Pokhran-II tests two weeks prior.

title: Bridge Creek-Moore F5 Tornado Devastates Suburban Oklahoma City with Record 301 Mph Winds
description: A violent multi-vortex tornado ripped a thirty-eight-mile path across central Oklahoma on May 3, 1999, generating radar-measured wind speeds of 301 mph, the highest ever recorded on Earth.

description: Over forty thousand direct-action activists shut down opening ceremonies of the World Trade Organization on November 30, 1999, prompting police to declare a civil emergency in downtown Seattle.

description: An internal hydrogen peroxide leak in a practice torpedo triggered two massive explosions on August 12, 2000, sinking the Project 949A Kursk 108 meters to the seabed with all crew.

title: ISRO PSLV-C26 Successfully Launches IRNSS-1C Navigation Satellite from Sriharikota
description: ISRO launched the IRNSS-1C satellite into geostationary orbit on October 16, 2014 aboard PSLV-C26, advancing India's indigenous regional satellite navigation network.

title: ISRO Successfully Flight Tests LVM3-X CARE Atmospheric Re-entry Experiment
description: ISRO launched the experimental LVM3-X rocket on December 18, 2014 carrying the 3.7-tonne CARE crew module, demonstrating successful atmospheric re-entry and splashdown in the Andaman Sea.

title: ISRO PSLV-C27 Successfully Places IRNSS-1D Fourth NavIC Navigation Satellite in Orbit
description: ISRO's PSLV-C27 successfully launched the 1,425 kg IRNSS-1D satellite on March 28, 2015 into sub-geosynchronous orbit, completing the minimum four-satellite constellation for navigation fixes.

title: ISRO PSLV-C28 Launches DMC3 Constellation in Heaviest Commercial Launch Mission
description: ISRO's PSLV-XL launched three DMC3 Earth observation satellites and two auxiliary payloads weighing 1,440 kg on July 10, 2015, marking Antrix's heaviest dedicated commercial mission.

title: ISRO GSLV-D6 Launches GSAT-6 Military Communications Satellite Using Indigenous Cryo Engine
description: ISRO's GSLV-D6 rocket successfully injected the GSAT-6 multimedia communication satellite into geosynchronous transfer orbit on August 27, 2015 with an indigenous cryogenic upper stage.

description: Edson Arantes do Nascimento, universally known as Pele and widely regarded as the greatest footballer in history, passed away from colon cancer in Sao Paulo on December 29, 2022.

title: Private Jet Carrying Wagner Chief Yevgeny Prigozhin Crashes in Tver Oblast Russia Killing All

description: An intraplate oblique-reverse earthquake struck southwest of Marrakesh on September 8, 2023, devastating historic brick and mud-stone mountain villages and killing 2,960 people.

description: Thousands of rockets and armed Hamas fighters breached the Gaza-Israel border barrier on October 7, 2023, massacring over 1,100 people at communities and the Nova music festival.

description: A major shallow earthquake struck the Noto Peninsula on New Year Day, January 1, 2024, toppling wooden homes, igniting extensive city fires in Wajima, and triggering coastal tsunamis.

description: Four gunmen affiliated with Islamic State Khorasan stormed the packed Crocus City Hall auditorium in Krasnogorsk on March 22, 2024, opening fire on concertgoers and setting the arena ablaze.

description: A Manhattan jury found Donald Trump guilty of thirty-four counts of falsifying business records on May 30, 2024, marking the first time in American history an ex-president was convicted of felonies.

title: Former Yugoslav President Slobodan Milosevic Arrested at His Belgrade Villa by Police
description: Serbian special police forces surrounded and arrested former dictator Slobodan Milosevic at his Dedinje residence on April 1, 2001, extraditing him to The Hague for war crimes trials.

description: En route to Santo Domingo, Flight 587 crashed into Belle Harbor Queens on November 12, 2001 after wake turbulence encounters and aggressive rudder pedal reversals sheared off its vertical stabilizer.

description: Dissident military officers detained Venezuelan President Hugo Chavez on April 11, 2002, but massive civilian protests and loyalist paratroopers restored him to Miraflores Palace within 47 hours.

description: Untrimmed trees contacting high-voltage power lines in Ohio triggered an unchecked transmission line cascade on August 14, 2003, blacking out eight states and Ontario within hours.

description: Jack Dorsey, Biz Stone, and Evan Williams officially launched Twitter to the general public on July 15, 2006, introducing the 140-character microblogging format that revolutionized real-time communications.

description: ULA's next-generation heavy-lift Vulcan Centaur rocket debuted from Cape Canaveral on January 8, 2024, successfully deploying Astrobotic's Peregrine commercial lunar lander.

title: Iran Launches Hundreds of Drones and Missiles in Direct Airstrike on Israel
description: The IRGC launched over three hundred suicide drones and cruise and ballistic missiles toward Israel on April 13, 2024, with Israeli and allied air defenses intercepting 99 percent.

description: A flurry of coronal mass ejections from solar sunspot region 3664 sparked the strongest geomagnetic storm since 2003 on May 8, 2024, painting night skies with auroras down to tropical latitudes.

title: Emperor Justinian Promulgates Fifty Books of the Pandects or Digest of Roman Law
description: Directed by jurist Tribonian, the comprehensive compilation of centuries of classical Roman legal opinions was formally confirmed on December 16, 533.

title: Emperor Leo III Issues Edict Ordering Removal of Religious Icons Initiating Byzantine Iconoclasm
description: Believing imperial crises were divine punishment for idolatry, Leo III enacted an imperial decree on January 17, 730 banning holy images across the Byzantine Empire.

title: Normans Under Robert Guiscard Capture Bari Ending Five Centuries of Byzantine Rule in Italy
description: Following a three-year siege, the Norman forces took the stronghold of Bari on April 16, 1071, expelling the last Eastern Roman garrison from southern Italy.

title: King Louis XVI and Royal Family Intercepted at Varennes During Flight from Paris
description: Attempting to escape to royalist strongholds near Montmedy, Louis XVI was recognized and detained on June 21, 1791, permanently destroying public faith in the constitutional monarchy.

title: Alexander Graham Bell Granted US Patent for Electric Telephone
description: Historical event: Alexander Graham Bell Granted US Patent for Electric Telephone took place on 1876-03-07.

description: Analyzing Geiger-Marsden gold foil alpha particle scattering in the Philosophical Magazine on May 7, 1911, Rutherford proved the atomic mass is concentrated in a tiny nucleus.

title: United Nations International Children Emergency Fund UNICEF Created by UNGA
description: Historical event: United Nations International Children Emergency Fund UNICEF Created by UNGA took place on 1946-12-11.

title: Prime Ministers Jawaharlal Nehru and Liaquat Ali Khan Sign Delhi Pact on Minority Rights
description: The bilateral Nehru-Liaquat Pact was concluded in New Delhi on April 8, 1950, pledging complete equality of citizenship and security for minorities in India and Pakistan.

title: Pan American World Airways Operates First Commercial Boeing 747 Flight Across Atlantic
description: Carrying 335 passengers and 20 crew members, Pan Am Clipper Victor flew from New York JFK to London Heathrow on January 22, 1970, launching jumbo jet travel.

title: Bill Gates and Paul Allen Found Microsoft in Albuquerque New Mexico
description: Historical event: Bill Gates and Paul Allen Found Microsoft in Albuquerque New Mexico took place on 1975-04-04.

title: West Germany Defeats Argentina in Rome to Win 1990 FIFA World Cup
description: Andreas Brehme converted an 85th-minute penalty kick on July 8, 1990 at the Stadio Olimpico, making Franz Beckenbauer the second person to win the World Cup as captain and coach.

title: European Space Agency Rosetta Spacecraft Launches Towards Comet 67P
description: An Ariane 5 rocket launched Rosetta and the Philae lander on March 2, 2004 from Kourou French Guiana, embarking on a decade-long voyage to orbit and land on comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko.

description: Bengaluru's rapid transit network launched services on October 20, 2011 between MG Road and Baiyappanahalli, becoming South India's first operational metro railway.

title: Twitter Debuts on New York Stock Exchange Soaring Seventy-Three Percent on First Day
description: Microblogging service Twitter listed on the NYSE under ticker TWTR on November 7, 2013, closing its first trading session at 44.90 dollars per share.

title: ISRO PSLV-C31 Launches IRNSS-1E Fifth NavIC Navigation Satellite into Geosynchronous Orbit
description: ISRO's PSLV-C31 successfully launched the IRNSS-1E navigation spacecraft on January 20, 2016 from Sriharikota, expanding India's independent positioning constellation.

title: President Xi Jinping Formally Opens Starfish-Shaped Beijing Daxing International Airport
description: Designed by Zaha Hadid Architects with a single 700,000-square-meter terminal, the massive mega-hub airport was inaugurated on September 25, 2019.

title: DRDO and Indian Navy Successfully Conduct First Flight Test of VL-SRSAM Missile
description: The indigenous Vertical Launch Short Range Surface to Air Missile was successfully tested from a static vertical launcher on February 22, 2021 off the Odisha coast.

title: Nikhat Zareen Wins Gold at World Women Boxing Championships in Istanbul
description: Indian boxer Nikhat Zareen defeated Thailand's Jutamas Jitpong 5-0 on May 19, 2022 to claim the flyweight gold medal at the IBA World Women's Boxing Championships.

title: Category 5 Hurricane Ian Makes Devastating Landfall Near Cayo Costa in Southwest Florida
description: Packing sustained winds of 240 km/h and a catastrophic 15-foot storm surge on September 28, 2022, Ian caused 112 billion dollars in damage, the third-costliest US hurricane.

title: Oppenheimer Dominates 96th Academy Awards Winning Seven Oscars Including Best Picture
description: Christopher Nolan's biographical epic about the father of the atomic bomb swept the Oscars on March 10, 2024, winning Best Picture, Director, Actor, and Supporting Actor.

title: Barricade Clashes Erupt in Berlin Between Prussian Troops and Citizens
description: Historical event: Barricade Clashes Erupt in Berlin Between Prussian Troops and Citizens took place on 1848-03-18.

description: Conducted by Anton Seidl on December 16, 1893 in New York, the ninth symphony drew standing ovations between movements, synthesizing Native American and African American themes.

title: Werner Heisenberg Formulates Uncertainty Principle in Historic Letter to Wolfgang Pauli
description: Heisenberg outlined on February 23, 1927 that the position and momentum of a subatomic particle cannot simultaneously be known with arbitrary precision.

title: Konrad Adenauer Elected as First Chancellor of Federal Republic of Germany
description: The Bundestag elected Christian Democratic leader Konrad Adenauer on September 15, 1949 by a one-vote margin, inaugurating the post-war West German democracy.

title: Parliament Enacts Air Corporations Act Nationalising Indian Airlines and Air India
description: The Government of India nationalised nine private airline operators on June 12, 1953, creating Indian Airlines for domestic routes and Air India International for overseas flights.

title: Education Minister Humayun Kabir Formally Inaugurates IIT Delhi at Hauz Khas
description: Established with collaboration and equipment assistance from the United Kingdom, IIT Delhi was formally dedicated on August 17, 1961 as a premier institute of technology.

title: Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew Announces Singapore Separation from Malaysia
description: Overcome with emotion in a televised press conference on August 9, 1965, Lee Kuan Yew proclaimed the Republic of Singapore an independent and sovereign democratic nation.

title: Brazil Wins Fourth World Cup Title in First Penalty Shootout Final in Pasadena
description: Following a 0-0 deadlock against Italy on July 17, 1994 at the Rose Bowl, Roberto Baggio's missed kick over the bar handed Brazil an emotional 3-2 shootout victory.

title: Zinedine Zidane Scores Twice as France Defeats Brazil to Win Maiden 1998 World Cup
description: Zidane headed two first-half corner kicks into the net on July 12, 1998 at the Stade de France, securing a memorable 3-0 victory for Les Bleus on home soil.

title: NASA Messenger Spacecraft Launches on Mission to Orbit Mercury
description: Carried aloft by a Delta II rocket on August 3, 2004 from Cape Canaveral, MESSENGER embarked on a 7.9-billion-kilometer journey to become the first probe to orbit the innermost planet.

title: NASA Deep Impact Spacecraft Successfully Impacts Comet Tempel 1
description: On July 4, 2005, the impactor probe from Deep Impact collided with comet Tempel 1 at 10.2 km/s, releasing pristine sub-surface debris for spectral analysis.

title: Alibaba Group Raises Record Twenty-Five Billion Dollars in Largest Global IPO on NYSE

description: The flight test was conducted on April 3, 2024 from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off Odisha, validating the canisterized propulsion and pre-fragmented warhead systems.

title: Michael Johnson Shatters Men 200m World Record in 19.32 Seconds at Atlanta Olympics
description: Running in custom golden spikes on August 1, 1996, Michael Johnson sliced more than three-tenths off the world record, completing an unprecedented 200m-400m Olympic double.

title: Lewis Hamilton Clinches Maiden Formula One World Championship on Final Corner in Interlagos
description: Passing Timo Glock in torrential rain on the final corner of the Brazilian Grand Prix on November 2, 2008, 23-year-old Hamilton became the youngest world champion at the time.

title: Juan Martin del Potro Stuns Five-Time Defending Champion Roger Federer to Win 2009 US Open
description: Twenty-year-old Argentine del Potro unleashed blistering forehands to rally past Federer in five sets on September 14, 2009, capturing his maiden Grand Slam title.

title: Rafael Nadal Defeats Novak Djokovic in Four Sets to Complete Career Grand Slam at US Open
description: Nadal won the rain-delayed final on September 13, 2010 at Flushing Meadows, becoming at age 24 the youngest man in the Open Era to win all four major tournaments.

title: Sebastian Vettel Wins Abu Dhabi Grand Prix Becoming Youngest Formula One World Champion
description: Overturning a 15-point deficit in a four-way championship decider on November 14, 2010, 23-year-old Red Bull driver Vettel claimed his first drivers' crown.

title: Usain Bolt Sets Olympic Record of 9.63 Seconds Winning 100m Gold at London Games
description: Defending his Olympic crown in blistering fashion on August 5, 2012 at London Olympic Stadium, Bolt posted the second-fastest 100m in history.

title: Andy Murray Defeats Novak Djokovic in Five-Set US Open Thriller to Win Maiden Grand Slam
description: Murray triumphed in four hours and 54 minutes on September 10, 2012, ending a 76-year drought for British male Grand Slam singles champions.

title: Sebastian Vettel Recovers from First-Lap Spin in Interlagos to Win Third F1 World Title
description: Surviving damage in a chaotic rain-soaked Brazilian Grand Prix on November 25, 2012, Vettel fought back to finish sixth and pip Fernando Alonso by three points.

title: King Felipe VI Formally Proclaimed King of Spain Following Abdication of Juan Carlos I
description: Following the abdication of King Juan Carlos I, Felipe VI was formally proclaimed King of Spain before the Cortes Generales in Madrid, ushering in a new era for the Spanish monarchy.

title: Usain Bolt Completes Historic Olympic 100m Three-Peat Winning Gold in Rio
description: Trailing Justin Gatlin at halfway on August 14, 2016 at the Maracana Stadium, Bolt surged ahead to clock 9.81 seconds, becoming the first athlete to win three 100m Olympic titles.

title: ISRO PSLV-C35 Successfully Launches Eight Satellites into Two Different Orbits
description: ISRO achieved an orbital maneuver first on September 26, 2016 as PSLV-C35 restarted its fourth stage twice to inject SCATSAT-1 and seven customer satellites into two distinct orbits.

title: Theresa May's Conservative Party Loses Parliamentary Majority in UK General Election
description: The United Kingdom held a snap general election resulting in a hung parliament, stripping Prime Minister Theresa May's Conservative Party of its majority and forcing a confidence agreement.

title: Daniil Medvedev Sweeps Novak Djokovic in US Open Final Denying Historic Calendar Grand Slam
description: Medvedev played flawless baseline tennis to win 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 on September 12, 2021 at Arthur Ashe Stadium, capturing his maiden major and stopping Djokovic's bid for all four slams.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Inaugurates Purvanchal Expressway in Sultanpur Uttar Pradesh
description: Spanning 341 kilometers from Lucknow to Ghazipur, the six-lane expressway with a 3.2-km airstrip for emergency fighter landings was inaugurated on November 16, 2021.

title: Max Verstappen Overtakes Lewis Hamilton on Final Lap of Abu Dhabi Grand Prix to Claim Maiden F1 Title
description: Following a controversial late safety car restart on December 12, 2021 at Yas Marina, Verstappen passed Hamilton on fresh soft tires on lap 58 to seize the championship.

title: DRDO Successfully Tests Extended Range Pinaka Rocket System at Pokhran Ranges
description: The upgraded multi-barrel Pinaka rocket launcher system demonstrated pinpoint accuracy in field trials on April 9, 2022 in the Rajasthan desert.

title: Carlos Alcaraz Wins 2022 US Open Becoming Youngest World Number One in ATP History
description: Nineteen-year-old Carlos Alcaraz defeated Casper Ruud in four sets on September 11, 2022 in New York, ascending to the top of the world rankings.

title: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty Claim Indonesia Open BWF Super 1000 Title
description: Rankireddy and Shetty swept world champions Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik on June 18, 2023 in Jakarta, becoming India's first ever doubles pair to win a Super 1000 crown.

title: President Droupadi Murmu Grants Assent to Three Criminal Law Reform Codes BNS BNSS and BSA
description: President Murmu signed the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam into law on December 25, 2023, replacing colonial-era penal codes.

title: Jannik Sinner Dominates Taylor Fritz in Straight Sets to Win Maiden US Open Title
description: World number one Jannik Sinner became the first Italian man to win the US Open on September 8, 2024, capping a dominant two-slam season at Flushing Meadows.

title: Michael Jordan Final Shot Gives Chicago Bulls Sixth NBA Championship in Utah
description: Stealing the ball from Karl Malone and burying a 17-foot jumper over Bryon Russell on June 14, 1998, Jordan sealed an 87-86 victory and his second three-peat with the Bulls.

title: Marat Safin Defeats Lleyton Hewitt to Win 2005 Australian Open Men Singles Title
description: Overcoming the partisan Melbourne crowd on January 30, 2005, Safin defeated Hewitt in four sets to claim his second career Grand Slam crown.

title: Novak Djokovic Claims Maiden Grand Slam Title Defeating Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in Melbourne
description: Twenty-year-old Serbian Novak Djokovic rallied past Tsonga 4-6, 6-4, 6-3, 7-6 on January 27, 2008 at Rod Laver Arena to win his first major trophy.

title: Novak Djokovic Outlasts Rafael Nadal in Longest Grand Slam Final in Australian Open History
description: Djokovic triumphed in five grueling sets lasting five hours and 53 minutes on January 29, 2012 in Melbourne, finishing at 1:37 AM.

title: Stan Wawrinka Defeats Injured Rafael Nadal to Win Maiden Major at 2014 Australian Open
description: Swiss eighth seed Stan Wawrinka broke through the Big Four's dominance on January 26, 2014, capturing his first Grand Slam with a four-set victory.

title: Parliament Enacts Real Estate Regulation and Development Act RERA
description: Aimed at protecting homebuyer interests and ensuring transparency in property sales, RERA received presidential assent on March 25, 2016.

title: LeBron James Leads Cleveland Cavaliers to Historic Game 7 NBA Finals Comeback Over Warriors
description: Completing the first recovery from 1-3 down in NBA Finals history, Cleveland won 93-89 in Oakland on June 19, 2016 behind 'The Block' by James and Kyrie Irving's tiebreaking three.

title: Roger Federer Defeats Rafael Nadal in Classic Five-Set 2017 Australian Open Final
description: Returning from a six-month injury layoff at age 35, Federer rallied from 1-3 down in the fifth set on January 29, 2017 to win his 18th Grand Slam title.

title: ISRO LVM3-D1 Successfully Launches GSAT-19 Satellite on Maiden Orbital Flight of Heavy Rocket
description: ISRO's heaviest rocket LVM3-D1 made its historic maiden developmental flight on June 5, 2017, placing the 3,136 kg GSAT-19 communications satellite into transfer orbit.

title: Giannis Antetokounmpo Scores 50 Points Leading Milwaukee Bucks to NBA Championship
description: Antetokounmpo delivered a historic Game 6 performance with 50 points, 14 rebounds, and five blocks on July 20, 2021, clinching the Bucks' first title in 50 years against Phoenix.

title: DRDO Successfully Flight Tests Indigenous Air Defence Anti-Tank Guided Missile Helina from Dhruv Helicopter
description: Launched from an Advanced Light Helicopter on April 11, 2022 at high altitude in Pokhran, the infrared-guided missile successfully hit simulated tank targets.

title: Stephen Curry and Golden State Warriors Defeat Boston Celtics to Win Fourth NBA Championship
description: Curry scored 34 points in Game 6 at TD Garden on June 16, 2022, securing a 103-90 win and earning his first unanimous NBA Finals MVP trophy.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Inaugurates Bundelkhand Expressway in Jalaun
description: The 296-kilometer four-lane expressway connecting Chitrakoot to the Agra-Lucknow expressway was formally opened to traffic on July 16, 2022, spurring regional industrial growth.

title: Nikola Jokic Leads Denver Nuggets to Maiden NBA Championship in Franchise History
description: Denver defeated the Miami Heat 94-89 in Game 5 on June 12, 2023 at Ball Arena, with Finals MVP Jokic capping a dominant playoff run to deliver Denver's first Larry O'Brien trophy.

title: Boston Celtics Defeat Dallas Mavericks in Game 5 to Clinch Record 18th NBA Championship
description: Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown led Boston to a 106-88 victory on June 17, 2024 at TD Garden, breaking a tie with the Los Angeles Lakers for the most championships in NBA history.

title: Three New Criminal Law Codes Officially Come into Force Across India
description: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, and Bharatiya Sakshya Act took effect on July 1, 2024, overhauling India's criminal justice system.

title: Leon Marchand Wins Two Olympic Swimming Gold Medals and Breaks Two Records in Single Evening
description: French swimmer Marchand won the 200m butterfly and 200m breaststroke within two hours on July 31, 2024 at Paris La Defense Arena, setting Olympic records in both.

title: Teddy Riner Wins Third Individual Olympic Judo Gold Medal in Paris
description: French heavyweight legend Teddy Riner threw South Korea's Kim Min-jong for ippon on August 2, 2024 at Champ-de-Mars Arena, winning his sixth overall Olympic medal.

title: Armand Duplantis Breaks Pole Vault World Record Clearing 6.25m to Win Paris Olympic Gold
description: Swedish sensation Mondo Duplantis cleared 6.25 meters on his third attempt on August 5, 2024 at the Stade de France, shattering his own world record before 75,000 cheering fans.

title: Stephen Curry Late Three-Point Barrage Seals Paris Olympic Gold for USA Men Basketball
description: Curry sank four spectacular three-pointers in the final two minutes on August 10, 2024 at Bercy Arena, powering the US past hosts France 98-87 for their fifth straight gold.

title: Rafael Nadal Wins Maiden French Open on Tournament Debut at Roland Garros
description: Two days after his 19th birthday, Nadal defeated Mariano Puerta in four sets on June 5, 2005, becoming the first man to win Roland Garros on debut since Mats Wilander.

title: New York Giants Stun Undefeated New England Patriots in Super Bowl XLII
description: David Tyree's miraculous helmet catch set up Plaxico Burress' winning touchdown on February 3, 2008 in Glendale, ruining New England's quest for an 18-0 perfect season.

title: Roger Federer Defeats Robin Soderling to Complete Career Grand Slam at French Open
description: Federer won in straight sets on June 7, 2009 at Court Philippe Chatrier, equalling Pete Sampras' record of 14 majors and completing his set of all four Slams.

title: Malcolm Butler Goal-Line Interception Wins Super Bowl XLIX for New England Patriots
description: Rookie cornerback Butler intercepted Russell Wilson at the one-yard line with twenty seconds remaining on February 1, 2015, securing a 28-24 win over Seattle.

title: Stan Wawrinka Stuns World Number One Novak Djokovic to Win 2015 French Open
description: Unleashing 60 blistering winners, Wawrinka recovered from a set down to defeat Djokovic 4-6, 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 on June 7, 2015, capturing his second Grand Slam title.

title: Novak Djokovic Defeats Andy Murray to Complete Career Grand Slam at French Open
description: Djokovic triumphed 3-6, 6-1, 6-2, 6-4 on June 5, 2016 at Roland Garros, becoming the first man since Rod Laver in 1969 to hold all four Grand Slam titles simultaneously.

title: Rafael Nadal Wins Historic Tenth Roland Garros Crown La Decima Without Dropping a Set
description: Demolishing Stan Wawrinka 6-2, 6-3, 6-1 on June 11, 2017, Nadal became the first tennis player in the Open Era to win ten titles at a single major tournament.

title: ISRO PSLV-C38 Launches Cartosat-2E Along with Thirty International Nanosatellites
description: ISRO's PSLV-C38 launched the Cartosat-2 series satellite alongside twenty-nine foreign nanosatellites from fourteen countries on June 23, 2017 from Sriharikota.

title: Nick Foles and Philadelphia Eagles Outduel Tom Brady to Win Maiden Super Bowl LII
description: Foles caught the famous 'Philly Special' touchdown pass on February 4, 2018 in Minneapolis, guiding Philadelphia to a thrilling 41-33 victory over New England.

title: Patrick Mahomes Rallies Kansas City Chiefs in Fourth Quarter to Win Super Bowl LIV
description: Trailing by ten points with seven minutes left on February 2, 2020 in Miami, Mahomes orchestrated three straight touchdown drives to defeat San Francisco 31-20.

title: Tom Brady and Tampa Bay Buccaneers Blow Out Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LV
description: Winning his seventh Super Bowl ring at age 43, Tom Brady led the Buccaneers to a 31-9 victory on February 7, 2021, becoming the first team to win on home turf.

title: Zomato Makes Blockbuster Stock Market Debut Becoming India First Tech Unicorn to List
description: Online food delivery platform Zomato listed on the BSE and NSE on July 23, 2021 at a sixty-six percent premium, opening the floodgates for Indian consumer-tech IPOs.

title: Rafael Nadal Rallies from Two Sets Down to Defeat Daniil Medvedev in Epic Australian Open Final
description: Nadal mounted a miraculous comeback over five hours and 24 minutes on January 30, 2022, clinching a record 21st men's major title.

title: Novak Djokovic Defeats Casper Ruud to Win Record 23rd Grand Slam Men Singles Title
description: Djokovic won in straight sets on June 11, 2023 at Roland Garros, breaking Rafael Nadal's men's record and becoming the first man to win each Grand Slam at least three times.

title: President Droupadi Murmu Grants Assent to Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam Women Reservation Act
description: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act reserving 33 percent of seats in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies for women received assent on September 28, 2023.

title: DRDO Conducts Successful Flight Test of Pralay Surface-to-Surface Quasi-Ballistic Missile
description: The solid-fueled battlefield missile demonstrated a 500-kilometer trajectory on November 7, 2023 from Abdul Kalam Island, clearing it for induction into the Indian Army.

title: Virat Kohli Scores Record 50th One Day International Century in World Cup Semifinal
description: Surpassing Sachin Tendulkar's tally of 49 ODI hundreds, Virat Kohli struck his historic 50th century on November 15, 2023 against New Zealand at Wankhede Stadium.

title: Jannik Sinner Rallies from Two Sets Down to Win Maiden Grand Slam at Australian Open
description: Italian star Jannik Sinner defeated Daniil Medvedev 3-6, 3-6, 6-4, 6-4, 6-3 on January 28, 2024 at Rod Laver Arena, capturing his first major crown.

title: Patrick Mahomes Leads Kansas City Chiefs Overtime Drive to Defeat 49ers in Super Bowl LVIII
description: Mahomes hit Mecole Hardman for the game-winning touchdown with three seconds left in overtime on February 11, 2024 in Las Vegas, securing back-to-back championships.

title: Carlos Alcaraz Outlasts Alexander Zverev in Five Sets to Win Maiden French Open Title
description: At age 21, Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz captured his third major on three different surfaces on June 9, 2024, rallying past Zverev over four hours and 19 minutes.

title: Angelos Charisteas Header Powers Underdogs Greece to Shock Euro 2004 Victory Over Hosts Portugal
description: Otto Rehhagel's defensively resilient Greece pulled off one of the greatest upsets in football history on July 4, 2004 in Lisbon, defeating Portugal 1-0 in the final.

title: Spain Demolishes Italy 4-0 in Kyiv Final to Win Euro 2012 and Complete Historic Treble
description: Silva, Alba, Torres, and Mata found the net on July 1, 2012 at the Olympic Stadium, recording the biggest margin of victory in European Championship final history.

title: Germany Smashes Host Nation Brazil 7-1 in Mineirazo Belo Horizonte World Cup Semifinal
description: Scoring five goals in the opening twenty-nine minutes on July 8, 2014 at the Mineirao, Germany handed Brazil their heaviest-ever competitive defeat, with Miroslav Klose scoring his 16th World Cup goal.

title: Argentina Defeats Netherlands on Penalties in Sao Paulo to Reach World Cup Final
description: Goalkeeper Sergio Romero saved two penalties from Ron Vlaar and Wesley Sneijder following a 0-0 draw on July 9, 2014, sending Argentina to the final.

title: Alexis Sanchez Panenka Penalty Delivers Maiden Copa America Title to Chile Over Argentina
description: Following a goalless final on July 4, 2015 at the Estadio Nacional in Santiago, Chile prevailed 4-1 on penalties, ending their 99-year search for continental glory.

title: Carli Lloyd Scores Sixteen-Minute Hat-Trick as United States Wins 2015 Women World Cup
description: Lloyd struck three times inside the first sixteen minutes from midfield on July 5, 2015 in Vancouver, leading the USA to a commanding 5-2 triumph over Japan.

title: Eder Extra-Time Long-Range Strike Crowned Portugal Euro 2016 Champions Over Hosts France
description: Despite losing injured Cristiano Ronaldo in the 25th minute, substitute Eder drove home from 25 yards on July 10, 2016 at the Stade de France, earning Portugal their first major trophy.

title: ISRO PSLV-C40 Launches Cartosat-2F Representing Hundredth Satellite Launched by ISRO
description: ISRO reached the milestone of orbiting its 100th satellite on January 12, 2018 as PSLV-C40 successfully launched Cartosat-2F and thirty co-passenger satellites.

title: Kylian Mbappe Scores Brace as France Edges Argentina 4-3 in Kazan World Cup Thriller
description: In one of the greatest World Cup knockout matches on June 30, 2018, Benjamin Pavard's spinning half-volley and Mbappe's twin strikes powered France into the quarterfinals.

title: Belgium Rallies from Two Down to Beat Japan 3-2 with 94th-Minute Chadli Winner
description: Executing a textbook 10-second counterattack from their own penalty box on July 2, 2018 in Rostov, Belgium completed the first World Cup knockout comeback from 0-2 down in 48 years.

title: Kevin De Bruyne Rocket Powers Belgium to Historic Quarterfinal Victory Over Brazil in Kazan
description: Belgium reached their first World Cup semifinal in 32 years on July 6, 2018, defeating five-time champions Brazil 2-1 with Thibaut Courtois making nine vital saves.

title: Samuel Umtiti Header Earns France 1-0 Victory Over Belgium in St Petersburg Semifinal
description: Umtiti outjumped Marouane Fellaini at the near post from a Griezmann corner on July 10, 2018, sending Didier Deschamps' Les Bleus into their third World Cup final.

title: Mario Mandzukic Extra-Time Winner Sends Croatia to Historic First World Cup Final Over England
description: Mandzukic pounced on Ivan Perisic's header in the 109th minute on July 11, 2018 at the Luzhniki Stadium in Moscow, securing a 2-1 comeback win over England.

title: Walmart Formally Completes Sixteen Billion Dollar Acquisition of Flipkart
description: American retail giant Walmart closed the acquisition of a 77 percent controlling stake in Indian e-commerce pioneer Flipkart on August 18, 2018, marking the largest e-commerce deal globally.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Launches PM-KISAN Direct Income Support Scheme at Gorakhpur
description: Providing vulnerable smallholder farming households 6,000 rupees per year in three equal tranches, the national income support scheme was officially launched on February 24, 2019.

title: United States Retains Women World Cup Defeating Netherlands in Lyon Final
description: Megan Rapinoe and Rose Lavelle scored second-half goals on July 7, 2019 at the Parc Olympique Lyonnais, securing a record fourth World Cup for the US women.

title: Angel Di Maria Chip Over Ederson Wins Copa America for Argentina Ending 28-Year Drought
description: Di Maria lofted a 22nd-minute strike at the Maracana on July 10, 2021 in Rio, earning Lionel Messi his first major senior international trophy with Argentina.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Inaugurates Samruddhi Mahamarg First Phase Between Nagpur and Shirdi
description: Spanning 520 kilometers, the initial phase of the Mumbai-Nagpur Super Communication Expressway was inaugurated on December 11, 2022 by PM Modi.

title: Virat Kohli Equals Sachin Tendulkar Record of 49 ODI Centuries on His 35th Birthday
description: Scoring an unbeaten 101 against South Africa at Eden Gardens Kolkata on November 5, 2023, Virat Kohli equalled the legendary mark of 49 ODI hundreds.

title: Lautaro Martinez 112th-Minute Extra-Time Goal Wins Copa America 2024 for Argentina in Miami
description: Coming off the bench after an injured Lionel Messi departed in tears, Martinez struck on July 14, 2024 at Hard Rock Stadium, securing a record 16th Copa America title for Argentina.

title: Seventeen-Year-Old Maria Sharapova Stuns Serena Williams to Win 2004 Wimbledon Title
description: Sharapova dominated the two-time defending champion 6-1, 6-4 on July 3, 2004 on Centre Court, becoming the third-youngest female champion in Wimbledon history.

title: Venus Williams Outlasts Lindsay Davenport in Longest Women Singles Final in Wimbledon History
description: Williams saved a championship point to prevail 4-6, 7-6, 9-7 on July 2, 2005, capturing her third Wimbledon title in a two-hour and 45-minute baseline battle.

title: Petra Kvitova Blasts Past Maria Sharapova to Win Maiden Wimbledon Title
description: Twenty-one-year-old Czech left-hander Kvitova fired a barrage of unreturned serves to win 6-3, 6-4 on July 2, 2011 on Centre Court, capturing her first major.

title: Serena Williams Defeats Garbine Muguruza to Complete Second Career Serena Slam at Wimbledon
description: Winning her fourth consecutive Grand Slam title on July 11, 2015 on Centre Court, Williams secured a 6-4, 6-4 triumph to hold all four major trophies simultaneously.

title: Sergi Roberto 95th-Minute Volley Completes Miraculous Barcelona 6-1 La Remontada Over PSG
description: Overturning a 0-4 first-leg deficit on March 8, 2017 at Camp Nou, Barcelona scored three goals after the 88th minute to execute the greatest comeback in Champions League history.

title: ISRO GSLV-F08 Launches GSAT-6A High-Power S-Band Communications Satellite
description: ISRO launched the GSAT-6A communication satellite on March 29, 2018 aboard GSLV-F08 from Sriharikota, featuring a large six-meter unfurlable S-band antenna.

title: Divock Origi Corner Taken Quickly Powers Liverpool to 4-0 Miracle Comeback Over Barcelona
description: Trailing 0-3 from the first leg, braces from Origi and Georginio Wijnaldum on May 7, 2019 at Anfield overturned the deficit, sending Liverpool to the Madrid final.

title: Lucas Moura 96th-Minute Hat-Trick Goal Sends Tottenham Past Ajax into Champions League Final
description: Tottenham rallied from 0-3 down on aggregate in Amsterdam on May 8, 2019, with Moura sweeping in a left-footed winner in the dying seconds to reach the final.

title: Reliance Industries Completes Rights Issue of Fifty-Three Thousand Crore Rupees
description: Mukesh Ambani's RIL successfully closed India's biggest ever rights issue on June 3, 2020, becoming completely net-debt-free well ahead of target.

title: Bayern Munich Utterly Decimates Barcelona 8-2 in Lisbon Champions League Quarterfinal
description: Hans-Dieter Flick's ruthless Bayern scored four goals in each half on August 14, 2020 at Estadio da Luz, inflicting Barcelona's heaviest European defeat in history.

title: Rodrygo Stunner in 90th and 91st Minutes Leads Real Madrid to Impossible Comeback Over Manchester City
description: Trailing 3-5 on aggregate with ninety seconds remaining on May 4, 2022 at the Bernabeu, Rodrygo scored twice in 89 seconds before Benzema's penalty won the tie in extra time.

title: DRDO Successfully Flight Tests Indigenous Astra Beyond Visual Range Air-to-Air Missile
description: Fired from a Sukhoi Su-30MKI fighter on May 31, 2022 off the Odisha coast, the Astra Mk-I demonstrated interception of high-speed aerial targets.

title: Saudi Arabia Pulls Off Monumental 2-1 World Cup Upset Over Lionel Messi Argentina
description: Saleh Al-Shehri and Salem Al-Dawsari scored stunning second-half goals on November 22, 2022 at Lusail Stadium, snapping Argentina's 36-match unbeaten streak.

title: Japan Stuns Four-Time Champions Germany 2-1 in World Cup Group Stage Shock in Doha
description: Substitutes Ritsu Doan and Takuma Asano struck late on November 23, 2022 at Khalifa International Stadium, securing Japan's greatest-ever World Cup victory.

title: Dominik Livakovic Penalty Heroics Lead Croatia Past Brazil into World Cup Semifinals
description: After Bruno Petkovic cancelled out Neymar's extra-time goal on December 9, 2022 at Education City, Croatia won the shootout 4-2 to eliminate tournament favorites Brazil.

title: Youssef En-Nesyri Soaring Header Propels Morocco Past Portugal into Historic World Cup Semifinal
description: En-Nesyri leaped 2.78 meters to head home on December 10, 2022 at Al Thumama Stadium, making Morocco the first African and Arab nation to reach the World Cup final four.

title: Julian Alvarez Brace and Lionel Messi Genius Power Argentina to 3-0 Semifinal Win Over Croatia
description: Messi converted a penalty and delivered an unforgettable assist to Alvarez on December 13, 2022 at Lusail Stadium, sending Argentina into the World Cup final.

title: Theo Hernandez and Randal Kolo Muani Strikes Send France Past Morocco into World Cup Final
description: Defending champions France halted Morocco's fairy tale run with a 2-0 victory on December 14, 2022 at Al Bayt Stadium, advancing to their second straight final.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Flags Off Uttarakhand First Vande Bharat Express Between Dehradun and Delhi
description: The semi-high speed train cutting travel time between Dehradun and Anand Vihar to four hours was virtually flagged off on May 25, 2023.

title: Royal Challengers Bangalore Win Maiden Women Premier League Title in New Delhi
description: Captain Smriti Mandhana led RCB to an eight-wicket victory over Delhi Capitals on March 17, 2024 at Arun Jaitley Stadium, securing their first franchise trophy.

title: Unranked Wildcard Kim Clijsters Stuns Tennis World to Win 2009 US Open Following Comeback
description: Playing in just her third tournament after an 18-month retirement, Clijsters defeated Caroline Wozniacki on September 13, 2009, becoming the first mother to win a major since 1980.

title: Francesca Schiavone Becomes First Italian Woman to Win Grand Slam Singles Title at Roland Garros
description: Ranked seventeenth seed, 29-year-old Schiavone defeated Samantha Stosur 6-4, 7-6 on June 5, 2010 in Paris, kissing the clay in emotional celebration.

title: Mamata Banerjee Sworn in as First Female Chief Minister of West Bengal
description: Ending thirty-four years of Left Front governance in Bengal, Trinamool Congress supremo Mamata Banerjee took oath at Raj Bhavan Kolkata on May 20, 2011.

title: Li Na Defeats Francesca Schiavone to Become First Asian Grand Slam Singles Champion in Paris
description: Watched by an estimated 116 million viewers in China on June 4, 2011, Li Na defeated the defending champion 6-4, 7-6 to make Asian sports history.

title: Serena Williams Defeats Angelique Kerber to Equal Steffi Graf Record of 22 Major Singles Titles
description: Firing 13 aces on July 9, 2016 at Wimbledon, Williams claimed a 7-5, 6-3 victory to match Graf's Open Era record and lift the Venus Rosewater Dish for the seventh time.

title: Naomi Osaka Wins 2018 US Open Defeating Serena Williams in Dramatic Final
description: Twenty-year-old Osaka showed extraordinary composure on September 8, 2018 at Arthur Ashe Stadium, winning 6-2, 6-4 to become the first Japanese player to win a Grand Slam singles title.

title: Simona Halep Produces Flawless Display with Three Unforced Errors to Defeat Serena Williams at Wimbledon
description: Halep captured her second major title on July 13, 2019 in just 56 minutes, dismantling Williams 6-2, 6-2 in one of the most clinical performances in Wimbledon final history.

title: Nineteen-Year-Old Bianca Andreescu Defeats Serena Williams to Win Maiden 2019 US Open
description: Andreescu became the first Canadian to win a Grand Slam singles title on September 7, 2019, holding off a fierce second-set comeback from Williams to prevail 6-3, 7-5.

title: Ashleigh Barty Defeats Karolina Pliskova in Three Sets to Win 2021 Wimbledon Title
description: World number one Barty became the first Australian women's champion since Evonne Goolagong Cawley in 1980, triumphing 6-3, 6-7, 6-3 on July 10, 2021.

title: Eighteen-Year-Old Qualifier Emma Raducanu Wins 2021 US Open Without Dropping a Set
description: In one of sports' greatest fairy tales on September 11, 2021, British qualifier Raducanu defeated Leylah Fernandez 6-4, 6-3, winning ten matches without losing a set.

title: DRDO and Indian Navy Successfully Test Naval Anti-Ship Missile NASM-SR from Sea King 42B Helicopter
description: The maiden flight trial of the indigenous short-range naval anti-ship weapon was executed on May 18, 2022 from ITR Chandipur off the Odisha coast.

title: Elena Rybakina Rallies from Set Down to Defeat Ons Jabeur and Win 2022 Wimbledon Title
description: Representing Kazakhstan, 23-year-old Rybakina won 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 on July 9, 2022 on Centre Court, becoming the youngest Wimbledon women's champion since 2011.

title: Iga Swiatek Defeats Ons Jabeur to Claim Third Grand Slam Title at 2022 US Open
description: World number one Swiatek triumphed 6-2, 7-6 on September 10, 2022 at Arthur Ashe Stadium, becoming the first Polish woman to win the US Open singles championship.

title: Mumbai Indians Win Inaugural Women Premier League Title at Brabourne Stadium
description: Led by Harmanpreet Kaur, Mumbai Indians defeated Delhi Capitals by seven wickets on March 26, 2023 to be crowned champions of the historic first WPL season.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Flags Off Northeast First Vande Bharat Express Between Guwahati and New Jalpaiguri
description: Connecting Assam to northern West Bengal across 411 kilometers, the maiden semi-high speed service for the northeastern region was flagged off on May 29, 2023.

title: Housing Development Finance Corporation HDFC Merges into HDFC Bank Creating Global Banking Giant
description: The mega-merger of India's largest mortgage lender into HDFC Bank took effect on July 1, 2023, creating the world's fourth largest bank by market capitalization.

title: Marketa Vondrousova Becomes First Unseeded Woman in Open Era to Win Wimbledon
description: Overcoming wrist injuries, the Czech left-hander defeated world number six Ons Jabeur 6-4, 6-4 on July 15, 2023 to capture her maiden Grand Slam championship.

title: Coco Gauff Rallies from Set Down to Defeat Aryna Sabalenka and Win Maiden 2023 US Open
description: Nineteen-year-old American Coco Gauff electrified the home crowd on September 9, 2023, prevailing 2-6, 6-3, 6-2 to become the youngest American US Open champion since Serena Williams in 1999.

title: Barbora Krejcikova Defeats Jasmine Paolini in Three Sets to Win 2024 Wimbledon Title
description: Krejcikova captured her second Grand Slam singles crown on July 13, 2024 on Centre Court, prevailing 6-2, 2-6, 6-4 in an emotional triumph dedicated to Jana Novotna.

title: Aryna Sabalenka Defeats Jessica Pegula in Straight Sets to Win Maiden 2024 US Open Title
description: Sabalenka captured her third Grand Slam singles crown on September 7, 2024 at Flushing Meadows, overcoming home favorite Pegula 7-5, 7-5 with blistering groundstrokes.

title: Serena Williams Routs Maria Sharapova to Win 2007 Australian Open Ranked 81 in World
description: Entering unseeded following a long injury absence, Williams demolished the world number one 6-1, 6-2 in 63 minutes on January 27, 2007 at Rod Laver Arena.

title: Maria Sharapova Defeats Ana Ivanovic to Win 2008 Australian Open Without Dropping a Set
description: Sharapova won her third Grand Slam title on January 26, 2008 in Melbourne, defeating Ivanovic 7-5, 6-3 without surrendering a single set in seven matches.

title: Maria Sharapova Defeats Sara Errani to Complete Career Grand Slam at Roland Garros
description: Winning 6-3, 6-2 on June 9, 2012 in Paris, Sharapova became only the tenth woman in tennis history to capture all four major championships.

title: Li Na Defeats Dominika Cibulkova to Win Maiden 2014 Australian Open Singles Title
description: After losing two previous Melbourne finals, Li Na triumphed 7-6, 6-0 on January 25, 2014, capturing her second major championship at age 31.

title: Maria Sharapova Outlasts Simona Halep in Three-Hour Epic to Win Second French Open
description: In the longest women's final at Roland Garros since 1996, Sharapova prevailed 6-4, 6-7, 6-4 on June 7, 2014, capturing her fifth and final career Grand Slam title.

title: Arvind Kejriwal Takes Oath as Chief Minister of Delhi Following AAP Decisive Victory
description: Aam Aadmi Party leader Arvind Kejriwal was sworn in as Delhi Chief Minister at Ramlila Maidan on February 14, 2015 after securing 67 out of 70 legislative assembly seats.

title: Angelique Kerber Stuns Defending Champion Serena Williams to Win 2016 Australian Open
description: In an exhilarating three-set final on January 30, 2016 in Melbourne, Kerber prevailed 6-4, 3-6, 6-4, becoming the first German Grand Slam winner since Steffi Graf in 1999.

title: Garbine Muguruza Defeats Defending Champion Serena Williams to Win 2016 French Open
description: Twenty-two-year-old Spaniard Muguruza captured her maiden major on June 4, 2016 at Court Philippe Chatrier, defeating Williams 7-5, 6-4 with commanding baseline power.

title: Unseeded 20-Year-Old Jelena Ostapenko Rallies Past Simona Halep to Win Shock 2017 French Open
description: Trailing by a set and 0-3 on June 10, 2017, Ostapenko blasted 54 winners to triumph 4-6, 6-4, 6-3, becoming the first unseeded woman to win Roland Garros since 1933.

title: Caroline Wozniacki Outlasts Simona Halep in Three Grueling Sets to Win 2018 Australian Open
description: Wozniacki won her maiden major and reclaimed world number one on January 27, 2018 in Melbourne, prevailing 7-6, 3-6, 6-4 in extreme heat over two hours and 49 minutes.

title: ISRO PSLV-C41 Launches IRNSS-1I Navigation Satellite into Geosynchronous Orbit
description: ISRO's PSLV-C41 successfully launched the IRNSS-1I replacement navigation satellite on April 12, 2018 from Sriharikota to strengthen the NavIC constellation.

title: Simona Halep Rallies Past Sloane Stephens to Win Maiden Grand Slam Title at 2018 French Open
description: After losing three previous major finals, Halep fought back from a set and a break down to prevail 3-6, 6-4, 6-1 on June 9, 2018 in Paris.

title: DRDO Successfully Test Fires Canisterized K-4 Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile from Pontoons
description: India validated its underwater nuclear deterrence leg on January 19, 2020 by successfully testing the 3,500-km range K-4 SLBM off the Visakhapatnam coast.

title: Nineteen-Year-Old Iga Swiatek Wins 2020 French Open Without Dropping a Set
description: Ranked 54 in the world, Swiatek conceded only 28 games throughout the autumn tournament on October 10, 2020, defeating Sofia Kenin 6-4, 6-1 in the final.

title: Ashleigh Barty Ends 44-Year Home Drought Winning 2022 Australian Open Women Title
description: Recovering from 1-5 down in the second set on January 29, 2022, Barty defeated Danielle Collins 6-3, 7-6, becoming the first homegrown Australian Open champion since Chris O'Neil in 1978.

title: Iga Swiatek Extends 35-Match Winning Streak Defeating Coco Gauff to Win 2022 French Open
description: Swiatek equalled Venus Williams' 21st-century record of 35 consecutive wins on June 4, 2022, sweeping past Gauff 6-1, 6-3 to capture her second Roland Garros crown.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Flags Off Nine Vande Bharat Express Trains Simultaneously
description: In the largest single-day rollout of semi-high speed services, PM Modi flagged off nine Vande Bharat trains across eleven states on September 24, 2023.

title: Aryna Sabalenka Defends Australian Open Title Sweeping Zheng Qinwen in Straight Sets
description: Sabalenka became the first woman in eleven years to retain the Melbourne title on January 27, 2024, defeating Zheng 6-3, 6-2 in 76 minutes without dropping a set all tournament.

title: Kolkata Knight Riders Clinch Third IPL Title Defeating Sunrisers Hyderabad in Chennai
description: Mentored by Gautam Gambhir and captained by Shreyas Iyer, KKR dominated the IPL final on May 26, 2024 at MA Chidambaram Stadium to claim their third trophy.

title: Iga Swiatek Sweeps Jasmine Paolini in 68 Minutes to Win Fourth French Open Title
description: Swiatek won ten games in a row to defeat Paolini 6-2, 6-1 on June 8, 2024, becoming only the third woman in the Open Era to win three consecutive Roland Garros titles.

title: Helmut Rahn 84th-Minute Winner Seals Miracle of Bern for West Germany Over Hungary
description: Trailing 0-2 inside eight minutes against the invincible Hungarian Mighty Magyars on July 4, 1954 in Bern, West Germany rallied to win 3-2, lifting their first World Cup.

title: Amarildo and Zito Strike as Brazil Defeats Czechoslovakia to Retain World Cup in Santiago
description: Overcoming the tournament-ending injury to Pele, Garrincha led Brazil to a 3-1 comeback victory on June 17, 1962 at Estadio Nacional.

title: Geoff Hurst Scores Historic Hat-Trick as England Defeats West Germany at Wembley
description: Hurst's controversial crossbar goal in extra time and emphatic 120th-minute finish on July 30, 1966 sealed a 4-2 triumph, giving England their only World Cup title.

title: Gianni Rivera 111th-Minute Strike Wins Game of the Century for Italy Over West Germany
description: In an exhilarating 4-3 semifinal featuring five extra-time goals at the Azteca Stadium on June 17, 1970, Italy triumphed despite Franz Beckenbauer playing with a dislocated shoulder.

title: Carlos Alberto Blasts Iconic Fourth Goal as Brazil Crushes Italy in 1970 World Cup Final
description: Pele laid off an unselfish pass for captain Carlos Alberto to rifle into the bottom corner on June 21, 1970 in Mexico City, crowning Brazil's legendary side 4-1 champions.

title: Gerd Muller Swivel Strike Delivers 1974 World Cup Victory to West Germany in Munich
description: After Johan Neeskens scored a first-minute penalty for the Dutch, Paul Breitner and Muller struck on July 7, 1974 at Olympiastadion, giving West Germany a 2-1 victory.

title: Mario Kempes Scores Twice in Extra Time as Argentina Defeats Netherlands to Win 1978 World Cup
description: Before ticker-tape-covered stands at the Estadio Monumental on June 25, 1978, Kempes and Daniel Bertoni earned Argentina a 3-1 victory and their first World Cup.

title: Paolo Rossi Hat-Trick Eliminates Socrates and Zico Brazil in Sarria Classic
description: Italian striker Rossi capitalized on defensive lapses to score in the 5th, 25th, and 74th minutes on July 5, 1982 in Barcelona, guiding Italy to a legendary 3-2 victory.

title: West Germany Edges France on Penalties in Epic Seville Semifinal After 3-3 Thriller
description: Surviving a 1-3 extra-time deficit on July 8, 1982 at the Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan, West Germany won 5-4 on penalties in the first-ever World Cup penalty shootout.

title: Sergio Goycochea Penalty Saves Eliminate Hosts Italy as Argentina Reaches 1990 Final
description: Goycochea denied Roberto Donadoni and Aldo Serena in the shootout on July 3, 1990 in Naples, sending Maradona's Argentina to the final following a 1-1 draw.

title: Stuart Pearce and Chris Waddle Miss Penalties as West Germany Beats England in Turin
description: Following Gary Lineker's 80th-minute equalizer on July 4, 1990 at the Stadio delle Alpi, West Germany won the shootout 4-3 to reach their third successive final.

title: Branco Thunderous 30-Yard Free Kick Wins Five-Goal World Cup Classic for Brazil in Dallas
description: Brazil and the Netherlands traded four second-half goals before left-back Branco drove a ferocious set-piece into the bottom corner on July 9, 1994 at the Cotton Bowl.

title: Michael Owen Wonder Goal and David Beckham Red Card Highlight St Etienne Classic
description: Eighteen-year-old Owen danced past two Argentine defenders on June 30, 1998, but Beckham was sent off and Argentina advanced on penalties following a 2-2 thriller.

title: Lilian Thuram Scores Only Two International Career Goals as France Reaches 1998 Final
description: After Davor Suker opened the scoring for Croatia on July 8, 1998 at the Stade de France, right-back Thuram struck twice with left and right foot to win 2-1.

title: Ronaldinho Forty-Yard Free Kick Lob Over David Seaman Sends Ten-Man Brazil Past England
description: Ronaldinho scored an audacious free kick in the 50th minute before being controversially sent off on June 21, 2002 in Shizuoka, securing a 2-1 quarterfinal win for Brazil.

title: Yogi Adityanath Sworn in as Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh at Kanshiram Smriti Upvan
