description: BJP leader Yogi Adityanath took the oath of office in Lucknow on March 19, 2017 following a landslide assembly election victory for the National Democratic Alliance.

title: ISRO PSLV-C42 Launches NovaSAR and S1-4 Commercial British Earth Observation Satellites
description: In a dedicated commercial mission on September 16, 2018, ISRO's PSLV-C42 launched two British satellites weighing 889 kg into sun-synchronous orbit.

title: Apple Formally Opens Its First Official Retail Flagship Store in India at BKC Mumbai
description: Apple CEO Tim Cook opened the doors of Apple BKC inside Jio World Drive on April 18, 2023, marking Apple's direct retail expansion into the Indian market.

title: DRDO Conducts Successful Flight Test of New Generation Surface to Air Missile Akash-NG
description: Tested from the Integrated Test Range Chandipur on January 12, 2024, Akash-NG demonstrated high-maneuverability interception of an aerial target at low altitude.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Flags Off Ten New Vande Bharat Express Trains from Ahmedabad
description: PM Modi dedicated ten additional Vande Bharat services and laid foundation stones for 85,000 crore rupees railway projects on March 12, 2024.

title: Dick Fosbury Wins Olympic High Jump Gold Popularizing Revolutionary Backward Flop Technique
description: Clearing 2.24 meters on October 20, 1968 in Mexico City, Fosbury revolutionized high jumping by launching himself over the bar head-first with his back to the bar.

title: Kevin Young Shatters 400m Hurdles World Record Running 46.78 Seconds in Barcelona
description: Young became the first human to break 47 seconds in the 400-meter intermediate hurdles on August 6, 1992, winning Olympic gold with a record that stood 29 years.

title: Fabio Grosso and Alessandro Del Piero Extra-Time Goals Stun Hosts Germany in Dortmund
description: Grosso curled in a first-time strike in the 119th minute and Del Piero finished a counterattack in the 121st on July 4, 2006, sending Italy into the World Cup final.

title: Jason Lezak Swims Miraculous 46.06 Anchor Leg in 4x100m Freestyle Relay in Beijing
description: Overtaking France's Alain Bernard in the final five meters on August 11, 2008, 32-year-old Lezak preserved Michael Phelps' quest for eight gold medals in the fastest relay in history.

title: Zambia Wins Emotional Africa Cup of Nations Final in Libreville Dedicated to 1993 Crash Victims
description: Stoppila Sunzu converted the winning penalty on February 12, 2012 as Zambia defeated Ivory Coast 8-7 in the shootout, miles from where their national team perished in 1993.

title: Australia Defeats South Korea in Extra Time to Win Maiden AFC Asian Cup Title in Sydney
description: James Troisi scored in the 105th minute on January 31, 2015 at Stadium Australia, making the Socceroos the first men's team to win championships in two confederations.

title: Katie Ledecky Destroys 800m Freestyle World Record by Two Seconds Winning Rio Gold
description: Clocking 8:04.79 on August 12, 2016 in Rio, Ledecky touched the wall over eleven seconds ahead of the silver medalist to complete the 200m, 400m, and 800m Olympic sweep.

title: Wayde van Niekerk Shatters Michael Johnson 400m World Record from Lane 8 in Rio
description: Running blind on the outside lane on August 14, 2016, South African sprinter Van Niekerk clocked 43.03 seconds, breaking Johnson's 17-year-old world record to win gold.

title: ISRO GSLV-MkIII-D2 Launches GSAT-29 High-Throughput Communications Satellite
description: ISRO's second developmental flight of the heavy-lift LVM3 rocket on November 14, 2018 successfully placed the 3,423 kg GSAT-29 multi-beam satellite into orbit.

title: River Plate Defeats Arch-Rivals Boca Juniors in Historic Madrid Copa Libertadores Final
description: Moved to the Santiago Bernabeu following fan violence in Buenos Aires, Juan Fernando Quintero's extra-time thunderbolt sealed a 3-1 win on December 9, 2018 in the 'Superfinal'.

title: Qatar Stuns Four-Time Champions Japan 3-1 in Abu Dhabi to Win First AFC Asian Cup
description: Almoez Ali's spectacular overhead bicycle kick and goals from Hatem and Afif on February 1, 2019 earned Qatar their maiden continental title with seven straight wins.

title: Gabriel Barbosa Two Late Goals Earn Flamengo Dramatic Copa Libertadores Win Over River Plate
description: Trailing 0-1 in the 89th minute on November 23, 2019 in Lima, 'Gabigol' struck in the 89th and 92nd minutes to complete an astonishing 2-1 comeback for Flamengo.

title: MK Stalin Takes Oath as Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Ending Ten Years of AIADMK Rule
description: DMK president MK Stalin was sworn in as the eighth Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu at Raj Bhavan Chennai on May 7, 2021.

title: Karsten Warholm Destroys 400m Hurdles World Record Running 45.94 Seconds in Tokyo
description: Warholm ripped his singlet in celebration on August 3, 2021 at the Tokyo Olympic Stadium, slashing three-quarters of a second off his own mark in one of the greatest races ever.

title: Sadio Mane Penalty Wins Maiden Africa Cup of Nations for Senegal Over Egypt in Yaounde
description: Mane struck the decisive spot kick in the shootout on February 6, 2022 in Cameroon, earning Senegal their first continental title following a 0-0 extra-time deadlock.

title: DRDO Flight Tests Quick Reaction Surface to Air Missile QRSAM Against High Speed Target
description: The indigenous all-weather truck-mounted air defence system achieved direct hits on simulated incoming aerial threats on September 8, 2022 off Chandipur.

title: Apple Opens Its Second Official Retail Store in India at Select Citywalk New Delhi
description: Tim Cook inaugurated the Apple Saket retail store in South Delhi on April 20, 2023, completing Apple's dual-flagship opening across India's financial and political capitals.

title: Chennai Super Kings Win Record-Equalling Fifth IPL Title in Last-Ball Thriller in Ahmedabad
description: Ravindra Jadeja struck ten runs off the final two deliveries past midnight on May 29, 2023 at Narendra Modi Stadium, powering MS Dhoni's CSK past Gujarat Titans.

title: Akram Afif Penalty Hat-Trick Retains AFC Asian Cup for Hosts Qatar Over Jordan in Lusail
description: Afif converted three clinical penalties on February 10, 2024 before 86,000 fans at Lusail Stadium, sealing a 3-1 victory as Qatar defended their Asian title.

title: Ivory Coast Completes Miracle Tournament Comeback to Win 2023 Africa Cup of Nations on Home Soil
description: After nearly being eliminated in the group stage, the Elephants defeated Nigeria 2-1 on February 11, 2024 in Abidjan with Sebastien Haller scoring the 81st-minute winner.

title: Underdogs Greece Shock Hosts Portugal 2-1 in Opening Match of Euro 2004 in Porto
description: Giorgos Karagounis and Angelos Basinas scored on June 12, 2004 at Estadio do Dragao, stunning European football in the opening game.

title: Philipp Lahm 90th-Minute Winner Sends Germany Past Turkey into Euro 2008 Final in Basel
description: After a frantic five-goal thriller on June 25, 2008 at St Jakob-Park, Lahm combined with Hitzlsperger to slot past Rustu Recber in the final minute.

title: Mario Balotelli First-Half Brace Powers Italy Past Germany into Euro 2012 Final in Warsaw
description: Balotelli headed in Cassano's cross and smashed a 15-yard drive past Manuel Neuer on June 28, 2012, celebrating with his famous flex pose in a 2-1 victory.

title: Iceland Stuns England 2-1 in Nice Producing Greatest Upset in Modern European Championship
description: Ragnar Sigurdsson and Kolbeinn Sigthorsson scored first-half goals on June 27, 2016 as tournament debutants Iceland eliminated England in the round of 16.

title: Antoine Griezmann Brace Propels France Past World Champions Germany into Euro 2016 Final
description: Griezmann converted a penalty and poked in a loose ball on July 7, 2016 at the Stade Velodrome in Marseille, sealing a memorable 2-0 semifinal triumph.

title: ISRO PSLV-C43 Launches HySIS Hyperspectral Imaging Satellite Along with 30 Co-Passenger Satellites
description: ISRO launched HySIS on November 29, 2018 aboard PSLV-C43 from Sriharikota, providing continuous hyperspectral monitoring of agriculture, forestry, and coastal waters.

title: Himanta Biswa Sarma Takes Oath as Chief Minister of Assam at Srimanta Sankaradeva Kalakshetra
description: BJP leader Himanta Biswa Sarma was sworn in as the 15th Chief Minister of Assam on May 10, 2021 in Guwahati, succeeding Sarbananda Sonowal.

title: Spain Overcomes Croatia 5-3 in Extra-Time Thriller in Copenhagen at Euro 2020
description: In the second highest-scoring match in Euro history on June 28, 2021, Alvaro Morata and Mikel Oyarzabal struck extra-time goals following an 8-goal epic.

title: Yuto Horigome Wins Inaugural Men Street Skateboarding Olympic Gold Medal in Tokyo
description: Competing in his hometown at Ariake Urban Sports Park on July 25, 2021, 22-year-old Horigome nailed high-difficulty grinds to become skateboarding's first Olympic champion.

title: DRDO Successfully Conducts Maiden Flight Test of Long-Range Glide Bomb from Fighter Jet
description: The precision-guided glide munition was successfully tested from an Indian Air Force aircraft on October 29, 2021 off the coast of Odisha.

title: Gujarat Titans Win Indian Premier League Trophy on Tournament Debut at Ahmedabad
description: Captained by Hardik Pandya, debutants Gujarat Titans defeated Rajasthan Royals by seven wickets on May 29, 2022 before 100,000 fans at Narendra Modi Stadium.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Flags Off Rajasthan First Vande Bharat Express Between Ajmer and Delhi
description: Connecting Ajmer, Jaipur, and Delhi Cantt, Rajasthan's first semi-high speed train with high-rise pantographs began commercial service on April 12, 2023.

title: Sixteen-Year-Old Lamine Yamal Curler Powers Spain Past France into Euro 2024 Final in Munich
description: Yamal became the youngest goalscorer in European Championship history with a 25-yard curling strike off the post on July 9, 2024, inspiring a 2-1 comeback win.

title: Ollie Watkins 90th-Minute Precision Strike Sends England Past Netherlands into Euro 2024 Final
description: Coming off the bench, Watkins received Cole Palmer's pass to drill home from a tight angle on July 10, 2024 in Dortmund, clinching a 2-1 victory.

title: Antoine Dupont Powers France to Rugby Sevens Olympic Gold Over Defending Champions Fiji
description: World rugby superstar Dupont scored two tries and set up another on July 27, 2024 at the Stade de France, securing France's first gold medal of the Paris Games 28-7.

title: Daniel Wiffen Sets Olympic Record to Win Men 800m Freestyle Gold for Ireland in Paris
description: Clocking 7:38.19 on July 30, 2024 at Paris La Defense Arena, Wiffen won Ireland's first Olympic swimming gold medal in twenty-eight years.

title: Femke Bol Produces Miraculous 47.93 Anchor Leg to Win Mixed 4x400m Relay Gold for Netherlands
description: Passing three runners in the final 200 meters on August 3, 2024 at the Stade de France, Bol stormed from fourth to first to snatch gold by three-tenths of a second.

title: Zheng Qinwen Wins Historic Women Singles Tennis Gold for China at Roland Garros
description: Defeating Donna Vekic 6-2, 6-3 on August 3, 2024 in Paris, 21-year-old Zheng became the first Asian player ever to win an Olympic singles tennis gold medal.

title: Quincy Hall Stages Ferocious Home Straight Comeback to Win Olympic 400m Gold in 43.40
description: Coming from fourth place at the final bend on August 7, 2024 in Paris, Hall dipped on the line to edge Matthew Hudson-Smith by four-hundredths of a second.

title: Rai Benjamin Runs 46.46 Seconds to Win Men 400m Hurdles Olympic Gold in Paris
description: Benjamin surged clear of Karsten Warholm and Alison dos Santos on August 9, 2024 at the Stade de France, capturing his maiden individual Olympic title.

title: Usain Bolt Smashes 200m World Record Running 19.19 Seconds in Berlin
description: Four days after his 100m triumph, Bolt shattered his 200m world record on August 20, 2009 in Berlin, winning by a staggering margin of six-tenths of a second.

title: Cadel Evans Becomes First Australian Cyclist to Win Tour de France in Paris
description: Sealing victory in the final time trial in Grenoble, Evans rode onto the Champs-Elysees in the yellow jersey on July 24, 2011 to make Australian sporting history.

title: Bradley Wiggins Becomes First British Rider to Win Tour de France
description: Helping teammate Mark Cavendish win the final Champs-Elysees sprint on July 22, 2012, Wiggins secured Britain's maiden Tour de France general classification victory.

title: Chris Froome Wins 100th Edition of Tour de France for Team Sky
description: Froome carried the yellow jersey through an illuminated twilight parade down the Champs-Elysees on July 21, 2013, winning his first of four Tour titles.

title: Vincenzo Nibali Wins Tour de France Completing Career Triple Crown of Cycling Grand Tours
description: Dominating with four stage victories across mountains and cobblestones, Nibali celebrated on the Champs-Elysees on July 27, 2014 as the sixth rider to win all three Grand Tours.

title: Justin Gatlin Defeats Usain Bolt in Bolt Farewell Individual 100m Final in London
description: Gatlin edged Christian Coleman and Usain Bolt in 9.92 seconds on August 5, 2017 at London Stadium, bowing before Bolt in a gesture of sportsmanship.

title: Geraint Thomas Wins 2018 Tour de France Becoming First Welshman to Claim Yellow Jersey
description: Thomas won back-to-back mountain stages at La Rosiere and Alpe d'Huez to claim the general classification victory on July 29, 2018 in Paris.

title: ISRO GSLV-F11 Launches GSAT-7A Military Communications Satellite for Indian Air Force
description: ISRO launched the 2,250 kg GSAT-7A communications satellite on December 19, 2018 aboard GSLV-F11 to interlink Indian Air Force radar stations, airbases, and airborne control aircraft.

title: ISRO PSLV-C44 Launches Microsat-R Military Satellite and Kalamsat Student Satellite
description: ISRO's PSLV-C44 launched the Microsat-R imaging payload and Kalamsat-V2 student satellite on January 24, 2019, utilizing the fourth stage as an orbital experiment platform.

title: Twenty-Two-Year-Old Egan Bernal Becomes First Latin American to Win Tour de France
description: Riding for Team Ineos, Colombian climber Bernal became the third-youngest Tour winner in history upon crossing the Champs-Elysees on July 28, 2019.

title: Tadej Pogacar Overturns Deficit in Dramatic Time Trial on La Planche des Belles Filles to Win Tour
description: In an unforgettable penultimate stage comeback, 21-year-old Slovenian Pogacar overhauled Primoz Roglic to claim victory on September 20, 2020 in Paris.

title: Thirteen-Year-Old Momiji Nishiya Wins Women Street Skateboarding Gold at Tokyo Olympics
description: Nishiya scored 15.26 points on July 26, 2021, becoming Japan's youngest-ever Olympic gold medalist and one of the youngest in Olympic history.

title: Sunisa Lee Wins Women Gymnastics Individual All-Around Gold Medal at Tokyo Olympics
description: Eighteen-year-old Hmong-American Lee posted a total score of 57.433 on July 29, 2021 at Ariake Gymnastics Centre, extending the US winning streak in the event to five Games.

title: Elaine Thompson-Herah Runs 10.61 Seconds Breaking Florence Griffith Joyner Olympic 100m Record
description: Leading a historic Jamaican podium sweep with Fraser-Pryce and Jackson on July 31, 2021 in Tokyo, Thompson-Herah defended her 100m title with the second-fastest time ever.

title: Sydney McLaughlin Smashes 400m Hurdles World Record in 51.46 Seconds at Tokyo Games
description: In an electrifying duel with Dalilah Muhammad on August 4, 2021 in Tokyo, McLaughlin sliced nearly half a second off her own world record to claim gold.

title: Bhagwant Mann Sworn in as Chief Minister of Punjab at Khatkar Kalan Ancestral Village of Bhagat Singh
description: AAP leader Bhagwant Mann took the oath of office before a massive gathering on March 16, 2022 following a 92-seat sweep in the Punjab assembly elections.

title: Eknath Shinde Takes Oath as Chief Minister of Maharashtra Alongside Devendra Fadnavis as Deputy
description: Rebel Shiv Sena leader Eknath Shinde was sworn in as Maharashtra Chief Minister on June 30, 2022 following the collapse of the Maha Vikas Aghadi coalition.

title: Jonas Vingegaard Wins Maiden Tour de France for Denmark After Alpine Duel with Pogacar
description: Breaking away on the Col du Granon, Jumbo-Visma leader Vingegaard sealed his maiden Grand Tour triumph on the Champs-Elysees on July 24, 2022.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Flags Off Five Vande Bharat Trains Simultaneously from Bhopal
description: Flagged off from Rani Kamalapati railway station on June 27, 2023, the new services expanded high-speed connectivity across Madhya Pradesh, Goa, Bihar, and Jharkhand.

title: Tadej Pogacar Completes Giro d'Italia and Tour de France Double with Third Tour Triumph in Nice
description: With the 2024 final stage shifted to Nice due to the Paris Olympics, Pogacar won six stages to become the first rider since Marco Pantani in 1998 to win the Giro-Tour double on July 21, 2024.

title: Viv Richards Unbeaten 138 Powers West Indies to Retain Cricket World Cup Against England
description: Richards and Collis King shared a devastating 139-run stand on June 23, 1979 at Lord's before Joel Garner took five wickets to secure a 92-run win.

title: Allan Border Leads Australia to Maiden Cricket World Cup Title Defeating England at Eden Gardens
description: Australia edged arch-rivals England by seven runs on November 8, 1987 before 95,000 fans in Calcutta following Mike Gatting's ill-fated reverse sweep.

title: Imran Khan Cornered Tigers Pakistan Defeats England at Melbourne Cricket Ground to Win World Cup
description: Wearing his famous tiger t-shirt, Imran Khan scored 72 and claimed the final wicket on March 25, 1992 in Melbourne, with Wasim Akram taking two crucial wickets.

title: Aravinda de Silva All-Round Masterclass Powers Sri Lanka to Maiden Cricket World Cup in Lahore
description: De Silva took three wickets and struck an unbeaten 107 on March 17, 1996 at Gaddafi Stadium as Arjuna Ranatunga's side chased down 241 against Australia.

title: Shane Warne Four-Wicket Spell Guides Australia to Dominant World Cup Final Triumph Over Pakistan
description: Warne took 4 for 33 to dismiss Pakistan for 132 on June 20, 1999 at Lord's, allowing Steve Waugh's Australia to chase the target down in just twenty overs.

title: Ricky Ponting Unbeaten 140 Powers Australia to Record 359 and World Cup Triumph Over India
description: Hitting eight sixes in Johannesburg on March 23, 2003, captain Ponting led Australia to an emphatic 125-run victory and an undefeated tournament defense.

title: Tiger Woods Chips in on 16th Hole on Way to Fourth Masters Victory in Playoff
description: Woods produced an unforgettable chip that paused on the lip of the cup before dropping on April 10, 2005, then birdied the first playoff hole against Chris DiMarco.

title: Adam Gilchrist Blistering 149 with Squash Ball in Glove Wins World Cup for Australia in Barbados
description: Gilchrist smashed 149 off 104 balls in a rain-reduced final on April 28, 2007 at Kensington Oval, earning Australia an unprecedented third consecutive World Cup.

title: Tiger Woods Wins 2008 US Open at Torrey Pines on Severely Fractured Leg in 19-Hole Playoff
description: Playing with a double stress fracture and torn ACL on June 16, 2008, Woods forced an 18-hole Monday playoff with a 72nd-hole birdie before defeating Rocco Mediate on the 19th hole.

title: Michael Clarke Half-Century Guides Australia to Fifth Cricket World Cup Title at Melbourne
description: Before 93,000 spectators on March 29, 2015 at the MCG, Australia bowled out New Zealand for 183 and chased the total down with seven wickets in hand.

title: Tiger Woods Completes Fairytale Comeback to Win Fifth Masters After Eleven-Year Major Drought
description: Surviving multiple back surgeries, 43-year-old Woods won his 15th major on April 14, 2019 at Augusta National, embraced by his children in an emotional celebration.

title: England Wins Cricket World Cup on Boundary Countback After Unbelievable Super Over Tie at Lords
description: In the most dramatic cricket final in history on July 14, 2019, England and New Zealand tied both the 50-over match and Super Over, with England crowned champions.

title: ISRO PSLV-C47 Launches Cartosat-3 High-Resolution Earth Observation Satellite
description: ISRO's PSLV-XL C47 launched the 1,625 kg Cartosat-3 third-generation imaging satellite with 25-centimeter ground resolution on November 27, 2019 from Sriharikota.

title: ISRO PSLV-C48 Launches RISAT-2BR1 Radar Imaging Reconnaissance Satellite
description: ISRO's PSLV-C48 launched the 628 kg RISAT-2BR1 X-band synthetic aperture radar satellite on December 11, 2019 along with nine international commercial payloads.

title: ISRO Launches GSAT-30 High-Power Communications Satellite Aboard Ariane 5 from Kourou
description: An Ariane 5 rocket launched ISRO's 3,357 kg GSAT-30 communications satellite from French Guiana on January 17, 2020 to replace aging INSAT-4A broadcasting capacity.

title: Fifty-Year-Old Phil Mickelson Wins PGA Championship Becoming Oldest Major Champion in History
description: Mickelson held off Brooks Koepka and Louis Oosthuizen on May 23, 2021 at the Ocean Course at Kiawah Island, breaking Julius Boros' 53-year-old record.

title: Siddaramaiah Sworn in as Chief Minister of Karnataka Following Congress Assembly Triumph
description: Veteran leader Siddaramaiah took the oath of office at Kanteerava Stadium in Bengaluru on May 20, 2023 alongside DK Shivakumar as Deputy Chief Minister.

title: Sha'Carri Richardson Outkips Shericka Jackson from Lane Nine to Win World 100m Gold in Budapest
description: American sprinter Richardson blazed from the outside lane in a championship record 10.65 seconds on August 21, 2023, capturing her maiden world title.

title: Noah Lyles Completes 100m and 200m World Sprint Double in Budapest
description: Clocking 19.52 seconds on August 25, 2023, Lyles captured his third consecutive world 200m gold and completed the sprint double at the National Athletics Centre.

title: Revanth Reddy Sworn in as Chief Minister of Telangana at LB Stadium Hyderabad
description: Congress leader A Revanth Reddy assumed office on December 7, 2023, becoming the second Chief Minister of Telangana following victory over the BRS.

title: French Settlements of Pondicherry and Karaikal Formally Transferred de Facto to India
description: The French tricolour was lowered and Indian national flag hoisted on November 1, 1954 as France ceded administrative control of Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam.

title: Parliament Enacts Consumer Protection Act 1986 Establishing Three-Tier Consumer Courts
description: The landmark consumer rights legislation received presidential assent on December 24, 1986, establishing district forums, state commissions, and the National Commission.

title: Mineiro Goal and Rogerio Ceni Saves Earn Sao Paulo Club World Championship Over Liverpool
description: Goalkeeper Ceni made a string of miraculous saves in Yokohama on December 18, 2005 as Brazilian champions Sao Paulo defeated European champions Liverpool 1-0.

title: Adriano Gabiru 82nd-Minute Breakaway Goal Wins Club World Cup for Internacional Over Barcelona
description: Substituted in the 76th minute, Gabiru scored on the counterattack on December 17, 2006 in Yokohama to shock Ronaldinho and Frank Rijkaard's Barcelona 1-0.

title: Kaka Produces Two Assists and Goal as AC Milan Wins 2007 Club World Cup Over Boca Juniors
description: Ballon d'Or winner Kaka orchestrated a 4-2 triumph on December 16, 2007 in Yokohama, avenging Milan's 2003 Intercontinental Cup loss to Boca.

title: Wayne Rooney Curler Delivers Club World Cup to Ten-Man Manchester United Over LDU Quito
description: Despite Nemanja Vidic being sent off, Rooney curled home in the 73rd minute on December 21, 2008 in Yokohama, making United the first British team to win the trophy.

title: Shahid Afridi Unbeaten Fifty Guides Pakistan to Maiden ICC World Twenty20 Title at Lords
description: Afridi struck 54 not out and claimed a wicket on June 21, 2009 in London, defeating Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the final.

title: Lionel Messi 110th-Minute Chest Goal Clinches Sextuple for Barcelona in Abu Dhabi
description: Directing Dani Alves' cross into the net with his badge on December 19, 2009 against Estudiantes, Messi delivered Barcelona an unprecedented six trophies in a single calendar year.

title: Paul Collingwood Leads England to First Global ICC Championship Defeating Australia in T20 Final
description: Craig Kieswetter scored 63 as England chased down 148 on May 16, 2010 in Barbados to beat arch-rivals Australia by seven wickets.

title: Barcelona Produces Passing Masterclass to Rout Neymar Santos 4-0 in Club World Cup Final
description: Lionel Messi scored twice as Pep Guardiola's side enjoyed 74 percent possession in Yokohama on December 18, 2011, described by Neymar as 'a lesson in football'.

title: Marlon Samuels Blistering 78 Powers West Indies Past Sri Lanka to Win 2012 World Twenty20
description: Defending a modest 137 on October 7, 2012 in Colombo, the West Indies bowled out hosts Sri Lanka for 101 to lift their first world title since 1979.

title: Paolo Guerrero Header and Cassio Heroics Deliver Club World Cup to Corinthians Over Chelsea
description: Peruvian striker Guerrero scored the only goal on December 16, 2012 in Yokohama before 30,000 traveling Brazilian fans, breaking European dominance in the tournament.

title: Kumar Sangakkara Farewell Half-Century Guides Sri Lanka to 2014 World Twenty20 Title
description: Restricting India to 130 in Dhaka on April 6, 2014, Sri Lanka chased the target down with Sangakkara hitting 52 not out in his final T20 international.

title: Carlos Brathwaite Smashes Four Consecutive Sixes in Final Over to Win T20 World Cup for West Indies
description: Needing 19 runs off the last six balls against Ben Stokes on April 3, 2016 at Eden Gardens, Brathwaite launched four towering sixes to pull off an impossible victory.

title: Roberto Firmino 99th-Minute Extra-Time Strike Wins Maiden Club World Cup for Liverpool in Doha
description: Finishing Sadio Mane's breakaway pass on December 21, 2019 against Flamengo, Firmino crowned European champions Liverpool world champions for the first time.

title: ISRO PSLV-C49 Launches EOS-01 Earth Observation Satellite Alongside Nine International Satellites
description: ISRO conducted its first launch during the pandemic on November 7, 2020 as PSLV-C49 placed EOS-01 synthetic aperture radar satellite and nine customer satellites into orbit.

title: ISRO PSLV-C50 Launches CMS-01 Communication Satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre
description: ISRO launched the CMS-01 telecommunications satellite aboard PSLV-C50 on December 17, 2020 from Sriharikota, providing extended-C band coverage across the Indian mainland and islands.

title: Mitchell Marsh Unbeaten 77 Powers Australia to Maiden Men T20 World Cup Championship in Dubai
description: Marsh and David Warner dismantled New Zealand's bowling attack on November 14, 2021, chasing down 173 with seven deliveries to spare.

title: Ben Stokes Unbeaten Fifty and Sam Curran Bowling Lead England to T20 World Cup Triumph in Melbourne
description: Curran took 3 for 12 and Stokes guided England across the line on November 13, 2022 at the MCG against Pakistan, making England dual white-ball world champions.

title: Mohan Charan Majhi Takes Oath as First BJP Chief Minister of Odisha at Janata Maidan
description: Tribal leader Mohan Charan Majhi was sworn in as Chief Minister on June 12, 2024 in Bhubaneswar, ending the twenty-four year tenure of Naveen Patnaik.

title: Radamel Falcao Header Powers Porto to Europa League Triumph Over Braga in Dublin
description: Andre Villas-Boas' Porto completed an undefeated European campaign on May 18, 2011 at the Aviva Stadium, with Falcao scoring his record 17th goal of the tournament.

title: Radamel Falcao Double Guides Atletico Madrid Past Athletic Bilbao in Bucharest Final
description: Diego Simeone won his first European trophy as manager on May 9, 2012 at the Arena Nationala as Falcao struck twice in a commanding 3-0 victory.

title: Branislav Ivanovic 93rd-Minute Looping Header Wins Europa League for Chelsea Over Benfica
description: Fernando Torres and Ivanovic scored on May 15, 2013 at the Amsterdam Arena, making Chelsea the first club to hold the Champions League and Europa League concurrently.

title: Mathew Hayman Stuns Tom Boonen in Velodrome Sprint to Win 2016 Paris-Roubaix at Age 37
description: Overcoming a fractured arm suffered five weeks earlier on April 10, 2016, Australian domestique Hayman outsprinted four-time champion Boonen in the Roubaix Velodrome.

title: Sevilla Defeats Liverpool 3-1 in Basel to Win Third Consecutive Europa League Title
description: Unai Emery's side rallied from a goal down with second-half strikes from Gameiro and Coke on May 18, 2016 at St Jakob-Park to seal an unprecedented three-peat.

title: Paul Pogba and Henrikh Mkhitaryan Strikes Deliver Europa League to Manchester United in Stockholm
description: Jose Mourinho's United defeated Ajax 2-0 on May 24, 2017 at Friends Arena, completing their set of all major European club honors.

title: Supreme Court Rules Living Will and Passive Euthanasia are Legally Permissible in Common Cause Verdict
description: A five-judge Constitution bench headed by CJI Dipak Misra affirmed the right to die with dignity on March 9, 2018, recognizing advance medical directives.

title: Supreme Court Strikes Down Section 497 Adultery Law as Unconstitutional and Gender-Biased
description: In the Joseph Shine case on September 27, 2018, a five-judge bench struck down the 158-year-old penal law on adultery as violative of Articles 14 and 21.

title: Eden Hazard Two Goals and Assist Inspire Chelsea to 4-1 Europa League Final Rout of Arsenal
description: In his final appearance for Chelsea on May 29, 2019 at Baku Olympic Stadium, Hazard dominated the London derby to deliver Maurizio Sarri his first major managerial trophy.

title: Luuk de Jong Two Headers Earn Sevilla Sixth Europa League Title Over Inter Milan in Cologne
description: Julen Lopetegui's Sevilla triumphed 3-2 in an entertaining clash on August 21, 2020 behind closed doors at RheinEnergieStadion, extending their tournament record.

title: Benjamin Pavard Volley Earns Bayern Munich Historic Sextuple in Club World Cup Final
description: Bayern defeated Mexico's Tigres UANL 1-0 on February 11, 2021 in Al Rayyan Qatar, becoming only the second club after Barcelona to hold all six major trophies at once.

title: ISRO PSLV-C51 Launches Brazilian Amazonia-1 Satellite and Eighteen Co-Passengers
description: ISRO's PSLV-C51 launched Amazonia-1, Brazil's first indigenously developed optical Earth observation satellite, and eighteen co-passenger payloads on February 28, 2021.

title: Geronimo Rulli Scores and Saves in 22-Kick Shootout as Villarreal Beats Manchester United
description: Following a 1-1 deadlock on May 26, 2021 in Gdansk, goalkeeper Rulli scored his penalty and saved David de Gea's kick to give Unai Emery his fourth Europa League.

title: ISRO GSLV-F10 Mission Suffers Cryogenic Stage Ignition Anomaly Failing to Orbit EOS-03
description: ISRO's GSLV-F10 rocket failed to inject the EOS-03 earth observation satellite on August 12, 2021 due to a cryogenic upper stage ignition anomaly four minutes into flight.

title: Kai Havertz 117th-Minute Penalty Delivers Maiden Club World Cup to Chelsea in Abu Dhabi
description: Havertz sent the goalkeeper the wrong way in extra time on February 12, 2022 against Palmeiras, completing Roman Abramovich's clean sweep of every available club trophy.

title: ISRO PSLV-C52 Launches EOS-04 Radar Imaging Satellite into Polar Sun-Synchronous Orbit
description: ISRO's PSLV-C52 successfully launched the 1,710 kg EOS-04 radar imaging satellite on February 14, 2022 from Sriharikota to provide all-weather radar data for agriculture and flood mapping.

title: Eintracht Frankfurt Edges Rangers on Penalties in Seville to Win First European Trophy in 42 Years
description: Rafael Borre equalized in the 69th minute and converted the winning spot kick on May 18, 2022 at Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan, delivering Frankfurt an undefeated triumph.

title: Gonzalo Montiel Decisive Penalty Clinches Seventh Europa League Title for Sevilla Over Roma
description: After a grueling 1-1 draw on May 31, 2023 at Puskas Arena in Budapest, World Cup winner Montiel repeated his Qatar heroics to hand Jose Mourinho his first European final defeat.

title: Julian Alvarez Scores Fastest Goal in Club World Cup Final History as Manchester City Wins Five Trophies
description: Scoring after forty seconds on December 22, 2023 in Jeddah, Alvarez struck twice as Pep Guardiola's City defeated Fluminense 4-0 to complete a five-trophy year.

title: Ademola Lookman Stunning Hat-Trick Powers Atalanta to Europa League Triumph Over Leverkusen
description: Lookman became the first player to score a hat-trick in a one-legged European final since 1969 on May 22, 2024 in Dublin, ending Bayer Leverkusen's 51-match unbeaten run.

title: Joel Stransky Extra-Time Drop Goal Wins 1995 Rugby World Cup for South Africa
description: Before President Nelson Mandela wearing the green Springbok jersey on June 24, 1995 at Ellis Park in Johannesburg, South Africa defeated New Zealand 15-12 in extra time.

title: Twenty-One-Year-Old Sebastian Vettel Wins Wet Italian Grand Prix for Toro Rosso at Monza
description: Driving in torrential rain on September 14, 2008, Vettel took pole and victory, becoming the youngest driver to win a Formula One race at the time.

title: Jenson Button Recovers from Six Pit Stops and Last Place to Win Four-Hour Canadian Grand Prix
description: In the longest race in Formula One history on June 12, 2011 in Montreal, McLaren's Button overtook Sebastian Vettel on the final lap following a two-hour rain stoppage.

title: Fernando Alonso Drives from Eleventh on Grid to Emotional Victory in Valencia European Grand Prix
description: Pulling off sensational overtakes around the outside of turns on June 24, 2012, Alonso broke down in tears on the podium before his home Spanish fans.

title: Supreme Court Recognizes Transgender Persons as Third Gender in Landmark NALSA Judgment
description: Delivered on April 15, 2014 by Justices KS Radhakrishnan and AK Sikri, the verdict affirmed equal constitutional rights and gender self-identification for transgender persons.

title: Supreme Court Rules Parliament Cannot Bypass Judicial Appointments via National Judicial Appointments Commission
description: A five-judge Constitution bench struck down the 99th Constitutional Amendment and NJAC Act on October 16, 2015, upholding the primacy of the Collegium system.

title: Eighteen-Year-Old Max Verstappen Wins Spanish Grand Prix on Red Bull Racing Debut
description: Following a first-lap collision between Mercedes teammates Hamilton and Rosberg on May 15, 2016 in Barcelona, Verstappen held off Kimi Raikkonen to become the youngest winner in F1 history.

title: Philippe Gilbert Launches Audacious 55-Kilometer Solo Breakaway to Win 2017 Tour of Flanders
description: Attacking over the steep slopes of the Oude Kwaremont on April 2, 2017, Belgian champion Gilbert rode alone to the finish in Oudenaarde, walking across the line with bike aloft.

title: Supreme Court Delivers Verdict Lifting Ban on Entry of Women of Menstruating Age into Sabarimala Temple
description: A 4-1 Constitution bench ruled on September 28, 2018 that devotion cannot be subjected to gender discrimination, allowing women of all ages into Sabarimala.

title: Charles Leclerc Resists Relentless Mercedes Pressure to Win Italian Grand Prix for Ferrari at Monza
description: Before 100,000 passionate tifosi on September 8, 2019, Leclerc defended fiercely against Hamilton and Bottas to claim Ferrari's first home victory since 2010.

title: Pierre Gasly Scores Miraculous Maiden Victory for AlphaTauri in Chaotic Italian Grand Prix at Monza
description: Holding off Carlos Sainz by four-tenths of a second on September 6, 2020, Gasly became the first French driver to win an F1 race since Olivier Panis in 1996.

title: Lewis Hamilton Masters Torrential Turkish Grand Prix to Clinch Record-Equalling Seventh World Title
description: Driving from sixth on a treacherous drying track on November 15, 2020 in Istanbul, Hamilton made a set of intermediate tires last 50 laps to equal Michael Schumacher's seven crowns.

title: Lewis Hamilton Becomes First Driver in Formula One History to Win 100 Grand Prix Races
description: Capitalizing on late rain in Sochi on September 26, 2021, Hamilton took his 100th victory as long-time race leader Lando Norris slid off on slick tires.

title: Sonny Colbrelli Wins Epic Mud-Soaked Autumn Paris-Roubaix in Thrilling Three-Man Velodrome Sprint
description: Covered in thick mud on October 3, 2021, European champion Colbrelli outsprinted Florian Vermeersch and Mathieu van der Poel in the first rain-lashed Roubaix in 19 years.

title: Matej Mohoric Uses Dropper Seatpost in Daredevil Poggio Descent to Win 2022 Milan-San Remo
description: Deploying a mountain bike dropper seatpost on the perilous descent down the Poggio on March 19, 2022, Mohoric held off Anthony Turgis to win 'La Primavera'.

title: ISRO PSLV-C53 Launches Three Singaporean Satellites into Low Earth Orbit
description: ISRO's commercial arm NewSpace India launched three Singaporean satellites aboard PSLV-C53 on June 30, 2022, also demonstrating the PSLV Orbital Experimental Module POEM.

title: ISRO Maiden SSLV-D1 Small Satellite Launch Vehicle Suffers Upper Stage Sensor Anomaly
description: ISRO debuted its Small Satellite Launch Vehicle SSLV-D1 on August 7, 2022 from Sriharikota, but an accelerometer sensor anomaly placed the two satellites into an unstable circular orbit.

title: Tadej Pogacar Drops Mathieu van der Poel on Oude Kwaremont to Win 2023 Tour of Flanders
description: Attacking on the final cobbled climb on April 2, 2023, two-time Tour de France champion Pogacar became only the third rider in history to win both the Tour and Flanders.

title: Mathieu van der Poel Solos to Victory in Fastest-Ever Edition of Paris-Roubaix
description: Averaging a record 46.8 km/h over 256 kilometers of punishing cobblestones on April 9, 2023, the Dutch superstar rode away from John Degenkolb and Wout van Aert.

title: Mathieu van der Poel Launches Sixty-Kilometer Solo Attack to Retain Paris-Roubaix in Record Time
description: Attacking on the Orchies cobblestone sector on April 7, 2024, World Champion Van der Poel crossed the line three minutes ahead of the field in a masterclass.

title: Davor Suker Secures Golden Boot as Croatia Defeats Netherlands for World Cup Bronze in Paris
description: Prosinecki and Suker scored on July 11, 1998 at the Parc des Princes as tournament debutants Croatia capped an astonishing run by taking third place.

title: Hakan Sukur Scores Fastest Goal in World Cup History in Eleven Seconds in Daegu
description: Sukur scored straight from kickoff on June 29, 2002 before Ilhan Mansiz struck twice, giving Turkey a 3-2 victory over co-hosts South Korea for bronze.

title: Jonny Wilkinson 100th-Minute Drop Goal Delivers Rugby World Cup to England in Sydney
description: With twenty seconds remaining in extra time on November 22, 2003 at Stadium Australia, Wilkinson slotted a right-footed drop goal to defeat hosts Australia 20-17.

title: Bastian Schweinsteiger Long-Range Strikes Deliver World Cup Bronze to Germany in Stuttgart
description: Schweinsteiger scored two thunderous curling drives on July 8, 2006 as hosts Germany defeated Portugal 3-1 before an ecstatic home crowd.

title: Andres Iniesta 93rd-Minute Equalizer at Stamford Bridge Sends Barcelona to Rome Final
description: With ten men in stoppage time on May 6, 2009 in London, Iniesta fired a sublime outside-of-the-boot drive into the top corner, eliminating Chelsea on away goals.

title: Ten-Man Inter Milan Under Jose Mourinho Resists Barcelona at Camp Nou to Reach Final
description: Despite Thiago Motta's 28th-minute red card on April 28, 2010, Inter held on with 19 percent possession to advance 3-2 on aggregate, celebrated by Mourinho sprinting across the pitch.

title: Sami Khedira Late Header Earns Germany Third Place Over Uruguay in Port Elizabeth Thriller
description: After Diego Forlan scored a sublime volley, Jansen and Khedira struck on July 10, 2010 to give Joachim Low's young German side a 3-2 victory.

title: New Zealand Edges France 8-7 in Nail-Biting Rugby World Cup Final at Eden Park
description: Tony Woodcock scored a first-half try and fourth-choice fly-half Stephen Donald kicked a penalty on October 23, 2011 in Auckland as the All Blacks won their second title.

title: Fernando Torres Breakaway Goal Seals Dramatic Chelsea Champions League Victory at Camp Nou
description: Down to ten men after John Terry's dismissal on April 24, 2012, Torres rounded Victor Valdes in the 92nd minute to secure a 2-2 draw and 3-2 aggregate triumph.

title: Pranab Mukherjee Sworn in as Thirteenth President of Republic of India
description: Former finance minister and veteran statesman Pranab Mukherjee took the presidential oath on July 25, 2012 in the Central Hall of Parliament.

title: Robin van Persie and Daley Blind Goals Condemn Hosts Brazil to 3-0 Defeat in Brasilia
description: Louis van Gaal's Netherlands claimed third place on July 12, 2014 at the Estadio Nacional Mane Garrincha, finishing their World Cup campaign undefeated.

title: Dan Carter Masterclass Leads New Zealand Past Australia to Retain Rugby World Cup at Twickenham
description: Fly-half Carter kicked 19 points including a crucial 40-meter drop goal on October 31, 2015, making the All Blacks the first nation to win back-to-back Rugby World Cups.

title: Thomas Meunier and Eden Hazard Goals Earn Belgium Third Place Over England in St Petersburg
description: Roberto Martinez's golden generation achieved Belgium's best-ever World Cup finish on July 14, 2018 with a clinical 2-0 victory over England.

title: Siya Kolisi Leads South Africa to Inspiring 32-12 Rugby World Cup Victory Over England in Yokohama
description: With late tries from Makazole Mapimpi and Cheslin Kolbe on November 2, 2019, Kolisi became the first Black captain to lift the Webb Ellis Cup.

title: Jagdeep Dhankhar Sworn in as Fourteenth Vice President of India
description: Former West Bengal governor Jagdeep Dhankhar took the oath of office as Vice President and Rajya Sabha Chairman on August 11, 2022 at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

title: ISRO LVM3-M2 Launches Thirty-Six OneWeb Broadband Satellites in First Commercial Mission
description: ISRO's heavy-lift LVM3 rocket successfully deployed thirty-six OneWeb broadband communication satellites on October 23, 2022 in its maiden dedicated commercial multi-satellite mission.

title: ISRO PSLV-C54 Successfully Injects Oceansat-3 EOS-06 Along with Eight Nanosatellites
description: ISRO launched EOS-06 Oceansat-3 and eight nanosatellites including BhutanSat aboard PSLV-C54 on November 26, 2022 from Sriharikota, enhancing oceanographic and wind monitoring.

title: Mislav Orsic Exquisite Curler Wins World Cup Bronze Medal for Croatia Over Morocco
description: Josko Gvardiol's diving header and Orsic's clipping strike off the far post on December 17, 2022 in Al Rayyan sealed a 2-1 victory for Luka Modric's Croatia.

title: ISRO SSLV-D2 Successfully Launches Three Satellites Demonstrating Small Rocket Reliability
description: ISRO's SSLV-D2 successfully launched EOS-07, Janus-1, and AzaadiSAT-2 satellites on February 10, 2023 from Sriharikota, validating the new small launcher for commercial low-Earth-orbit missions.

title: Handre Pollard Penalties Power Fourteen-Man South Africa to Record Fourth Rugby World Cup in Paris
description: Despite captain Siya Kolisi and Sam Cane receiving cards on October 28, 2023 at the Stade de France, the Springboks edged New Zealand 12-11 in a defensive war of attrition.

title: ISRO PSLV-C8 Successfully Launches Italian AGILE Gamma-Ray Astronomy Satellite
description: ISRO's first dedicated commercial launch on April 23, 2007 deployed the 352 kg Italian scientific satellite AGILE into low Earth orbit from Sriharikota.

title: Sergio Aguero 93rd-Minute Stoppage Time Winner Snatches Premier League Title for Manchester City
description: Trailing QPR 1-2 in injury time on May 13, 2012, Edin Dzeko and Aguero scored in the 92nd and 94th minutes, snatching City's first league title in 44 years on goal difference.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo Breaks Champions League Single-Season Goal Record in 4-0 Rout of Bayern Munich
description: Ronaldo scored his 15th and 16th goals of the European campaign on April 29, 2014 at the Allianz Arena, as Carlo Ancelotti's Real Madrid handed Bayern their heaviest European home defeat.

title: Vincent Kompany Thirty-Yard Thunderbolt Against Leicester Preserves Manchester City Title March
description: City captain Kompany unleashed an astonishing long-range rocket into the top corner on May 6, 2019 at the Etihad, securing a vital 1-0 win to keep City one point ahead of Liverpool.

title: Naomi Osaka Defeats Victoria Azarenka in Three Sets to Win Second US Open Singles Crown
description: Naomi Osaka staged an impressive three-set comeback to defeat Victoria Azarenka at Arthur Ashe Stadium, capturing her second US Open championship and third major title.

title: Novak Djokovic Defeats Daniil Medvedev in Straight Sets to Win Ninth Australian Open Title
description: Novak Djokovic delivered a dominant straight-sets performance against Daniil Medvedev at Melbourne Park, securing his ninth Australian Open singles championship.

title: Ilkay Gundogan Scores Twice in Five Minutes as Manchester City Rallies to Win Premier League Title
description: Trailing Aston Villa 0-2 with fifteen minutes left on May 22, 2022, Gundogan and Rodri scored three goals in five minutes to retain the Premier League title by one point.

title: Yulimar Rojas Leaps 15.47 Meters to Win Third Consecutive World Triple Jump Title in Oregon
description: Venezuelan world record holder Rojas dominated the field on July 18, 2022 at Hayward Field in Eugene, winning by over half a meter.

title: Shericka Jackson Blazes 21.45 Seconds to Win World 200m Gold in Eugene
description: Jamaican sprinter Jackson clocked the second-fastest women's 200m time in history on July 21, 2022, defeating Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce and Dina Asher-Smith.

title: Bhupendra Patel Sworn in as Chief Minister of Gujarat for Second Consecutive Term
description: BJP leader Bhupendra Patel took oath at Helipad Ground Gandhinagar on December 12, 2022 after leading his party to a record 156 seats in the assembly elections.

title: Aryna Sabalenka Defeats Elena Rybakina to Win Maiden Grand Slam Title at Australian Open
description: Aryna Sabalenka fought back from a set down to defeat Elena Rybakina in the women's singles final at Melbourne Park, claiming her first career Grand Slam singles trophy.

title: ISRO LVM3-M3 Launches Thirty-Six OneWeb Satellites Completing Gen-1 Constellation
description: ISRO's LVM3-M3 placed thirty-six OneWeb satellites into 450 km circular polar orbit on March 26, 2023, marking NewSpace India's second major commercial multi-satellite deployment.

title: ISRO PSLV-C55 Launches Singaporean TeLEOS-2 Radar Satellite from Sriharikota
description: ISRO launched the 741 kg Singaporean synthetic aperture radar satellite TeLEOS-2 aboard PSLV-C55 on April 22, 2023 in a core-alone commercial flight from Sriharikota.

title: Manchester City Dispatches Real Madrid 4-0 at Etihad Stadium in Flawless Semifinal Masterclass
description: Bernardo Silva struck twice in the first half on May 17, 2023 as Pep Guardiola's side overwhelmed the reigning European champions 5-1 on aggregate to reach Istanbul.

title: Ryan Crouser Smashes World Athletics Championships Shot Put Record with 23.51m in Budapest
description: Competing despite blood clots in his leg on August 19, 2023, Crouser unleashed the second-longest throw in history on his final attempt to retain his world title.

title: Faith Kipyegon Runs Masterclass 3:54.87 to Claim Third World 1500m Gold in Budapest
description: Kenyan superstar Kipyegon led from gun to tape on August 22, 2023, confirming her status as the greatest female middle-distance runner of all time.

title: Karsten Warholm Reclaims 400m Hurdles World Title in Budapest Becoming First Three-Time Champion
description: Norwegian world record holder Warholm dominated the final on August 23, 2023, winning in 46.89 seconds to secure his third world gold medal.

title: Femke Bol Dominates Women 400m Hurdles Final to Win Maiden World Title in 51.70 in Budapest
description: Dutch sensation Bol won by more than a second on August 24, 2023 at the National Athletics Centre, redeeming her mixed relay fall on the opening night.

title: Faith Kipyegon Completes Historic 1500m and 5000m Double at World Championships in Budapest
description: Outsprinting Sifan Hassan in the final 100 meters on August 26, 2023, Kipyegon became the first woman ever to win both the 1500m and 5000m at the World Championships.

title: Vishnu Deo Sai Sworn in as First Tribal Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh
description: BJP leader Vishnu Deo Sai took the oath of office at Science College Ground in Raipur on December 13, 2023 in the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

title: Venetian Traveler Marco Polo Visits Motupalli Port Under Queen Rudrama Devi
description: Marco Polo visited the Kakatiya sea port of Motupalli in coastal Andhra, recording in his travels the prosperous diamond trade, exquisite muslin textiles, and the wise rule of Queen Rudrama Devi.

title: Giuseppe Mazzini Founds Young Italy Movement in Marseille
description: Exiled Italian republican Giuseppe Mazzini founded the secret society Young Italy in Marseille, advocating a unified, independent, and republican Italian nation through popular uprising.

title: King Charles Albert Promulgates Statuto Albertino Constitution in Piedmont Sardinia
description: King Charles Albert of Sardinia-Piedmont promulgated the Statuto Albertino, establishing a constitutional monarchy with bicameral parliament that later served as the constitution of united Italy.

title: Count Cavour Appointed Prime Minister of Piedmont Sardinia
description: King Victor Emmanuel II appointed Count Camillo Benso di Cavour as Prime Minister of Sardinia-Piedmont, initiating economic modernisation, railway expansion, and diplomatic alliances.

title: Piedmont Sardinia Dispatches Expeditionary Army to Crimean War
description: Prime Minister Cavour dispatched fifteen thousand Piedmontese troops under General Alfonso La Marmora to the Crimea, earning international diplomatic standing at the subsequent Congress of Paris.

title: Battle of Montebello Franco Piedmontese Forces Repulse Austrian Advance
description: French and Sardinian troops commanded by General Forey halted and repulsed Austrian Field Marshal Stadion corps at Montebello, opening the Second Italian War of Independence.

title: Ghadar Party Formed in Astoria Oregon by Indian Immigrants to Overthrow British Colonial Rule
description: Indian expatriates and nationalists led by Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, and Kartar Singh Sarabha met in Astoria, Oregon to found the revolutionary Ghadar Party dedicated to freeing India from British rule.

title: Vallabhbhai Patel Launches Bardoli Satyagraha Against Unjust British Land Revenue Assessment
description: Vallabhbhai Patel convened a conference of farmers in Bardoli, Gujarat, officially initiating the non-violent no-tax campaign that earned him the revered title of Sardar.

title: British Colonial Police Arrest Labor and Communist Leaders Across India in Meerut Conspiracy Case
description: British authorities staged coordinated nationwide raids arresting 31 trade union and socialist leaders in the Meerut Conspiracy Case to suppress rising communist and labor activism.

title: Congress Socialist Party Formally Established at Anjuman-e-Islamia Hall in Patna
description: Socialist leaders within the Indian National Congress including Jayaprakash Narayan, Acharya Narendra Deva, and Ram Manohar Lohia convened in Patna to form the Congress Socialist Party.

title: British Prime Minister Clement Attlee Introduces Indian Independence Bill in Parliament
description: Prime Minister Clement Attlee introduced the historic Indian Independence Bill in the British House of Commons, providing for the partition of British India into the independent Dominions of India and Pakistan.

title: Soviet Union Defeats Yugoslavia in Extra Time to Win Inaugural European Nations Cup in Paris
description: Viktor Ponedelnik headed a 113th-minute extra-time winner at the Parc des Princes as the Soviet Union defeated Yugoslavia 2-1 to capture the first European Nations' Cup.

title: Spain Defeats Soviet Union 2-1 in Madrid to Win 1964 European Nations Cup
description: Marcelino Martinez scored an 84th-minute diving header at the Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid to carry Spain to a 2-1 victory over the defending champion Soviet Union.

title: Italy Defeats Yugoslavia 2-0 in Final Replay in Rome to Win UEFA Euro 1968
description: Following a 1-1 draw in the first match, goals from Luigi Riva and Pietro Anastasi at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome guided Italy to a 2-0 replay win to claim the European championship.

title: West Germany Defeats Soviet Union 3-0 in Brussels to Win UEFA Euro 1972
description: Gerd Muller scored two goals and Herbert Wimmer added a third at Heysel Stadium in Brussels as Helmut Schon's West Germany swept aside the Soviet Union 3-0 in the European Championship final.

title: Antonin Panenka Scores Legendary Chipped Penalty as Czechoslovakia Wins Euro 1976
description: Antonin Panenka famously chipped the decisive penalty down the center past Sepp Maier in Belgrade, sealing a 5-3 shootout win for Czechoslovakia over West Germany in the European final.

title: Horst Hrubesch Header Fires West Germany to 2-1 Win Over Belgium in Euro 1980 Final
description: Horst Hrubesch scored twice, including an 88th-minute headed winner from a corner at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome, leading West Germany to a 2-1 victory over Belgium to win Euro 1980.

title: Michel Platini Scores Ninth Goal of Tournament as France Defeats Spain in Euro 1984 Final
description: Michel Platini converted a free-kick for his record ninth goal of the tournament at the Parc des Princes as France defeated Spain 2-0 to claim their first major international football trophy.

title: Marco van Basten Scores Iconic Volley as Netherlands Defeats Soviet Union in Euro 1988 Final
description: Marco van Basten unleashed a breathtaking dipping volley from an acute angle at Munich's Olympiastadion, sealing a 2-0 victory for the Netherlands over the USSR to win Euro 1988.

title: Denmark Stuns World Champions Germany 2-0 in Gothenburg to Complete Fairy-Tale Euro 1992 Triumph
description: Having qualified as late replacements for Yugoslavia, Denmark completed one of football's greatest upsets as John Jensen and Kim Vilfort scored to defeat Germany 2-0 in Gothenburg.

title: Ketamalla Constructs Twin Shrines of Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu
description: Hoysala courtier Ketamalla commissioned the Dvikuta twin Shiva temple Hoysaleswara at Halebidu, carving thousands of chloritic schist relief friezes of elephants, lions, and epics.

title: Hoysala Emperor Veera Ballala II Crowns Himself Independent Sovereign
description: Veera Ballala II declared complete Hoysala sovereign independence from Western Chalukya suzerainty, defeating Chalukya forces and establishing an empire spanning the southern Deccan.

title: Hoysala King Veera Ballala III Establishes Fortified Base at Hosapattana Hampi
description: Veera Ballala III established a strategic fortified northern outpost at Hosapattana on the Tungabhadra River, laying the geographic and defensive foundation for the Vijayanagara Empire.

title: Battle of Palestro Sardinian Army and Zouaves Repulse Austrian Assault
description: King Victor Emmanuel II fought alongside French 3rd Zouave Regiment at Palestro in Lombardy, repelling Austrian counterattacks across flooded irrigation ditches.

title: Armistice of Villafranca Napoleon III and Franz Joseph Conclude Peace
description: Emperor Napoleon III met Austrian Emperor Franz Joseph I at Villafranca without consulting Cavour, agreeing to transfer Lombardy to France for transfer to Sardinia while leaving Venice Austrian.

title: Garibaldi and the Thousand Sail from Quarto for Sicilian Expedition
description: Giuseppe Garibaldi and approximately one thousand Redshirt volunteers set sail aboard steamships Piemonte and Lombardo from Quarto near Genoa to overthrow the Bourbon Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

title: National Institute of Design Founded in Ahmedabad Setting Benchmark for Design Education in India
description: The Government of India established the National Institute of Design in Ahmedabad following recommendations from the landmark Eames Report to advance industrial and visual communication design.

title: Unit Trust of India Commences Operations as Pioneer Mutual Fund and Financial Institution
description: The Unit Trust of India was formally established under the UTI Act of 1963 to mobilize small domestic savings and channel individual investments into the nation's capital markets.

title: Central Pollution Control Board Constituted Under Water Prevention and Control of Pollution Act
description: The Government of India constituted the Central Pollution Control Board as a statutory authority to advise the central government on environmental protection and promote cleanliness of streams and wells.

title: Bureau of Indian Standards Replaces Indian Standards Institution to Regulate Quality Standards
description: The Bureau of Indian Standards was officially established under the BIS Act of 1986, taking over from the Indian Standards Institution to oversee product certification and national quality standards.

title: Romario Header Powers Brazil to 1-0 Win Over Uruguay at Maracana to Win 1989 Copa America
description: Romario scored a second-half header in front of 132,000 fans at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro as Brazil defeated Uruguay 1-0 to end their 40-year Copa America drought.

title: Gabriel Batistuta Brace Fires Argentina to 2-1 Victory Over Mexico in 1993 Copa America Final
description: Gabriel Batistuta scored two second-half goals at the Estadio Monumental in Guayaquil, Ecuador, as Alfio Basile's Argentina defeated debutants Mexico 2-1 to retain their Copa America title.

title: National Highways Authority of India Operationalized to Modernize National Highway Network
description: The National Highways Authority of India became fully operational as an autonomous agency under the Ministry of Surface Transport, entrusted with developing and maintaining primary highway corridors.

title: Oliver Bierhoff Scores First Golden Goal in Major Football History as Germany Wins Euro 1996
description: Substitute Oliver Bierhoff scored twice, including the first-ever golden goal in the 95th minute at Wembley Stadium, as Germany defeated the Czech Republic 2-1 to capture Euro 1996.

title: Ronaldo and Ze Roberto Score as Brazil Overcomes Bolivia in Altitude to Win 1997 Copa America
description: Edmundo, Ronaldo, and Ze Roberto scored at the Estadio Hernando Siles in La Paz, 3,600 meters above sea level, as Mario Zagallo's Brazil defeated hosts Bolivia 3-1 to win the Copa America.

title: Rivaldo and Ronaldo Score Two Goals Each as Brazil Sweeps Uruguay 3-0 in 1999 Copa America Final
description: Rivaldo scored twice in the first half and Ronaldo added a third in Asuncion, Paraguay, as Wanderley Luxemburgo's Brazil defeated Uruguay 3-0 to defend their Copa America championship.

title: David Trezeguet Scores Golden Goal as France Defeats Italy 2-1 in Rotterdam for Euro 2000
description: Sylvain Wiltord's 93rd-minute equalizer forced extra time before David Trezeguet smashed a 103rd-minute golden goal volley at De Kuip, making world champions France European champions.

title: Ivan Cordoba Header Seals Maiden Copa America Championship for Hosts Colombia in Bogota
description: Captain Ivan Cordoba headed home a 65th-minute free-kick at El Campin in Bogota as Colombia defeated Mexico 1-0, winning the Copa America without conceding a single goal in the entire tournament.

title: Adriano Strikes in 93rd Minute as Brazil Defeats Argentina on Penalties in 2004 Copa America Final
description: Adriano controlled with his back to goal and volleyed an equalizer in the 93rd minute in Lima before Brazil prevailed 4-2 in the penalty shootout over rivals Argentina to win the Copa America.

title: Julio Baptista and Dani Alves Fire Brazil to 3-0 Rout Over Argentina in 2007 Copa America Final
description: Julio Baptista scored early and Dani Alves added a third as Dunga's disciplined Brazil comprehensively outplayed Lionel Messi's Argentina 3-0 at the Estadio Jose Pachencho Romero in Maracaibo.

title: Garibaldi Captures Palermo After Fierce Street Fighting
description: Giuseppe Garibaldi and his insurgent army breached the Porta Termini and took control of Palermo after four days of urban barricade warfare against twenty thousand Bourbon troops.

title: Battle of Milazzo Garibaldi Redshirts Defeat Bourbon Fortress Garrison
description: Garibaldi volunteers defeated Colonel Bosco Bourbon infantry outside Milazzo castle in Sicily, forcing the evacuation of the fortress and opening the way to the Italian mainland.

title: Garibaldi Crosses Strait of Messina Landing at Melito in Calabria
description: Garibaldi slipped across the Strait of Messina aboard the steamer Franklin, landing at Melito di Porto Salvo in Calabria to launch his offensive against Naples.

title: Battle of Castelfidardo Piedmontese Army Defeats Papal Forces
description: Sardinian generals Cialdini and Fanti defeated General de Pimodan Papal army at Castelfidardo in the Marches, securing papal territories of Umbria and the Marches for united Italy.

title: Battle of the Volturnus Garibaldi Repulses Bourbon Royalist Offensive
description: Garibaldi thirty thousand volunteers repulsed a major counter-offensive by King Francis II Bourbon royalist army along the Volturno River in the largest pitched battle of the expedition.

title: Siege of Gaeta Concludes Ending Bourbon Rule in Southern Italy
description: Bourbon King Francis II and Queen Maria Sophie surrendered the coastal fortress of Gaeta to General Cialdini Piedmontese besiegers, terminating the historic Bourbon dynasty of Naples.

title: First International Film Festival of India Opens at New Empire Cinema in Bombay
description: Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated the inaugural International Film Festival of India in Bombay, screening 40 feature films and introducing Italian neorealist cinema to Indian filmmakers.

title: Hrishikesh Mukherjee Directed Masterpiece Anand Premieres Across Theatres in India
description: The classic Hindi drama Anand starring Rajesh Khanna as a terminally ill optimist and Amitabh Bachchan as Dr. Bhaskar Banerjee was released in theatres, earning universal critical and public acclaim.

title: Indo-Bangladeshi Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Peace Signed in Dacca
description: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and Prime Minister Sheikh Mujibur Rahman signed a 25-year bilateral friendship and cooperation treaty in Dacca to solidify bilateral ties and post-war reconstruction.

title: Emmanuel Amuneke Brace Powers Nigeria to 2-1 Comeback Win Over Zambia for 1994 AFCON Title
description: Playing his first match of the tournament, winger Emmanuel Amuneke scored twice in Tunis as Clemens Westerhof's Super Eagles defeated Zambia 2-1 to win Nigeria's second Africa Cup of Nations.

title: Mark Williams Brace Fires South Africa to 2-0 Win Over Tunisia for 1996 AFCON in Johannesburg
description: Substitute Mark Williams scored two quickfire second-half goals at FNB Stadium in Johannesburg as Bafana Bafana defeated Tunisia 2-0 before President Nelson Mandela to win their maiden AFCON.

title: Ahmed Hassan and Tarek Mostafa Score as Egypt Defeats South Africa 2-0 for 1998 AFCON Title
description: Ahmed Hassan's long-range drive and Tarek Mostafa's strike inside the opening fifteen minutes in Ouagadougou propelled Mahmoud El-Gohary's Egypt to a 2-0 win over South Africa for their fourth AFCON crown.

title: Cameroon Defeats Hosts Nigeria on Penalties in Lagos Thriller to Win 2000 Africa Cup of Nations
description: Rigobert Song converted the decisive penalty at the National Stadium in Surulere, Lagos, after a 2-2 extra-time draw, securing Cameroon's third AFCON title in a contentious shootout.

title: Lagaan and Gadar Ek Prem Katha Release Simultaneously in Monumental Box Office Clash
description: Aamir Khan's colonial cricket epic Lagaan and Sunny Deol's partition drama Gadar: Ek Prem Katha were both released in theatres on the same day, going on to become landmark cultural and commercial blockbusters.

title: Cameroon Defeats Senegal on Penalties in Bamako to Retain Africa Cup of Nations Championship
description: Following 120 scoreless minutes at the Stade du 26 Mars in Bamako, Mali, Cameroon defeated El Hadji Diouf's Senegal 3-2 on penalties to become the first team to defend the AFCON title since Ghana in 1965.

title: Ziad Jaziri Strike Powers Hosts Tunisia to 2-1 Victory Over Morocco for Maiden 2004 AFCON Title
description: Francileudo Santos and Ziad Jaziri scored at the Stade 7 Novembre in Rades as Roger Lemerre's Tunisia defeated regional rivals Morocco 2-1 to capture their first-ever Africa Cup of Nations trophy.

title: Luis Suarez and Diego Forlan Double Fire Uruguay to Record 15th Copa America Title in Buenos Aires
description: Luis Suarez scored the opener and Diego Forlan added two goals at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires as Uruguay defeated Paraguay 3-0 to capture a record 15th Copa America championship.

title: Chile Defeats Argentina on Penalties at MetLife Stadium to Win Copa America Centenario
description: Francisco Silva converted the decisive penalty in East Rutherford, New Jersey, after Lionel Messi skied his spot-kick, sealing Chile's back-to-back Copa America final shootout victories over Argentina.

title: Gabriel Jesus and Everton Score as Ten-Man Brazil Defeats Peru 3-1 to Win 2019 Copa America
description: Everton, Gabriel Jesus, and Richarlison scored at the Maracana Stadium as Tite's Brazil defeated Peru 3-1 despite Jesus receiving a second-half red card, securing their ninth Copa America crown.

title: SS Rajamouli Directed Epic Period Action Film RRR Premieres Worldwide in Theatres
description: S.S. Rajamouli's Telugu epic RRR starring N.T. Rama Rao Jr. and Ram Charan as fictionalized revolutionaries was released worldwide, grossing over 1,200 crore rupees and earning global acclaim.

title: Battle of Aspromonte Italian Royal Troops Halt Garibaldi March on Rome
description: Italian regular bersaglieri intercepted Giuseppe Garibaldi volunteer force on the slopes of Aspromonte in Calabria, wounding Garibaldi in the foot and arresting him to avoid war with France.

title: King William I Appoints Otto von Bismarck Minister President of Prussia
description: Prussian King William I appointed Otto von Bismarck as Minister President and Foreign Minister to overcome the parliamentary constitutional crisis regarding military budget reforms.

title: London Conference on Schleswig Holstein Fails to Reach Diplomatic Solution
description: Envoys of the European Great Powers meeting in London failed to resolve the Danish-German succession dispute over Schleswig and Holstein, leading to resumed military hostilities.

title: September Convention Signed Italy Agrees to Relocate Capital to Florence
description: Italy and France signed the September Convention, whereby Napoleon III agreed to withdraw French garrison troops from Rome and Italy agreed to relocate its national capital from Turin to Florence.

title: Gastein Convention Prussian Austrian Partition of Schleswig Holstein Administration
description: Prussia and Austria agreed at Bad Gastein to divide administration of conquered Danish duchies, with Prussia administering Schleswig and Austria governing Holstein.

title: Battle of Mentana French Papal Troops Defeat Garibaldi Volunteers
description: French forces equipped with breech-loading Chassepot rifles assisted papal soldiers in crushing Garibaldi volunteer legion at Mentana, preventing his capture of Rome.

title: James Hunt Drives Through Torrents at Fuji to Win F1 World Championship by One Point
description: In monsoon conditions at Fuji Speedway, James Hunt drove his McLaren to third place following Niki Lauda's withdrawal, clinching the 1976 Formula One World Championship by a single point.

title: Yash Raj Films Romantic Drama Veer-Zaara Premieres Worldwide Across Diwali Weekend
description: Yash Chopra's cross-border romance Veer-Zaara starring Shah Rukh Khan and Preity Zinta premiered worldwide, featuring legendary posthumous music compositions by Madan Mohan.

title: Egypt Defeats Ivory Coast 4-2 on Penalties in Cairo to Capture Fifth Africa Cup of Nations
description: Goalkeeper Essam El-Hadary saved penalties from Didier Drogba and Bakari Kone at the Cairo International Stadium as Hassan Shehata's Egypt won 4-2 on penalties following a goalless draw.

title: Mohamed Aboutrika Strike Sinks Cameroon as Egypt Retains Africa Cup of Nations in Accra
description: Mohamed Zidan dispossessed Rigobert Song and squared for Mohamed Aboutrika to slot home a 77th-minute winner at Ohene Djan Stadium in Accra, securing a 1-0 win for Egypt to retain the title.

title: Rajkumar Hirani Comedy Drama 3 Idiots Premieres Shattering Box Office Records Worldwide
description: Aamir Khan starred in Rajkumar Hirani's coming-of-age comedy drama 3 Idiots, based on Chetan Bhagat's novel Five Point Someone, becoming the highest-grossing Indian film of its time.

title: Super-Sub Gedo Strikes as Egypt Edges Ghana 1-0 in Luanda for Historic AFCON Three-Peat
description: Tournament sensation Mohamed Nagy Gedo curled in an 85th-minute winner at the Estadio 11 de Novembro in Luanda, guiding Egypt to an unprecedented third consecutive Africa Cup of Nations crown.

title: Stoppila Sunzu Scores Decisive Shootout Penalty as Zambia Defeats Ivory Coast for 2012 AFCON
description: Stoppila Sunzu converted in sudden death at the Stade d'Angondje in Libreville as Herve Renard's Chipolopolo defeated Ivory Coast 8-7 on penalties to win an emotional maiden title in the city of the 1993 plane crash.

title: Sunday Mba Half-Volley Fires Nigeria to 1-0 Victory Over Burkina Faso for 2013 AFCON Trophy
description: Sunday Mba flicked the ball over a defender and volleyed home with his left foot at FNB Stadium in Johannesburg, sealing a 1-0 win for Stephen Keshi's Nigeria to capture their third African championship.

title: Goalkeeper Boubacar Barry Scores Winning Penalty as Ivory Coast Beats Ghana for 2015 AFCON
description: After saving counterpart Brimah Razak's penalty in sudden death in Bata, Equatorial Guinea, veteran goalkeeper Boubacar Barry converted his own spot-kick to give Ivory Coast a 9-8 shootout win.

title: Vincent Aboubakar Late Flick Fires Cameroon to 2-1 Comeback Win Over Egypt for 2017 AFCON
description: Vincent Aboubakar controlled with his chest, lobbed a defender, and volleyed into the corner in the 88th minute in Libreville as Hugo Broos' Indomitable Lions rallied from a goal down to beat Egypt 2-1.

title: Baghdad Bounedjah Deflected Strike Seals 1-0 Win for Algeria Over Senegal for 2019 AFCON Crown
description: Baghdad Bounedjah's second-minute shot took a wild deflection off Salif Sane to loop over Alfred Gomis at the Cairo International Stadium, delivering Algeria's first Africa Cup of Nations in 29 years.

title: Siddharth Anand Directed Spy Thriller Pathaan Breaks All-Time Hindi Opening Day Box Office Records
description: Shah Rukh Khan made a triumphant return to cinemas with Pathaan, breaking domestic box-office opening day records with over 100 crore rupees worldwide on day one.

title: Kochi Water Metro Commences Commercial Operations as First Integrated Urban Water Ferry System in India
description: India's first urban water ferry network, the Kochi Water Metro, began passenger operations connecting mainland Kochi with surrounding islands using battery-powered electric-hybrid catamarans.

title: Atlee Directed High-Octane Action Thriller Jawan Releases Globally Across Five Thousand Screens
description: Shah Rukh Khan and Nayanthara starred in the vigilante action thriller Jawan, shattering single-day box office collections and becoming the highest-grossing Hindi film in history.

title: Secret Prussian Italian Military Alliance Concluded in Berlin
description: Count Bismarck and Italian envoy General Govone signed a three-month secret defensive and offensive treaty against Austria, coordinating a two-front war for German and Italian unification.

title: Prussian Forces Invade Austrian Administered Holstein Starting Austro Prussian War
description: General Edwin von Manteuffel led Prussian regiments across the Eider River into Holstein, expelling the Austrian civil governor and declaring the German Confederation assembly broken.

title: Battle of Langensalza Prussian Army Captures Kingdom of Hanover
description: Prussian forces under General von Flies clashed with the Royal Hanoverian Army at Langensalza, forcing King George V of Hanover to surrender his kingdom to Prussian annexation.

title: Armistice of Nikolsburg Bismarck Restrains Prussian Annexation of Austrian Territory
description: Otto von Bismarck overcame King William I demands to march on Vienna, signing the preliminary Peace of Nikolsburg to secure Prussian dominance while preserving Austria as a future ally.

title: North German Confederation Reichstag Adopts Federal Constitution in Berlin
description: The constituent Reichstag of the North German Confederation voted to approve Bismarck federal constitution, establishing the Bundesrat, Reichstag, and Prussian royal presidency.

title: Ems Dispatch Bismarck Edits Imperial Telegram Provoking War with France
description: Bismarck condensed King William I telegraphic report of his conversation with French ambassador Benedetti at Bad Ems, releasing the sharp version to the press to provoke French outrage.

title: Niki Lauda Finishes Second at Estoril to Defeat Alain Prost by Half a Point for Third F1 Title
description: Niki Lauda carved through the field from eleventh on the grid in Portugal to finish second, edging McLaren teammate Alain Prost by 0.5 points in the closest championship finish in F1 history.

title: Ayrton Senna and Alain Prost Collide at Suzuka Chicane Deciding 1989 F1 World Championship
description: McLaren teammates Alain Prost and Ayrton Senna collided at the Casio Triangle on lap 47 of the Japanese Grand Prix, leading to Senna's controversial disqualification and handing Prost the title.

title: Ayrton Senna and Alain Prost Collide into Turn One at Suzuka Handing Senna Second F1 Title
description: Just 800 feet after the race start at Suzuka, Ayrton Senna drove into Alain Prost's Ferrari at 160 mph into the first corner, eliminating both cars and guaranteeing Senna his second world championship.

title: Ayrton Senna Gifts Suzuka Victory to Teammate Gerhard Berger After Clinching Third F1 Title
description: Having secured his third Formula One World Drivers' Championship when Nigel Mansell spun out, Ayrton Senna slowed on the final corner at Suzuka to allow McLaren teammate Gerhard Berger to win.

title: Michael Schumacher and Damon Hill Collide in Adelaide Deciding 1994 F1 Championship
description: Michael Schumacher clipped the outside wall and collided with Damon Hill at the East Terrace corner in Adelaide, putting both out of the race and securing the German's controversial first F1 title.

title: Michael Schumacher Wins Pacific Grand Prix at Aida to Become Youngest Double F1 World Champion
description: Michael Schumacher executed a three-stop strategy to perfection for Benetton at the TI Circuit Aida in Japan, defeating David Coulthard to wrap up his second consecutive world championship.

title: Damon Hill Wins Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka to Clinch 1996 Formula One World Championship
description: Damon Hill led from start to finish in the season finale at Suzuka following teammate Jacques Villeneuve's wheel failure, becoming the first son of a world champion to win the Formula One title.

title: Jacques Villeneuve Survives Schumacher Ramming at Jerez to Win 1997 F1 World Championship
description: When Jacques Villeneuve attempted an inside pass at Dry Sac corner at Jerez, Michael Schumacher turned into him and got beached in the gravel, allowing Villeneuve to nurse his Williams to 3rd and win the title.

title: Mika Hakkinen Dominates Suzuka to Clinch Maiden Formula One World Championship for McLaren
description: Mika Hakkinen drove an immaculate race from the front row at Suzuka after rival Michael Schumacher stalled on the grid, securing victory and his first Formula One World Drivers' Championship.

title: VVS Laxman Scores Epochal 281 at Eden Gardens to Resurrect India from Follow-On Against Australia
description: VVS Laxman played a legendary marathon innings of 281 at Kolkata's Eden Gardens, sharing a 376-run stand with Rahul Dravid after India was forced to follow on against Steve Waugh's Australia.

title: Somdev Devvarman Wins Men's Singles Tennis Gold Medal at Delhi 2010 Commonwealth Games
description: Somdev Devvarman defeated Greg Jones of Australia in straight sets at the R.K. Khanna Tennis Stadium to claim the men's singles tennis gold medal at the Commonwealth Games in Delhi.

title: Prime Minister Modi Inaugurates 351-Kilometre New Bhaupur to New Khurja Section of Eastern Freight Corridor
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the New Bhaupur-New Khurja stretch of the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor in Uttar Pradesh alongside the state-of-the-art Operation Control Centre at Prayagraj.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Dedicates 306-Kilometre Rewari-Madar Section of Western Dedicated Freight Corridor
description: The 306-kilometer Rewari-Madar section of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor in Haryana and Rajasthan was officially dedicated to the nation, featuring double-stack long-haul container train operations.

title: Rishabh Pant Smashes Unbeaten 89 as India Breaches Fortress Gabba in Historic Test Series Victory
description: India chased down 328 runs on the final day at the Brisbane Cricket Ground behind an unbeaten 89 by Rishabh Pant, ending Australia's 32-year unbeaten streak at the Gabba and winning the Border-Gavaskar Trophy.

title: Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan I Consecrated at Srirangam Weighing Himself in Gold
description: Pandya Emperor Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan I celebrated his digvijaya conquests at the Srirangam Temple, weighing himself against heaps of gold and gilding the sanctum vimana.

title: Sundara Pandya Defeats Hoysala Someshwara at Battle of Kannanur Koppam
