description: Alejandro G Inarritu's black comedy Birdman or The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance captured four Academy Awards including Best Picture.

title: The Shape of Water Wins Academy Award for Best Picture at 90th Annual Oscars Ceremony
description: Guillermo del Toro's romantic fantasy film The Shape of Water won four Academy Awards including Best Picture and Best Director at Dolby Theatre.

title: Justice Indu Malhotra Takes Oath Becoming First Woman Elevated Directly from Bar to Supreme Court
description: Senior Advocate Indu Malhotra was sworn in as a Supreme Court judge, becoming the first woman lawyer in Indian legal history to be elevated directly from the Bar to the apex court bench.

title: President Harry S Truman Formally Dedicates Everglades National Park in Florida
description: President Truman dedicated Everglades National Park to protect the delicate subtropical wilderness and biodiversity of southern Florida.

title: Nobel Laureate Sir CV Raman Inaugurates Raman Research Institute at Hebbal in Bangalore
description: Sir C.V. Raman founded the independent Raman Research Institute on land gifted by the Maharaja of Mysore, personally leading research in optics, spectroscopy, and crystal dynamics.

title: Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru Formally Names First Nuclear Reactor Apsara at Trombay
description: Prime Minister Nehru formally dedicated the Trombay swimming-pool reactor, naming it Apsara (celestial water nymph) to signify the tranquil harnessing of atomic power for human welfare.

title: Justice Anna Chandy Appointed First Woman High Court Judge in India at Kerala High Court
description: Anna Chandy was appointed judge of the Kerala High Court by President Rajendra Prasad, having earlier become the first female munsif in Anglo-Indian legal history in 1937.

title: Local Farmers Digging Well Unearth First Clues of Emperor Qin Terracotta Army in Xi'an
description: Chinese farmers digging a water well near Mount Li unearthed terracotta fragments leading to the discovery of Qin Shi Huang's buried army.

title: Greg LeMond Wins Tour de France by Record Eight Seconds in Final Time Trial on Champs-Elysees
description: American cyclist Greg LeMond used revolutionary aerodynamic handlebars to overturn a 50-second deficit on Laurent Fignon in Paris.

title: German Tourists Discover Preserved Chalcolithic Mummy Otzi the Iceman in Otztal Alps
description: Hikers Helmut and Erika Simon found the 5,300-year-old naturally mummified remains of a Copper Age hunter in the Alps along the Austrian-Italian border.

title: John Paxson Hits Dramatic Game-Winning Three-Pointer as Bulls Seal First Three-Peat in Phoenix
description: John Paxson drained an open three with 3.9 seconds remaining in Game 6 as Chicago defeated the Phoenix Suns to complete a three-peat.

title: Speleologists Discover Chauvet Cave Upper Paleolithic Animal Paintings in Ardeche France
description: Jean-Marie Chauvet and fellow cavers discovered pristine 36,000-year-old cave art depicting lions, mammoths, and rhinos in southern France.

title: Marco Pantani Wins 1998 Tour de France Completing Historic Giro-Tour Double in Paris
description: Italian climber Marco Pantani rode into the Champs-Elysees in the yellow jersey, becoming the last cyclist to win both the Giro and Tour in one year.

title: Joint Australian-Indonesian Research Team Unearths Remains of Homo Floresiensis on Flores Island
description: Archaeologists discovered fossil remains of a diminutive extinct hominin species dubbed the Hobbit in Liang Bua cave on Flores, Indonesia.

title: Detroit Pistons Stun Heavily Favored Los Angeles Lakers in Five Games to Win 2004 NBA Title
description: Chauncey Billups and Ben Wallace led Larry Brown's suffocating Detroit Pistons defense to a dominant 100-87 Game 5 win in Auburn Hills.

title: Germany Defeats Brazil Two-Nil to Retain FIFA Women's World Cup Without Conceding a Single Goal
description: Nadine Angerer saved a Marta penalty in Shanghai as Germany became the first team to defend the Women's World Cup.

title: Dirk Nowitzki Leads Dallas Mavericks to Maiden NBA Championship Defeating Miami Heat in Game 6
description: German superstar Dirk Nowitzki earned Finals MVP honors as the Mavericks defeated Miami's Big Three in Miami to win Dallas's first title.

title: Final Transit of Venus of the 21st Century Viewed by Millions Across the Pacific Ocean
description: Skywatchers observed the second transit of Venus in eight years, marked as the final transit event until the year 2117.

title: LeBron James Scores 37 Points in Game 7 as Miami Heat Defeats San Antonio Spurs to Repeat
description: LeBron James hit a clutch pull-up jumper with 27 seconds left to cap a 95-88 Game 7 victory over the Spurs in Miami.

title: Toronto Raptors Defeat Golden State Warriors in Game 6 to Win First NBA Championship Outside USA
description: Kawhi Leonard led the Toronto Raptors to a 114-110 Game 6 victory at Oracle Arena, capturing Canada's first NBA championship.

title: Tadej Pogacar Snatches Tour de France Victory on La Planche des Belles Filles Time Trial
description: Young Slovenian Tadej Pogacar overturned a 57-second deficit on Primoz Roglic in an unforgettable uphill time trial to win his first Tour.

title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella Receives Padma Bhushan from Indian Consul General in Seattle
description: Microsoft chairman and CEO Satya Nadella was formally conferred India's third-highest civilian honor, the Padma Bhushan, by Consul General Somnath Ghosh in Seattle.

title: Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai Presented Padma Bhushan by Indian Ambassador in San Francisco
description: Indian Ambassador to the United States Taranjit Singh Sandhu presented the Padma Bhushan in Trade and Industry to Google and Alphabet chief Sundar Pichai in San Francisco.

title: Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers Discovers Asteroid Vesta in Asteroid Belt
description: German astronomer Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers discovered 4 Vesta from Bremen, the brightest asteroid visible from Earth.

title: French Astronomer Jules Janssen Observes Solar Helium Spectral Line During Guntur Eclipse
description: Jules Janssen analyzed the solar spectrum during a total eclipse in Guntur, discovering the yellow spectral line of element helium.

title: Richard Byrd and Bernt Balchen Complete First Flight Over Geographic South Pole
description: American explorer Richard E. Byrd and pilot Bernt Balchen flew the Ford Trimotor Floyd Bennett over the South Pole from Little America base.

title: Lowell Observatory Formally Announces Discovery of Ninth Planet Pluto on Percival Lowell Birthday
description: Lowell Observatory publicly telegraphed the discovery of Trans-Neptunian Planet X, later named Pluto, to the Harvard College Observatory.

title: Jamaica Formally Proclaims Independence from Great Britain with Alexander Bustamante as Prime Minister
description: Jamaica celebrated independence at the National Stadium in Kingston, becoming the first English-speaking Caribbean nation to gain independence.

title: Trinidad and Tobago Achieves Formal Independence from Great Britain under Eric Williams
description: Prime Minister Eric Williams led Trinidad and Tobago into national independence, establishing sovereign governance in Port of Spain.

title: Barbados Achieves National Independence from United Kingdom under Prime Minister Errol Barrow
description: Errol Barrow led Barbados to independence from Britain at the Garrison Savannah in Bridgetown, raising the newly designed ultramarine and gold trident flag.

title: Astronomers Aboard Concorde Prototype Chase Total Solar Eclipse Across Africa for 74 Minutes
description: A French-British scientific team flew Concorde 001 at Mach 2 along the eclipse path over the Sahara, setting an enduring record for totality observation.

title: Kaziranga Upgraded and Declared Full-Fledged National Park by Government of Assam
description: The Assam government formally designated the 430-square-kilometer Kaziranga floodplain along the Brahmaputra River as a National Park, securing the primary sanctuary for the great one-horned rhinoceros.

title: Australian Parliament Passes Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Act Creating Marine Protected Sanctuary
description: Australia passed landmark conservation legislation to protect the 2,300-kilometer Great Barrier Reef coral ecosystem from oil drilling and mining.

title: Ministry of Environment Launches Project Elephant to Provide Financial and Technical Support to Range States
description: The Government of India launched Project Elephant to ensure the long-term survival of viable elephant populations in their natural habitats and secure vital elephant migratory corridors.

title: Nigel Mansell Clinches Maiden Formula One World Championship with Second Place in Hungary
description: British driver Nigel Mansell drove the active-suspension Williams-Renault FW14B to second place at the Hungaroring to clinch his world title.

title: Paula Radcliffe Smashes Women's Marathon World Record by Over Three Minutes in London
description: British runner Paula Radcliffe ran a legendary time of 2:15:25 at the London Marathon, establishing an iconic world record that stood for 16 years.

title: Six-Time World Boxing Champion MC Mary Kom Receives Padma Bhushan from President Pranab Mukherjee
description: President Pranab Mukherjee conferred the Padma Bhushan upon Olympic bronze medalist M.C. Mary Kom and batting stalwart Rahul Dravid at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

title: Junot Diaz Wins Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao
description: Dominican-American author Junot Diaz won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for his debut novel exploring immigrant identity and the Trujillo dictatorship.

title: Elizabeth Strout Wins Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for Connected Story Novel Olive Kitteridge
description: Elizabeth Strout was awarded the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for Olive Kitteridge, featuring thirteen interconnected tales set in coastal Maine.

title: Robert Edwards Awarded Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for Development of In Vitro Fertilization
description: The Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet awarded the prize to British physiologist Robert Edwards for pioneering human IVF therapy.

title: John Gurdon and Shinya Yamanaka Awarded Nobel Prize for Discovery That Mature Cells Can Be Reprogrammed
description: Gurdon and Yamanaka won the Nobel Prize in Medicine for discovering that differentiated adult cells can be reprogrammed to pluripotency.

title: Donna Tartt Wins Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for Dickensian Epic The Goldfinch
description: Donna Tartt won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for The Goldfinch, chronicling a young boy's survival after an art museum bombing in Manhattan.

title: John O'Keefe May-Britt Moser and Edvard Moser Awarded Nobel Prize for Discovering Brain GPS System
description: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discovering place cells and grid cells constituting the brain's internal positioning system.

title: Anthony Doerr Wins Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for World War Two Novel All the Light We Cannot See
description: Anthony Doerr was awarded the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for his bestselling novel interweaving the lives of a blind French girl and German orphan boy.

title: Colson Whitehead Wins Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for The Underground Railroad
description: Colson Whitehead won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for reimagining the Underground Railroad as a literal subterranean locomotive network.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Inaugurates Bhupen Hazarika Setu Longest River Bridge in India
description: Prime Minister Modi opened the 9.15-kilometer Dhola-Sadiya Bridge connecting Assam and Arunachal Pradesh over the Lohit River.

title: Rima Das Releases Assamese Indie Masterpiece Village Rockstars Premiering at Toronto International Film Festival
description: Rima Das's self-funded indie film Village Rockstars won four National Film Awards including Best Feature Film and was India's Oscar entry.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Dedicates Revamped National Police Memorial in Chanakyapuri New Delhi
description: Prime Minister Modi unveiled the 30-foot black granite monolith at the National Police Memorial commemorating police personnel martyred on duty.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Dedicates National War Memorial at India Gate Complex in New Delhi
description: Prime Minister Modi dedicated the 40-acre National War Memorial featuring the eternal flame Amar Jawan Jyoti honoring over 26,000 fallen soldiers.

title: Richard Powers Wins Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for Sweeping Ecological Novel The Overstory
description: Richard Powers was awarded the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for The Overstory, weaving human lives with the preservation of ancient forests.

title: Colson Whitehead Wins Rare Second Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for The Nickel Boys
description: Colson Whitehead became only the fourth writer to win two fiction Pulitzers with his novel exposing Jim Crow reform school abuse in Florida.

title: Barbara Kingsolver and Hernan Diaz Share Historic Joint Pulitzer Prize for Fiction
description: The Pulitzer board awarded a rare joint prize to Barbara Kingsolver for Demon Copperhead and Hernan Diaz for Trust.

title: UNESCO Proclaims Kutiyattam Sanskrit Temple Theatre Masterpiece of Intangible Heritage
description: UNESCO proclaimed Kutiyattam, Kerala's ancient Sanskrit theatre tradition, among the first Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity.

title: UNESCO Proclaims Ancient Tradition of Vedic Chanting Masterpiece of Intangible Cultural Heritage
description: UNESCO recognized the oral chanting of the Vedas in India as a Masterpiece of Oral and Intangible Heritage for its flawless phonetic transmission across millennia.

title: Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for Groundbreaking Experiments on Graphene
description: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the Physics Nobel to Geim and Novoselov for isolating two-dimensional graphene using scotch tape.

title: Saul Perlmutter Brian Schmidt and Adam Riess Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for Accelerating Expansion of Universe
description: The Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for discovering the accelerating expansion of the universe through observations of distant Type Ia supernovae.

title: Serge Haroche and David Wineland Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for Measuring and Manipulation of Individual Quantum Systems
description: Haroche and Wineland won the Physics Nobel for groundbreaking experimental methods enabling measurement and control of single quantum particles.

title: Francois Englert and Peter Higgs Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for Theoretical Discovery of Higgs Mechanism
description: Englert and Higgs received the Nobel Prize after CERN's Large Hadron Collider confirmed the existence of the mass-giving Higgs boson.

title: Isamu Akasaki Hiroshi Amano and Shuji Nakamura Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for Invention of Blue Light-Emitting Diodes
description: Akasaki, Amano, and Nakamura won the Physics Nobel for inventing bright blue LEDs, enabling energy-saving white LED lighting across the world.

title: William Campbell Satoshi Omura and Tu Youyou Awarded Nobel Prize for Novel Therapies Against Parasitic Infections
description: Tu Youyou won for her discovery of artemisinin against malaria, alongside Campbell and Omura for avermectin against roundworm parasites.

title: Yoshinori Ohsumi Awarded Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for Discoveries of Mechanisms for Autophagy
description: Japanese cell biologist Yoshinori Ohsumi was awarded the solo Nobel Prize for elucidating the molecular mechanisms of cellular recycling and degradation.

title: Jeffrey Hall Michael Rosbash and Michael Young Awarded Nobel Prize for Molecular Mechanisms Controlling Circadian Rhythm
description: The Nobel Prize in Medicine was awarded for isolating the period gene and explaining how biological clocks sync with Earth's 24-hour cycle.

title: James Allison and Tasuku Honjo Awarded Nobel Prize for Cancer Therapy by Inhibition of Negative Immune Regulation
description: Allison and Honjo won the Nobel Prize for discovering immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting CTLA-4 and PD-1 to unleash T-cells against tumors.

title: William Kaelin Peter Ratcliffe and Gregg Semenza Awarded Nobel Prize for How Cells Sense Oxygen Availability
description: The Nobel Assembly honored Kaelin, Ratcliffe, and Semenza for identifying the molecular machinery that regulates gene activity in response to oxygen levels.

title: Harvey Alter Michael Houghton and Charles Rice Awarded Nobel Prize for Discovery of Hepatitis C Virus
description: Alter, Houghton, and Rice received the Nobel Prize in Medicine for identifying the blood-borne Hepatitis C virus, enabling life-saving diagnostic blood tests.

title: David Julius and Ardem Patapoutian Awarded Nobel Prize for Discoveries of Receptors for Temperature and Touch
description: Julius used capsaicin to identify heat sensor TRPV1 and Patapoutian identified pressure-sensitive ion channels Piezo1 and Piezo2.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Formally Inaugurates Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya at Teen Murti Estate
description: Prime Minister Modi inaugurated the museum dedicated to all 14 former Prime Ministers of India at the Teen Murti Complex on Ambedkar Jayanti.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Inaugurates Revamped Kartavya Path and Unveils Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Statue
description: Prime Minister Modi inaugurated the revamped Kartavya Path and unveiled the 28-foot jet-black granite statue of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose at India Gate.

title: Svante Paabo Awarded Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for Sequencing Neanderthal Genome and Human Evolution
description: Swedish geneticist Svante Paabo was awarded the Nobel Prize for pioneering paleogenomics, sequencing the Neanderthal genome, and discovering Denisovans.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Inaugurates World-Class Bharat Mandapam International Convention Centre in Pragati Maidan
description: Prime Minister Modi inaugurated the 123-acre Bharat Mandapam complex in New Delhi, hosting the landmark G20 Leaders' Summit.

title: Katalin Kariko and Drew Weissman Awarded Nobel Prize for Nucleoside Base Modifications Enabling mRNA Vaccines
description: Kariko and Weissman won the Nobel Prize for discover of base-modified mRNA, suppressing inflammatory responses and enabling rapid COVID-19 vaccines.

title: Victor Ambros and Gary Ruvkun Awarded Nobel Prize for Discovery of MicroRNA and Post-Transcriptional Gene Regulation
description: Ambros and Ruvkun were awarded the Nobel Prize for discovering microRNAs in C. elegans, uncovering an essential mechanism of cellular gene regulation.

title: UNESCO Inscribes Ramlila Traditional Performance of the Ramayana on Intangible Cultural Heritage List
description: UNESCO inscribed Ramlila performances staged during Dussehra across northern India on the Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage.

title: UNESCO Inscribes Kalbelia Folk Songs and Dances of Rajasthan on Intangible Cultural Heritage List
description: The nomadic serpent-charming community's energetic swirling dances and songs in Rajasthan received formal UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage status.

title: Dan Shechtman Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Solo Discovery of Quasicrystals
description: Israeli materials scientist Dan Shechtman was awarded the Chemistry Nobel for discovering non-repeating ordered atomic patterns called quasicrystals.

title: Robert Lefkowitz and Brian Kobilka Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Studies of G-Protein-Coupled Receptors
description: Lefkowitz and Kobilka received the Nobel Prize for deciphering how GPCR cell-surface receptors transmit hormones and neurotransmitters into cells.

title: UNESCO Inscribes Buddhist Chanting of Ladakh Recitations by Monks on Intangible Heritage List
description: UNESCO inscribed the sacred Buddhist monastic chanting in the monasteries and villages of Ladakh on the Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage.

title: UNESCO Inscribes Manipuri Sankirtana Ritual Singing Drumming and Dancing on Intangible Heritage List
description: The Vaishnava ritual art of Sankirtana performed in temples and domestic courtyards across Manipur was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Heritage list.

title: Eric Betzig Stefan Hell and William Moerner Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Development of Super-Resolved Fluorescence Microscopy
description: The Chemistry Nobel recognized Betzig, Hell, and Moerner for bypassing the optical diffraction limit to enable nanoscale imaging of live cells.

title: UNESCO Inscribes Traditional Brass and Copper Craft of Thatheras of Jandiala Guru on Intangible List
description: The Thatheras of Punjab practicing hereditary brass and copper vessel making in Amritsar district earned inscription on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

title: Takaaki Kajita and Arthur McDonald Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for Discovery of Neutrino Oscillations
description: The Super-Kamiokande and SNO experiments demonstrated that neutrinos switch identities, proving that neutrinos possess non-zero mass.

title: Tomas Lindahl Paul Modrich and Aziz Sancar Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Mechanistic Studies of DNA Repair
description: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded for mapping how cells repair damaged DNA at the molecular level to safeguard genetic integrity.

title: David Thouless Duncan Haldane and Michael Kosterlitz Awarded Nobel Prize for Topological Phase Transitions in Matter
description: The Physics Nobel was awarded for utilizing topological concepts in physics to reveal exotic states of matter such as superconductors and superfluids.

title: Jean-Pierre Sauvage Fraser Stoddart and Bernard Feringa Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Design and Synthesis of Molecular Machines
description: Sauvage, Stoddart, and Feringa won the Nobel Prize for synthesizing controllable molecular nanomotors, catenanes, and rotaxanes.

title: Rainer Weiss Barry Barish and Kip Thorne Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for Decisive Contributions to LIGO Detector
description: Weiss, Barish, and Thorne won the Nobel Prize in Physics following LIGO's historic first direct detection of gravitational waves from colliding black holes.

title: Jacques Dubochet Joachim Frank and Richard Henderson Awarded Nobel Prize for Developing Cryo-Electron Microscopy
description: Dubochet, Frank, and Henderson were awarded the Chemistry Nobel for high-resolution 3D structure determination of biomolecules in solution.

title: Arthur Ashkin Gerard Mourou and Donna Strickland Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for Groundbreaking Inventions in Laser Physics
description: Ashkin won for optical tweezers, while Mourou and Strickland won for generating high-intensity ultra-short optical pulses with chirped pulse amplification.

title: James Peebles Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz Awarded Nobel Prize for Discoveries in Physical Cosmology and Exoplanet Orbiting Sun-Like Star
description: Peebles won for theoretical framework of modern cosmology, while Mayor and Queloz won for discovering the first exoplanet 51 Pegasi b in 1995.

title: Roger Penrose Reinhard Genzel and Andrea Ghez Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for Black Hole Formation and Supermassive Centre of Milky Way
description: Penrose won for proving black hole formation is a robust prediction of general relativity, and Genzel and Ghez won for discovering Sagittarius A*.

title: Alain Aspect John Clauser and Anton Zeilinger Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for Experiments with Entangled Photons and Quantum Information Science
description: Aspect, Clauser, and Zeilinger won for pioneering experiments demonstrating quantum entanglement and violation of Bell inequalities.

title: Pierre Agostini Ferenc Krausz and Anne L'Huillier Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for Experimental Methods Generating Attosecond Pulses of Light
description: The Royal Swedish Academy awarded the Physics Nobel for creating light pulses measured in attoseconds to track electrons inside atoms and molecules.

title: John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for Foundational Inventions Enabling Machine Learning with Artificial Neural Networks
description: John Hopfield created associative memory networks and Geoffrey Hinton invented the Boltzmann machine, laying the foundations for modern artificial intelligence.

title: PH Newby Awarded Inaugural Booker Prize for Novel Something to Answer For
description: English novelist P.H. Newby won the inaugural Booker-McConnell Prize for his novel set in Port Said during the Suez Crisis.

title: Bernice Rubens Becomes First Woman to Win Booker Prize for The Elected Member
description: Welsh author Bernice Rubens made literary history as the first female recipient of the Booker Prize for her psychological novel.

title: VS Naipaul Awarded Booker Prize for Short Fiction Collection In a Free State
description: Trinidadian-British writer V.S. Naipaul won the Booker Prize for his linked fiction collection exploring exile and post-colonial displacement.

title: John Berger Wins Booker Prize for Experimental Novel G Announcing Donation to Black Panthers
description: Art critic and novelist John Berger won the Booker Prize for G., using his acceptance speech to pledge half his prize money to the Black Panther Party.

title: JG Farrell Wins Booker Prize for Historical Masterpiece The Siege of Krishnapur
description: J.G. Farrell was awarded the Booker Prize for his Empire Trilogy novel depicting the 1857 Indian rebellion from a British residency.

title: Nadine Gordimer and Stanley Middleton Share Booker Prize in Rare Joint Award
description: South African author Nadine Gordimer for The Conservationist shared the Booker Prize with English novelist Stanley Middleton for Holiday.

title: Ruth Prawer Jhabvala Wins Booker Prize for Anglo-Indian Drama Heat and Dust
description: German-born British novelist Ruth Prawer Jhabvala won the Booker Prize for Heat and Dust, later writing the Academy Award-winning screenplay.

title: David Storey Awarded Booker Prize for Autobiographical Yorkshire Novel Saville
description: Yorkshire dramatist and novelist David Storey won the Booker Prize for his coming-of-age mining community novel Saville.

title: Jyoti Basu Sworn in as Chief Minister of West Bengal Heading Left Front Government
description: Marxist veteran Jyoti Basu took the oath of office in Calcutta, initiating a record 23-year uninterrupted tenure as Chief Minister of West Bengal.

title: MG Ramachandran Sworn in as Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Leading AIADMK to Victory
description: Matinee idol M.G. Ramachandran was sworn in as Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu at Raj Bhavan in Madras, beginning a decade of AIADMK dominance.

title: NT Rama Rao Sworn in as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Leading Telugu Desam Party
description: Cinema icon N.T. Rama Rao took oath before massive crowds at Lal Bahadur Shastri Stadium in Hyderabad, nine months after founding the Telugu Desam Party.

title: UNESCO Inscribes Kumbh Mela World's Largest Peaceful Congregation on Intangible Cultural Heritage List
description: The sacred pilgrimage of Kumbh Mela held rotationally in Haridwar, Prayagraj, Nashik, and Ujjain was inscribed by UNESCO on its Intangible Heritage list.

title: Frances Arnold George Smith and Gregory Winter Awarded Nobel Prize for Directed Evolution of Enzymes and Phage Display
description: Frances Arnold conducted the first directed evolution of enzymes, while Smith and Winter developed phage display to evolve novel therapeutic proteins.

title: John B Goodenough Stanley Whittingham and Akira Yoshino Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Development of Lithium-Ion Batteries
description: Ninety-seven-year-old John Goodenough and colleagues were awarded the Nobel Prize for developing lightweight, rechargeable lithium-ion battery technology.

title: Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Development of CRISPR-Cas9 Genome Editing
description: Charpentier and Doudna made history as the first all-female duo to win a science Nobel for discovering the CRISPR-Cas9 genetic scissors.

title: Benjamin List and David MacMillan Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Development of Asymmetric Organocatalysis
description: List and MacMillan received the Chemistry Nobel for developing precise small organic molecules as environmentally friendly catalysts for chemical synthesis.

title: Carolyn Bertozzi Morten Meldal and Barry Sharpless Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Development of Click Chemistry and Bioorthogonal Reactions
description: Sharpless won his second Nobel Prize, sharing with Meldal for modular click reactions and Bertozzi for mapping living cells via bioorthogonal chemistry.

title: Moungi Bawendi Louis Brus and Alexei Ekimov Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Discovery and Synthesis of Quantum Dots
description: The Royal Swedish Academy awarded the Chemistry Nobel for developing semiconductor nanocrystals called quantum dots that illuminate LED displays.

title: UNESCO Inscribes Garba Folk Dance of Gujarat on Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage
description: The devotional circular dance of Garba celebrated during the Navratri festival in Gujarat was inscribed by UNESCO at its 18th session in Botswana.

title: David Baker Demis Hassabis and John Jumper Awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Computational Protein Design and Structure Prediction
description: David Baker won for designing entirely new proteins, while Hassabis and Jumper of Google DeepMind won for AlphaFold AI predicting 200 million protein structures.

title: Paul Scott Posthumously Honored as Staying On Wins Booker Prize
description: Paul Scott's poignant coda to the Raj Quartet, Staying On, won the Booker Prize portraying an elderly British couple remaining in India after independence.

title: Iris Murdoch Wins Booker Prize for The Sea The Sea on Her Seventh Nomination
description: Philosopher and novelist Iris Murdoch captured the Booker Prize for The Sea, The Sea exploring obsession and vanity through a retired theatre director.

title: Penelope Fitzgerald Wins Booker Prize for Houseboat Novel Offshore
description: Penelope Fitzgerald won the Booker Prize for Offshore, depicting a bohemian community of barge-dwellers living on the River Thames at Battersea.

title: William Golding Wins Booker Prize for Sea Voyage Novel Rites of Passage
description: Lord of the Flies author William Golding was awarded the Booker Prize for Rites of Passage, the opening volume of his To the Ends of the Earth trilogy.

title: Thomas Keneally Wins Booker Prize for Holocaust Epic Schindler's Ark
description: Australian author Thomas Keneally won the Booker Prize for his biographical novel about Oskar Schindler, later adapted into Schindler's List.

title: JM Coetzee Wins Booker Prize for South African Allegory Life and Times of Michael K
description: South African novelist J.M. Coetzee won the Booker Prize for Life & Times of Michael K, chronicling a gardener's journey during a fictional civil war.

title: Anita Brookner Wins Booker Prize for Solitary Romance Hotel du Lac
description: Art historian Anita Brookner won the Booker Prize for Hotel du Lac, defeating favorite J.G. Ballard's Empire of the Sun.

title: Keri Hulme Wins Booker Prize for The Bone People First New Zealander Honored
description: Maori writer Keri Hulme won the Booker Prize for her debut novel The Bone People, which had originally been rejected by multiple publishers.

title: Kingsley Amis Wins Booker Prize for Acerbic Comedy The Old Devils
description: English satirist Kingsley Amis won the Booker Prize for The Old Devils, chronicling the reunion of lifelong friends in suburban Wales.

title: Penelope Lively Wins Booker Prize for Memory and History Novel Moon Tiger
description: Penelope Lively was awarded the Booker Prize for Moon Tiger, narrating the life of a dying historian from a hospital bed in kaleidoscopic flashbacks.

title: Peter Carey Wins First Booker Prize for Australian Picaresque Oscar and Lucinda
description: Australian novelist Peter Carey won the Booker Prize for Oscar and Lucinda, depicting a glass church transported across the Australian outback.

title: Kazuo Ishiguro Wins Booker Prize for Aristocratic Butler Portrait The Remains of the Day
description: Thirty-four-year-old Kazuo Ishiguro was awarded the Booker Prize for his sublime portrait of repression and English decorum in post-war Britain.

title: Mulayam Singh Yadav Sworn in for First Time as Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh
description: Janata Dal leader Mulayam Singh Yadav took the oath of office as Chief Minister of India's most populous state, Uttar Pradesh, in Lucknow.

title: Lalu Prasad Yadav Sworn in as Chief Minister of Bihar Ushering in Social Justice Era
description: Janata Dal leader Lalu Prasad Yadav took the oath of office in Patna, beginning a transformative political era focused on backward caste empowerment.

title: AS Byatt Wins Booker Prize for Victorian Romance Literary Mystery Possession
description: A.S. Byatt won the Booker Prize for Possession: A Romance, interweaving contemporary academic sleuths with two fictional Victorian poets.

title: Jayalalithaa Sworn in as First Woman Elected Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu
description: AIADMK general secretary J. Jayalalithaa was sworn in as Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu following a landslide victory in the state assembly election.

title: Ben Okri Wins Booker Prize for The Famished Road First Nigerian Author Honored
description: Thirty-two-year-old Ben Okri won the Booker Prize for his magical realist masterpiece The Famished Road, narrated by spirit child Azaro.

title: Michael Ondaatje and Barry Unsworth Share Booker Prize in Contentious Decision
description: Sri Lankan-Canadian Michael Ondaatje for The English Patient shared the Booker with Barry Unsworth for slave-trade historical drama Sacred Hunger.

title: Mayawati Sworn in as First Dalit Woman Chief Minister of Any Indian State in Uttar Pradesh
description: Bahujan Samaj Party leader Mayawati was sworn in as Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh at age 39, creating history as India's first Dalit woman chief minister.

title: Naveen Patnaik Sworn in for First Term as Chief Minister of Odisha
description: Biju Janata Dal president Naveen Patnaik was sworn in as Chief Minister of Odisha in Bhubaneswar, commencing a historic 24-year tenure.

title: Roddy Doyle Wins Booker Prize for Ten-Year-Old Voice in Paddy Clarke Ha Ha Ha
description: Irish author Roddy Doyle won the Booker Prize for Paddy Clarke Ha Ha Ha, capturing working-class Dublin boyhood amid parental divorce.

title: James Kelman Wins Booker Prize for Working-Class Glaswegian Monologue How Late It Was How Late
description: Scottish writer James Kelman won the Booker Prize for his stream-of-consciousness novel written in phonetic Glasgow dialect.

title: Pat Barker Wins Booker Prize for World War One Regeneration Finale The Ghost Road
description: Pat Barker concluded her celebrated Regeneration Trilogy by winning the Booker Prize for The Ghost Road examining shell-shocked soldiers.

title: Graham Swift Wins Booker Prize for Pub Camaraderie Novel Last Orders
description: Graham Swift won the Booker Prize for Last Orders, narrating four Bermondsey friends journeying to scatter their butcher friend's ashes at Margate pier.

title: Ian McEwan Wins Booker Prize for Satirical Moral Fable Amsterdam
description: English author Ian McEwan won the Booker Prize for Amsterdam, exploring a euthanasia pact between two prominent cultural figures.

title: Sheila Dikshit Sworn in as Chief Minister of Delhi Leading Congress to Assembly Victory
description: Sheila Dikshit was sworn in as Chief Minister of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, beginning a 15-year transformation of Delhi's infrastructure.

title: JM Coetzee Becomes First Double Booker Prize Winner for Post-Apartheid Masterpiece Disgrace
description: J.M. Coetzee made literary history by becoming the first author to win the Booker twice, recognized for his incisive post-apartheid novel Disgrace.

title: Margaret Atwood Wins Booker Prize for Historical Mystery The Blind Assassin
description: Canadian author Margaret Atwood won the Booker Prize on her fourth nomination for her layered historical and pulp sci-fi novel The Blind Assassin.

title: Narendra Modi Sworn in for First Time as Chief Minister of Gujarat at Raj Bhavan Gandhinagar
description: Narendra Modi took the oath of office as Chief Minister of Gujarat administered by Governor Sundar Singh Bhandari, succeeding Keshubhai Patel.

title: Peter Carey Wins Rare Second Booker Prize for True History of the Kelly Gang
description: Peter Carey joined J.M. Coetzee as the second two-time Booker recipient for his vernacular epistolary epic of Australian bushranger Ned Kelly.

title: Yann Martel Wins Booker Prize for Philosophical Castaway Tale Life of Pi
description: Canadian author Yann Martel won the Booker Prize for Life of Pi, narrating a teenage boy surviving 227 days on a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger.

title: DBC Pierre Wins Booker Prize for Satirical Texas School Shooting Debut Vernon God Little
description: Australian-born author DBC Pierre (Peter Finlay) won the Booker Prize for his darkly satirical debut novel set in the aftermath of a Texas high school massacre.

title: Alan Hollinghurst Wins Booker Prize for Thatcher-Era Homosexual Masterpiece The Line of Beauty
description: Alan Hollinghurst won the Booker Prize for The Line of Beauty, examining class, aestheticism, and the AIDS crisis in 1980s London.

title: John Banville Wins Booker Prize for Memory-Laden Grief Novel The Sea
description: Irish stylist John Banville captured the Booker Prize for The Sea, defeating Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go in a close jury vote.

title: Justice KG Balakrishnan Sworn in as First Dalit Chief Justice of India in Rashtrapati Bhavan
description: Justice K.G. Balakrishnan was sworn in by President A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, becoming the first person from the Dalit community to serve as Chief Justice of India.

title: Anne Enright Wins Booker Prize for Raw Irish Family Elegy The Gathering
description: Dublin writer Anne Enright won the Booker Prize for The Gathering, exploring family trauma and grief following a brother's suicide in the sea.

title: Hilary Mantel Wins Booker Prize for Thomas Cromwell Historical Epic Wolf Hall
description: Hilary Mantel was awarded the Booker Prize for Wolf Hall, transforming Tudor historical fiction through the pragmatic lens of Thomas Cromwell.

title: Howard Jacobson Wins Booker Prize for Jewish Comedy The Finkler Question
description: British satirist Howard Jacobson won the Booker Prize for The Finkler Question, the first comic novel to win the prize in over twenty years.

title: Arvind Kejriwal Sworn in as Chief Minister of Delhi at Historic Ramlila Maidan Ceremony
description: Aam Aadmi Party convenor Arvind Kejriwal took oath as Delhi Chief Minister before tens of thousands of citizens at Ramlila Maidan.

title: Justice JS Khehar Sworn in as First Sikh Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India
description: Justice Jagdish Singh Khehar was sworn in by President Pranab Mukherjee as the 44th Chief Justice of India, the first from the Sikh community.

title: University of Delhi Formally Established by Central Legislative Assembly Act
description: The University of Delhi began operations with three founding colleges (St. Stephen's, Hindu, and Ramjas) and two faculties in Old Delhi.

title: Parliament Enacts University of Hyderabad Act Establishing Premier Central University in Telangana
description: The University of Hyderabad was established under the Six-Point Formula on Gandhi Jayanti, becoming an Institute of Eminence in higher research.

title: Dhirubhai Ambani's Reliance Textile Industries Completes Historic Public IPO on Bombay Stock Exchange
description: Reliance Textile Industries issued equity shares to 58,000 retail investors, pioneering the equity investment culture among middle-class Indian families.

title: Dead Poets Society Wins BAFTA Award for Best Film at 43rd British Academy Ceremony
description: Peter Weir's prep school drama Dead Poets Society starring Robin Williams won the BAFTA for Best Film in London.

title: Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas Dominates 44th British Academy Film Awards Winning Best Film
description: Goodfellas won five BAFTAs including Best Film and Best Director for Martin Scorsese at the Grosvenor House Hotel in London.

title: Julian Barnes Wins Booker Prize for Novella The Sense of an Ending
description: Julian Barnes won the Booker Prize on his fourth nomination for his concise meditation on memory, aging, and remorse in The Sense of an Ending.

title: Hilary Mantel Makes History Winning Second Booker Prize for Bring Up the Bodies
description: Hilary Mantel became the first woman and first British author to win the Booker Prize twice, recognized for her Cromwell sequel Bring Up the Bodies.

title: Twenty-Eight-Year-Old Eleanor Catton Becomes Youngest Booker Winner in History for The Luminaries
description: New Zealand author Eleanor Catton won the Booker Prize for her 832-page astrological Victorian murder mystery set during the Hokitika Gold Rush.

title: Richard Flanagan Wins Booker Prize for Burma Railway War Novel The Narrow Road to the Deep North
description: Tasmanian author Richard Flanagan won the Booker Prize for his harrowing novel inspired by his father's survival as a prisoner of war on the Death Railway.

title: Marlon James Becomes First Jamaican Author to Win Booker Prize for A Brief History of Seven Killings
description: Marlon James won the Booker Prize for his 680-page polyphonic epic exploring the 1976 assassination attempt on Bob Marley and Jamaica's gang wars.

title: Paul Beatty Becomes First American Author to Win Booker Prize for Satire The Sellout
description: Paul Beatty made Booker history as the first US author to win the prize following the opening of eligibility, recognized for his biting racial satire.

title: George Saunders Wins Booker Prize for Polyphonic Ghost Masterpiece Lincoln in the Bardo
description: American short-story master George Saunders won the Booker Prize for his debut novel depicting Abraham Lincoln visiting the crypt of his deceased son Willie.

title: Justice Ranjan Gogoi Sworn in as First Chief Justice of India from Northeast Region
description: Justice Ranjan Gogoi of Assam was sworn in as the 46th Chief Justice of India by President Ram Nath Kovind at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

title: Anna Burns Wins Booker Prize for Belfast Troubles Stream-of-Consciousness Novel Milkman
description: Northern Irish author Anna Burns won the Booker Prize for Milkman, chronicling a young woman navigating surveillance and paramilitarism in 1970s Belfast.

title: Margaret Atwood and Bernardine Evaristo Break Rules to Share Booker Prize in Joint Award
description: The Booker jury broke rule restrictions to award the prize jointly to Margaret Atwood for The Testaments and Bernardine Evaristo for Girl, Woman, Other.

title: Douglas Stuart Wins Booker Prize for Glasgow Working-Class Debut Shuggie Bain
description: Scottish-American fashion designer Douglas Stuart won the Booker Prize for Shuggie Bain, chronicling a queer boy's fierce love for his alcoholic mother.

title: Damon Galgut Wins Booker Prize for South African Family Saga The Promise
description: South African novelist Damon Galgut won the Booker Prize on his third nomination for The Promise, examining the unraveling of a white family across four funerals.

title: Shehan Karunatilaka Wins Booker Prize for Ghostly Colombo Satire The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida
description: Sri Lankan writer Shehan Karunatilaka was presented the Booker Prize by Queen Camilla for his afterlife murder mystery set during the Sri Lankan Civil War.

title: Justice DY Chandrachud Sworn in as 50th Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India
description: Justice D.Y. Chandrachud was sworn in by President Droupadi Murmu, becoming Chief Justice 44 years after his father Y.V. Chandrachud took the same post.

title: Paul Lynch Wins Booker Prize for Dystopian Dublin Nightmare Novel Prophet Song
description: Irish author Paul Lynch won the Booker Prize at Old Billingsgate in London for Prophet Song, portraying a mother fighting to protect her family in a totalitarian Ireland.

title: Alan Parker's Soul Drama The Commitments Wins Four BAFTAs Including Best Film
description: The Commitments chronicling a young Dublin soul band won four major BAFTA trophies including Best Film and Best Director.

title: Merchant Ivory Period Drama Howards End Wins BAFTA for Best Film at 46th Ceremony
description: James Ivory's E.M. Forster adaptation Howards End won the BAFTA for Best Film and Best Actress for Emma Thompson.

title: Delhi High Court Formally Established with Four Judges at South End Road
description: The Delhi High Court commenced functions with Chief Justice K.S. Hegde and three judges, carved out from the High Court of Punjab.

title: Forty-Six-Year-Old Jack Nicklaus Shoots Historic Final-Round 65 to Win Sixth Masters at Augusta
description: Jack Nicklaus stormed the back nine with an eagle and four birdies at Augusta National to become the oldest Masters champion at age 46.

title: Nick Faldo Defeats Raymond Floyd in Sudden-Death Playoff to Retain Green Jacket at 1990 Masters
description: English golfer Nick Faldo parred the second playoff hole on the eleventh green to become only the second golfer to successfully defend the Masters.

title: Fred Couples Birdies Final Holes as Ball Clings to Bank of Twelfth Hole to Win 1992 Masters
description: Fred Couples's tee shot miraculously held on the grass above Rae's Creek at the par-3 twelfth, leading to his two-shot triumph at Augusta.

title: Bernhard Langer Dominates Final Round at Augusta National to Win Second Masters Green Jacket
description: German golfer Bernhard Langer posted an 11-under-par total to win his second Masters title on Easter Sunday by four strokes.

title: Ben Crenshaw Wins Emotional 1995 Masters Days After Serving as Pallbearer for Harvey Penick
description: Ben Crenshaw broke down in tears on the 18th green after winning his second Masters title, dedicating his victory to his late mentor Harvey Penick.

title: Jia Zhangke's Three Gorges Drama Still Life Wins Golden Lion at 63rd Venice Film Festival
description: Jia Zhangke's surprise addition Still Life documenting the human cost of the Three Gorges Dam project won the Golden Lion.

title: Ang Lee Wins Second Consecutive Golden Lion for Espionage Thriller Lust Caution in Venice
description: Ang Lee joined an elite rank of multi-awardees by capturing his second Golden Lion for his wartime Shanghai espionage drama Lust, Caution.

title: Darren Aronofsky's Wrestling Drama The Wrestler Starring Mickey Rourke Wins Golden Lion in Venice
description: Darren Aronofsky's gritty drama The Wrestler starring Mickey Rourke won the Golden Lion at the 65th Venice International Film Festival.

title: Sofia Coppola's Chateau Marmont Portrait Somewhere Wins Golden Lion at 67th Venice Film Festival
description: Quentin Tarantino's jury awarded the Golden Lion to Sofia Coppola's minimalist Hollywood study Somewhere starring Stephen Dorff.

title: Kim Ki-duk's Brutal Debt-Collector Tragedy Pieta Wins Golden Lion for South Korea in Venice
description: Kim Ki-duk's moral parable Pieta became the first South Korean film to win the top prize at any of the big three European film festivals.

title: High Court of Meghalaya Formally Established in Shillong After Constitutional Amendment
description: Chief Justice of India Altamas Kabir inaugurated the High Court of Meghalaya in Shillong with Justice T. Meena Kumari taking oath as Chief Justice.

title: High Court of Tripura Formally Inaugurated at Capital Agartala
description: Chief Justice Altamas Kabir inaugurated the High Court of Tripura at Agartala with Justice Deepak Gupta taking the oath as its first Chief Justice.

title: High Court of Manipur Formally Inaugurated at Imphal Complex
description: Chief Justice of India Altamas Kabir inaugurated the High Court of Manipur with Justice Abhay Manohar Sapre sworn in as its inaugural Chief Justice.

title: Roy Andersson's Absurdist Tableau A Pigeon Sat on a Branch Reflecting on Existence Wins Golden Lion
description: Swedish director Roy Andersson won the Golden Lion on the Lido for the final chapter of his Living trilogy composed of meticulous static comic vignettes.

title: Todd Phillips's Psychological Comic Adaptation Joker Wins Prestigious Golden Lion in Venice
description: Todd Phillips's dark character study Joker starring Joaquin Phoenix won the Golden Lion, becoming the first comic book-based film honored.

title: Laura Poitras's Nan Goldin Documentary All the Beauty and the Bloodshed Wins Golden Lion in Venice
description: Laura Poitras's film chronicling photographer Nan Goldin's crusade against the Sackler opioid dynasty became only the second documentary to win the Golden Lion.

title: Yorgos Lanthimos's Gothic Feminist Fantasy Poor Things Wins Golden Lion at 80th Venice Film Festival
description: Yorgos Lanthimos's surreal Victorian Frankenstein reimagining Poor Things starring Emma Stone captured the Golden Lion on the Lido.

title: Pedro Almodovar's Euthanasia Drama The Room Next Door Wins Golden Lion at 81st Venice Film Festival
description: Spanish master Pedro Almodóvar won his first Golden Lion for his English-language debut The Room Next Door starring Julianne Moore and Tilda Swinton.

title: Malayalam Poet G Sankara Kurup Conferred Inaugural Jnanpith Award for Odakkuzhal in Delhi
description: Mahakavi G. Sankara Kurup received the first Jnanpith Award for his poetry collection Odakkuzhal (The Bamboo Flute) presented in Vigyan Bhavan.

title: Kannada National Poet Kuvempu Conferred Jnanpith Award for Sri Ramayana Darshanam
description: K.V. Puttappa (Kuvempu) was presented the prestigious Jnanpith Award for his epic Kannada poem Sri Ramayana Darshanam composed in Mahachhandas.

title: Urdu Poet Firaq Gorakhpuri Conferred Jnanpith Award for Poetry Collection Gul-e-Naghma
description: Raghupati Sahay, known as Firaq Gorakhpuri, was awarded the Jnanpith Award in New Delhi for his acclaimed Urdu poetry collection Gul-e-Naghma.

title: Viswanatha Satyanarayana Conferred Jnanpith Award for Telugu Magnum Opus Srimad Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu
description: Telugu poet and scholar Kavisamrat Viswanatha Satyanarayana was presented the Jnanpith Award for his monumental verse work in classical Telugu.

title: Bob Tway Chips in from Bunker on 72nd Hole to Win 1986 PGA Championship
description: Bob Tway holed a 25-foot greenside bunker shot on the 72nd hole at Inverness Club to defeat Greg Norman for his solitary major.

title: John Daly Wins 1991 PGA Championship at Crooked Stick as Ninth Alternate
description: Long-driving rookie John Daly drove through the night after entering as ninth alternate, winning the PGA Championship by three shots.

title: Paul Azinger Defeats Greg Norman in Sudden-Death Playoff to Win 1993 PGA Championship
description: Paul Azinger parred the second playoff hole at Inverness Club to defeat Greg Norman and claim his sole major championship.

title: Nick Faldo Capitalizes on Greg Norman Six-Shot Collapse to Win Third Masters Tournament
description: Nick Faldo shot a clinical final-round 67 as overnight leader Greg Norman stumbled to a 78 in one of golf's most dramatic final-round turnarounds.

title: Vijay Singh Wins Maiden Masters Green Jacket at Augusta National by Three Strokes
description: Fijian golfer Vijay Singh carded a steady final-round 69 to hold off Ernie Els and claim his first Masters title at Augusta National.

title: Mike Weir Becomes First Canadian and First Left-Hander to Win Masters in Playoff at Augusta
description: Mike Weir defeated Len Mattiace on the first extra hole to become Canada's first male major champion and the first left-handed Masters winner.

title: Phil Mickelson Birdies Final Hole Leaping for Joy to Win Maiden Major at 2004 Masters
description: Phil Mickelson rolled in an 18-foot birdie putt on the 72nd green at Augusta National to claim his long-awaited first major championship.

title: Angel Cabrera Wins 2009 Masters in Three-Way Playoff Becoming First South American Green Jacket Winner
description: Argentine power-hitter Angel Cabrera defeated Kenny Perry and Chad Campbell in a playoff to win the Masters at Augusta.

title: Charl Schwartzel Birdies Final Four Holes on 50th Anniversary of Gary Player Win to Capture Masters
description: South African Charl Schwartzel closed with four consecutive birdies to claim the Green Jacket by two strokes on a chaotic final Sunday at Augusta.

title: Bubba Watson Hits Miraculous Hooking Wedge from Pine Straw to Win 2012 Masters in Playoff
description: Bubba Watson hooked a 52-degree wedge 40 yards out of the trees on the tenth hole to defeat Louis Oosthuizen on the second playoff hole.

title: Adam Scott Ends Australian Drought Winning 2013 Masters in Rainy Twilight Playoff
description: Adam Scott drained a 12-foot birdie putt on the second playoff hole against Angel Cabrera to deliver Australia's first Masters championship.

title: Twenty-One-Year-Old Jordan Spieth Ties Tiger Woods Scoring Record to Win 2015 Masters Wire-to-Wire
description: Jordan Spieth tied the 18-under 270 scoring record at Augusta National, becoming the second-youngest Masters champion in history.

title: Sergio Garcia Defeats Justin Rose in Playoff on Seve Ballesteros Sixtieth Birthday to Win Masters
description: On his 74th major championship appearance, Sergio Garcia birdied the first playoff hole at Augusta to win his maiden major on Seve's 60th birthday.

title: Separate Andhra Pradesh High Court Established at Temporary Complex in Amaravati
description: President Ram Nath Kovind issued the presidential notification establishing the separate High Court of Andhra Pradesh following the bifurcation of Hyderabad High Court.

title: Hideki Matsuyama Becomes First Japanese Male Major Champion Winning 2021 Masters at Augusta
description: Hideki Matsuyama held on to win the Masters by one stroke, creating historic sports celebrations across Japan as its first male major golf winner.

title: Jon Rahm Overcomes Brooks Koepka on Easter Sunday to Win 2023 Masters Green Jacket
description: Spanish golfer Jon Rahm shot a final-round 69 to overturn a four-shot deficit and win the Masters on the day his hero Seve Ballesteros would have turned 66.

title: Tamil Novelist Akhilan Conferred Jnanpith Award for Celebrated Novel Chittirappavai
description: P.V. Akilandam, popularly known as Akhilan, became the first Tamil writer to receive the Jnanpith Award for his sociological novel Chittirappavai.

title: Bengali Novelist Ashapoorna Devi Conferred Jnanpith Award for Prothom Protishruti
description: Ashapoorna Devi became the first woman to win the Jnanpith Award for her landmark feminist novel Prothom Protishruti depicting Satyabati's defiance.

title: Kannada Polymath K Shivaram Karanth Conferred Jnanpith Award for Mookajjiya Kanasugalu
description: Dr. Kota Shivaram Karanth received the Jnanpith Award for his existential masterpiece Mookajjiya Kanasugalu exploring metaphysics and ritual tradition.

title: Urdu Novelist Qurratulain Hyder Conferred Jnanpith Award for Aag Ka Darya
description: Qurratulain Hyder was presented the Jnanpith Award in New Delhi celebrating her monumental river-of-fire novel Aag Ka Darya spanning 2,500 years.

title: Kannada Scholar VK Gokak Conferred Jnanpith Award for Epic Bharatha Sindhu Rashmi
description: Prof. V.K. Gokak was awarded the Jnanpith Award for his 35,000-line modern Kannada epic poem Bharatha Sindhu Rashmi depicting the Vedic age.

title: Steve Elkington Defeats Colin Montgomerie in Playoff at Riviera to Win 1995 PGA Championship
description: Australian Steve Elkington rolled in a 20-foot birdie putt on the first extra hole at Riviera to defeat Colin Montgomerie.

title: Tiger Woods Holds Off Nineteen-Year-Old Sergio Garcia to Win 1999 PGA Championship at Medinah
description: Tiger Woods saved crucial pars on the closing holes at Medinah to hold off scissor-kicking Spanish teenager Sergio Garcia by one stroke.

title: Tiger Woods Outduels Bob May in Thrilling Three-Hole Playoff to Retain 2000 PGA Championship
description: Tiger Woods and Bob May both shot 18-under at Valhalla before Woods won the three-hole aggregate playoff for his third consecutive major.

title: David Toms Lays Up on 72nd Hole to Defeat Phil Mickelson for 2001 PGA Championship
description: David Toms famously laid up short of the water on the 72nd hole at Atlanta Athletic Club, pitching to 12 feet to save par and win.

title: Rich Beem Holds Off Charging Tiger Woods to Win 2002 PGA Championship at Hazeltine
description: Rich Beem birdied the 16th hole with a 35-foot eagle putt to hold off four consecutive birdies by Tiger Woods at Hazeltine National.

title: Shaun Micheel Hits Seven-Iron to Two Inches on Final Hole to Win 2003 PGA Championship
description: Shaun Micheel struck one of the greatest approach shots in major history on the 72nd hole at Oak Hill to seal his maiden major title.

title: Vijay Singh Wins Three-Hole Playoff at Whistling Straits to Capture 2004 PGA Championship
description: Vijay Singh defeated Justin Leonard and Chris DiMarco in a three-hole playoff on the Lake Michigan shoreline to claim his third major.

title: Phil Mickelson Flops Pitch Shot on Eighteenth to Win 2005 PGA Championship at Baltusrol
description: Phil Mickelson hit an iconic flop shot out of thick rough to two feet on the 72nd hole in a Monday finish at Baltusrol to win by one.

title: Tiger Woods Romps to Five-Shot Victory at Medinah to Win 2006 PGA Championship
description: Tiger Woods tied the tournament scoring record at 18-under-par at Medinah to capture his twelfth major championship by five strokes.

title: Tiger Woods Wins Twelfth Major at 2007 PGA Championship in Sweltering Southern Hills Heat
description: Tiger Woods held off Woody Austin in 100-degree Oklahoma temperatures at Southern Hills to claim his fourth PGA Championship title.

title: Padraig Harrington Wins Back-to-Back Majors with Victory at 2008 PGA Championship
description: Irishman Padraig Harrington made three late birdies at Oakland Hills to defeat Sergio Garcia and Ben Curtis for consecutive major titles.

title: YE Yang Stuns Tiger Woods at Hazeltine to Become First Asian Male Major Champion
description: South Korean Y.E. Yang became the first player to overcome a 54-hole major deficit against Tiger Woods, holing a hybrid from 210 yards on 18.

title: Martin Kaymer Defeats Bubba Watson in Playoff at Whistling Straits to Win 2010 PGA Championship
description: German golfer Martin Kaymer won a three-hole aggregate playoff after Dustin Johnson suffered a two-stroke grounding penalty on the 72nd hole.

title: Keegan Bradley Overcomes Triple Bogey to Win 2011 PGA Championship on Major Debut
description: Keegan Bradley defeated Jason Dufner in a three-hole playoff at Atlanta Athletic Club, becoming the third golfer to win a major on debut.

title: Rory McIlroy Wins 2012 PGA Championship by Record Eight Strokes on Ocean Course at Kiawah
description: Twenty-three-year-old Rory McIlroy shattered Jack Nicklaus's record margin of victory by winning by eight strokes in South Carolina.

title: Thomas Edison Files Historic Patent Application for Incandescent Carbon-Filament Electric Lamp
description: Thomas Edison filed US Patent Application No. 223,898 describing an electric lamp using a carbonized filament enclosed in an evacuated glass bulb.

title: Willis Carrier Completes Engineering Drawings for World's First Modern Mechanical Air Conditioner
description: Engineer Willis Carrier finalized drawings for a humidity-controlling air treatment system installed at the Sackett-Wilhelms printing plant in Brooklyn.

title: Mary Anderson Granted Patent for Window Cleaning Device Precursor to Mechanical Windshield Wipers
description: Mary Anderson received US Patent 743,801 for a manually operated lever-controlled rubber blade designed to clean trolley car windshields.

title: Leo Baekeland Files Landmark Patent for Bakelite First Fully Synthetic Thermosetting Plastic
description: Belgian chemist Leo Baekeland filed patent for Bakelite synthesized from phenol and formaldehyde, launching the modern synthetic plastics age.

title: Union Cultural Affairs Minister Humayun Kabir Formally Inaugurates IIT Madras in Chennai
description: IIT Madras was inaugurated in Chennai with academic, technical, and financial assistance from the government of West Germany.

title: Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati Established Under Historic Assam Accord
description: IIT Guwahati was founded on the northern banks of the Brahmaputra River, fulfilling a core infrastructural commitment of the 1985 Assam Accord.

title: Playwright Girish Karnad Conferred Prestigious 34th Jnanpith Award in New Delhi
description: Eminent playwright and filmmaker Girish Karnad was presented the Jnanpith Award celebrating plays like Yayati, Tughlaq, Hayavadana, and Nagamandala.

title: Jason Dufner Shoots Second-Round 63 on Way to Winning 2013 PGA Championship at Oak Hill
description: Jason Dufner redeemed his 2011 heartbreak by shooting 10-under-par at Oak Hill to defeat Jim Furyk by two shots for his first major.

title: Rory McIlroy Outlasts Phil Mickelson in Twilight at Valhalla to Win 2014 PGA Championship
description: Rory McIlroy rallied from three shots back on the back nine in near-darkness at Valhalla to claim his fourth major championship.

title: Jason Day Shoots Record Twenty-Under-Par to Win Maiden Major at 2015 PGA Championship
description: Australian Jason Day became the first player in major championship history to finish at 20-under-par, holding off Jordan Spieth at Whistling Straits.

title: Jimmy Walker Holds Off Jason Day in 36-Hole Sunday Marathon to Win 2016 PGA Championship
description: Jimmy Walker led wire-to-wire at Baltusrol, completing 36 holes on Sunday to hold off defending champion Jason Day by one shot.

title: Justin Thomas Wins 2017 PGA Championship at Quail Hollow for Maiden Major Triumph
description: Justin Thomas chipped in for birdie on the 13th hole and held on through the Green Mile at Quail Hollow to claim his first major title.

title: Brooks Koepka Holds Off Surging Tiger Woods to Win 100th PGA Championship at Bellerive
description: Brooks Koepka posted an aggregate 16-under 264 to hold off Tiger Woods's thrilling final-round 64 before 50,000 spectators in St. Louis.

title: Brooks Koepka Becomes First Player to Successfully Defend PGA Championship Wire-to-Wire
description: Brooks Koepka survived high winds and a Dustin Johnson challenge at Bethpage Black to become the first back-to-back PGA champion since Tiger Woods.

title: Collin Morikawa Drives Sixteenth Green for Eagle to Win 2020 PGA Championship at Harding Park
description: Collin Morikawa shot a bogey-free final-round 64 highlighted by a sensational 294-yard driver to seven feet on the 16th hole in San Francisco.

title: Assamese Poet Nilmani Phookan Conferred 56th Jnanpith Award at Guwahati Ceremony
description: Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma presented the 56th Jnanpith Award to legendary Assamese poet Nilmani Phookan at Rabindra Bhawan in Guwahati.

title: Justin Thomas Overcomes Seven-Shot Deficit to Win 2022 PGA Championship in Playoff
description: Justin Thomas tied the largest 54-hole comeback in PGA Championship history, defeating Will Zalatoris in a three-hole playoff at Southern Hills.

title: Brooks Koepka Wins Third PGA Championship and Fifth Career Major at Oak Hill Country Club
description: Brooks Koepka fired a final-round 67 at Oak Hill to become only the third player in the stroke-play era to win three PGA Championships.

title: Konkani Writer Damodar Mauzo Conferred 57th Jnanpith Award by Goa Governor at Raj Bhavan
description: Goa Governor P.S. Sreedharan Pillai conferred the 57th Jnanpith Award on acclaimed Konkani novelist Damodar Mauzo at Raj Bhavan in Dona Paula.

title: Xander Schauffele Birdies 72nd Hole to Win 2024 PGA Championship at Valhalla with Record 21-Under
description: Xander Schauffele sank a six-foot birdie putt on the 18th green to card an all-time major championship record 21-under-par total of 263.

title: Bell Telephone Laboratories Publicly Demonstrates Working Point-Contact Transistor in Manhattan
description: Bell Labs scientists held a press demonstration of the solid-state transistor radio amplifier, heralding the end of vacuum tubes.

title: Government of Bombay Formally Establishes Tadoba National Park in Chandrapur
description: Tadoba National Park was created in eastern Maharashtra, later becoming the core of the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve celebrated for dense tiger populations.

title: Indian Institute of Management Bangalore Formally Inaugurated by Union Education Minister
description: IIM Bangalore was inaugurated to focus on public sector management, agriculture, and rural development in southern India.

title: Government of Madhya Pradesh Formally Notifies Pench National Park in Seoni District
description: The teak and mixed forests of Pench that inspired Rudyard Kipling's The Jungle Book were protected as a National Park.

title: Government of India Establishes Indian Institute of Management Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh
description: IIM Lucknow was founded as the fourth national management institute, developing an expansive 200-acre green campus in Prabandh Nagar.

title: Thomason College of Civil Engineering Formally Re-Incorporated as IIT Roorkee
description: The University of Roorkee, originally founded in 1847 as India's oldest technical institution, was transformed into the nation's seventh IIT.

title: Ismail Kadare Awarded Inaugural Man Booker International Prize in Edinburgh
description: Albanian author Ismail Kadare received the inaugural Man Booker International Prize honoring his lifetime body of literary work.

title: Chinua Achebe Awarded the Man Booker International Prize in Oxford
description: Nigerian literary titan Chinua Achebe received the Man Booker International Prize for his lifelong contribution to world literature.

title: Alice Munro Wins the Man Booker International Prize in Dublin
description: Celebrated Canadian master of the short story Alice Munro was awarded the third biennial Man Booker International Prize.

title: Philip Roth Awarded the Man Booker International Prize at Sydney Writers' Festival
description: Renowned American author Philip Roth was named winner of the fourth Man Booker International Prize for his literary career.

title: Lydia Davis Wins the Man Booker International Prize at the Victoria and Albert Museum
description: American fiction writer and translator Lydia Davis won the Man Booker International Prize in London.

title: Laszlo Krasznahorkai Wins the Sixth Man Booker International Prize
description: Hungarian novelist Laszlo Krasznahorkai was awarded the final lifetime-achievement Man Booker International Prize.

title: Han Kang and Translator Deborah Smith Win Man Booker International Prize for The Vegetarian
description: South Korean author Han Kang and translator Deborah Smith won the revamped annual Man Booker International Prize for The Vegetarian.

title: David Grossman and Jessica Cohen Win International Booker Prize for A Horse Walks into a Bar
description: Israeli author David Grossman and translator Jessica Cohen won the Man Booker International Prize.

title: Olga Tokarczuk and Jennifer Croft Win Man Booker International Prize for Flights
description: Polish author Olga Tokarczuk and American translator Jennifer Croft won the Man Booker International Prize in London.

title: Jokha Alharthi and Marilyn Booth Win Man Booker International Prize for Celestial Bodies
description: Omani author Jokha Alharthi became the first Arabic-language writer to win the Man Booker International Prize.

title: Marieke Lucas Rijneveld and Michele Hutchison Win International Booker Prize for The Discomfort of Evening
description: Dutch author Marieke Lucas Rijneveld became the youngest winner of the International Booker Prize alongside translator Michele Hutchison.

title: David Diop and Anna Moschovakis Win International Booker Prize for At Night All Blood Is Black
description: French author David Diop and translator Anna Moschovakis won the International Booker Prize.

title: Georgi Gospodinov and Angela Rodel Win International Booker Prize for Time Shelter
description: Bulgarian writer Georgi Gospodinov and translator Angela Rodel won the International Booker Prize in London for Time Shelter.

title: Jenny Erpenbeck and Michael Hofmann Win International Booker Prize for Kairos
description: German novelist Jenny Erpenbeck and translator Michael Hofmann won the International Booker Prize for Kairos.

title: Joseph Lister Performs First Antiseptic Surgery Using Carbolic Acid Dressing in Glasgow
description: British surgeon Joseph Lister applied carbolic acid dressings to treat a compound fracture in Glasgow, founding modern antiseptic surgical practice.

title: Frederick Banting and Charles Best Isolate Working Insulin Secretions in Toronto Laboratory
description: Canadian researchers Frederick Banting and Charles Best isolated pancreatic islet extract at the University of Toronto, discovering insulin.

title: Kanha Reserve Forest Upgraded to Full-Fledged National Park by Madhya Pradesh Government
description: The Madhya Pradesh government enacted special legislation upgrading the Kanha wildlife sanctuary into a National Park, protecting the central Indian barasingha and sal forests.

title: Bandipur Sanctuary Formally Notified as National Park Under Project Tiger in Karnataka
description: The Karnataka government formally notified the Venugopala Wildlife Park as Bandipur National Park, establishing one of India's premier dry deciduous tiger reserves.

title: Don Quarrie Wins Olympic 200m Gold Medal in Montreal for Jamaica
description: Jamaican sprinting great Don Quarrie held off Millard Hampton in 20.22 seconds to claim gold in the men's 200 meters at Montreal Olympic Stadium.

title: Pietro Mennea Edges Allan Wells by Two Hundredths of a Second to Win 1980 Olympic 200m Gold
description: Italian world record holder Pietro Mennea staged a legendary surge from lane eight to snatch 200m Olympic gold in Moscow.

title: Government of Karnataka Formally Upgrades Nagarhole Sanctuary into National Park
description: Nagarhole (Rajiv Gandhi National Park) in Kodagu and Mysuru was elevated to National Park status, harboring key Asian elephant and tiger corridors.

title: Government of Odisha Formally Notifies Bhitarkanika National Park Protecting Mangrove Ecosystem
description: The estuarine crocodile and olive ridley sea turtle habitats of Bhitarkanika were formally declared a National Park in coastal Kendrapara.

title: Konstantinos Kenteris Wins Shock Olympic 200m Gold Medal for Greece in Sydney
description: Greek outsider Konstantinos Kenteris powered past Darren Campbell and Ato Boldon in 20.09 seconds to win Olympic gold at Stadium Australia.

title: Jeremy Wariner Leads American Sweep in Men's 400m at Athens Olympic Games
description: Twenty-year-old Jeremy Wariner ran 44.00 seconds to lead Otis Harris and Derrick Brew in an American medal sweep at the Athens Olympic Stadium.

title: Shawn Crawford Leads American Podium Sweep to Win Men's 200m Olympic Gold in Athens
description: Shawn Crawford clocked 19.79 seconds to defeat Bernard Williams and Justin Gatlin in an American sweep at the Athens Olympic Stadium.

title: Government of Tamil Nadu Notifies Anamalai Tiger Reserve in Southern Western Ghats
description: The Indira Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary in the Anamalai Hills was formally declared a Tiger Reserve to safeguard contiguous wet evergreen habitats.

title: Kirani James Wins Men's 400m Gold at London Olympic Games Earning Grenada's First Ever Medal
description: Nineteen-year-old world champion Kirani James clocked 43.94 seconds to deliver the Caribbean island nation of Grenada its first Olympic gold medal.

title: Usain Bolt Defeats Yohan Blake to Retain Olympic 200m Crown in London Declaring Himself a Legend
description: Usain Bolt led a Jamaican sweep with Yohan Blake and Warren Weir in 19.32 seconds, becoming the first man to defend both Olympic sprint titles.

title: Magnus Carlsen Defeats Viswanathan Anand in Chennai to Win First World Chess Championship
description: Norwegian prodigy Magnus Carlsen drew game ten in Chennai to defeat Viswanathan Anand 6.5-3.5, claiming the World Chess Championship.

title: Usain Bolt Completes Unprecedented Olympic Sprint Triple-Triple Winning 200m Gold in Rio
description: Usain Bolt ran 19.78 seconds in pouring rain at the Maracana to win his third consecutive Olympic 200m gold medal.

title: Magnus Carlsen Defeats Sergey Karjakin in Tiebreaks on 26th Birthday to Retain World Chess Championship
description: Magnus Carlsen defeated Sergey Karjakin 3-1 in rapid tiebreaks in New York City on his 26th birthday to retain his world title.

title: Magnus Carlsen Sweeps Fabiano Caruana in Rapid Tiebreaks to Retain World Chess Title in London
description: Magnus Carlsen swept Fabiano Caruana 3-0 in the rapid playoff in London after twelve consecutive classical draws to retain his title.

title: Magnus Carlsen Defeats Ian Nepomniachtchi in Dubai to Retain World Chess Championship Title
description: Magnus Carlsen clinched his fifth World Chess Championship title in Dubai by defeating challenger Ian Nepomniachtchi 7.5-3.5.

title: Ding Liren Defeats Ian Nepomniachtchi in Astana to Become China's First Men's World Chess Champion
description: Ding Liren won the fourth rapid tiebreak game in Astana to become the 17th undisputed World Chess Champion and first from China.

title: Ragnar Frisch and Jan Tinbergen Awarded Inaugural Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences
description: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the first Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences for dynamic models in econometrics.

title: Paul Samuelson Awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Paul Samuelson of MIT became the first American to win the Nobel Prize in Economics for developing static and dynamic economic theory.

title: Simon Kuznets Awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Simon Kuznets was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics for his empirical interpretation of economic growth and national income accounting.

title: John Hicks and Kenneth Arrow Awarded Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: John Hicks and Kenneth Arrow were honored for pioneering contributions to general economic equilibrium theory and welfare economics.

title: Wassily Leontief Awarded Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Russian-American economist Wassily Leontief won the Nobel Prize in Economics for inventing input-output analysis.

title: Gunnar Myrdal and Friedrich Hayek Awarded Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Gunnar Myrdal and Friedrich August von Hayek were awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics for money and economic fluctuations research.

title: Leonid Kantorovich and Tjalling Koopmans Awarded Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Soviet mathematician Leonid Kantorovich and Tjalling Koopmans won for contributions to the theory of optimum allocation of resources.

title: Milton Friedman Awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Milton Friedman of the University of Chicago won the Nobel Prize in Economics for monetary history and consumption analysis.

title: Bertil Ohlin and James Meade Awarded Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Bertil Ohlin and James Meade won the Nobel Prize in Economics for groundbreaking contributions to the theory of international trade.

title: Herbert A. Simon Awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Herbert A. Simon won the Nobel Prize in Economics for pioneering research into the decision-making process within economic organizations.

title: Theodore Schultz and Sir Arthur Lewis Awarded Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Theodore Schultz and Sir Arthur Lewis won the Nobel Prize in Economics for pioneering research into economic development.

title: Lawrence Klein Awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Lawrence Klein was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics for the creation of econometric models and analysis of economic fluctuations.

title: James Tobin Awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Yale economist James Tobin won the Nobel Prize in Economics for his analysis of financial markets and portfolio selection theory.

title: George Stigler Awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: George Stigler won the Nobel Prize in Economics for seminal studies of industrial structures, markets, and causes of public regulation.

title: Gerard Debreu Awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: French-born mathematician Gerard Debreu won the Nobel Prize in Economics for reformulating the theory of general equilibrium.

title: Ajanta Caves Formally Inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage List in Florence
description: The ancient rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments of Ajanta in Maharashtra were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

title: Ellora Caves Inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Site at World Heritage Committee Session
description: The monumental Kailash temple and 34 rock-cut monasteries at Ellora were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

title: Agra Fort Formally Inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage List
description: The historic 16th-century Mughal imperial fortress Agra Fort was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Taj Mahal Inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage List at World Heritage Committee in Italy
description: The iconic white marble mausoleum Taj Mahal in Agra was officially declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Sun Temple at Konark Inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage List in Buenos Aires
description: The 13th-century Surya Sun Temple carved in the shape of a monumental chariot in Konark was inscribed as a World Heritage Site.

title: Richard Stone Awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences
description: Sir Richard Stone was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics for fundamental contributions to the development of national accounts.

title: Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram Inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage List
description: The 7th-century Pallava coastal sanctuary monuments and rock reliefs at Mahabalipuram were designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Tiger Woods Goes Wire-to-Wire at Punishing Bethpage Black to Win Second US Open
