description: Vidarbha successfully defends its Irani Cup crown against Rest of India at Jamtha Stadium to complete consecutive domestic doubles.

title: Tao Geoghegan Hart Wins Autumn Giro d'Italia in Final Milan Time Trial
description: Tao Geoghegan Hart edges Jai Hindley in the final Milan time trial after entering the last stage tied on exact second in the rescheduled autumn Giro.

title: Egan Bernal Dominates Mountains and Gravel to Win 2021 Giro d'Italia
description: Egan Bernal attacks on the gravel roads of Campo Felice and the Giau Pass to ride into Milan and capture his second Grand Tour title.

title: INS Rajput Guided Missile Destroyer Commissioned into Indian Navy
description: Lead ship of the Rajput class, INS Rajput (D51), is commissioned at Poti, Georgia, becoming the first destroyer in the Indian Navy to be fitted with BrahMos missiles.

title: INS Rana Guided Missile Destroyer Commissioned at Poti
description: INS Rana (D52) is formally commissioned into the Eastern Fleet of the Indian Navy at Poti on the Black Sea coast.

title: INS Ranvir Guided Missile Destroyer Commissioned into Indian Navy
description: INS Ranvir (D54) joins the Western Fleet following its commissioning ceremony, bolstering India's naval surface warfare capabilities.

title: Sean Kelly Wins 1988 Vuelta a Espana with Devastating Final Time Trial
description: Irish legend Sean Kelly overhauls Anselmo Fuerte in the final 35km time trial into Collado Villalba to win his only Grand Tour title.

title: Pedro Delgado Wins Second Vuelta a Espana in Madrid
description: Perico Pedro Delgado holds off Fabio Parra and Ivan Ivanov to capture his second career Vuelta a Espana general classification.

title: Marco Giovannetti Breaks Away Early to Win 1990 Vuelta a Espana in Madrid
description: Italian rider Marco Giovannetti capitalizes on an early breakaway cushion to hold off Pedro Delgado and win the 1990 Vuelta.

title: Melcior Mauri Dominates Time Trials to Win 1991 Vuelta a Espana
description: ONCE rider Melcior Mauri upsets five-time Tour champion Miguel Indurain with blistering time trial speed to win the 1991 Vuelta in Madrid.

title: Tony Rominger Defends Vuelta a Espana Crown in Madrid Battle with Zulle
description: Tony Rominger fends off compatriot Alex Zulle in the high mountains to capture back-to-back Vuelta a Espana championships.

title: Laurent Jalabert Sweeps All Jerseys in Historic Autumn 1995 Vuelta
description: Laurent Jalabert wins the general classification, points, and mountains competitions in the first edition of the Vuelta moved to September.

title: Alex Zulle Dominates Time Trials to Win 1996 Vuelta a Espana in Madrid
description: ONCE rider Alex Zulle crushes Laurent Dufaux and Tony Rominger to capture his maiden Vuelta a Espana title by over six minutes.

title: Alex Zulle Defends Vuelta a Espana Title with Dominant Madrid Finish
description: Alex Zulle holds off Fernando Escartin and Laurent Dufaux to win back-to-back Vuelta a Espana championships in Madrid.

title: Abraham Olano Wins 1998 Vuelta a Espana in Dramatic Final Time Trial
description: Abraham Olano overhauls Jose Maria Jimenez in the final time trial in Fuenlabrada to claim his maiden Grand Tour title in Madrid.

title: Roberto Heras Conquers Angliru to Win Maiden 2000 Vuelta a Espana
description: Roberto Heras destroys his rivals on the monstrous Alto de l'Angliru to solo into Madrid and claim his first Vuelta a Espana crown.

title: Aitor Gonzalez Snatches 2002 Vuelta a Espana in Santiago Bernabeu Stadium
description: Aitor Gonzalez wins the final time trial finishing inside Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu Stadium to snatch the gold jersey from Roberto Heras.

title: Roberto Heras Attacks on Alto de Abantos to Steal 2003 Vuelta from Nozal
description: Roberto Heras overturns Isidro Nozal on the penultimate stage mountain time trial at Abantos to claim his second Vuelta a Espana in Madrid.

title: Roberto Heras Matches Tony Rominger with Third Vuelta a Espana Title
description: Roberto Heras dominates the mountains to defeat Santiago Perez and equal the all-time record of three Vuelta a Espana championships.

title: Alexander Vinokourov Attacks on Sierra de la Pandera to Win 2006 Vuelta
description: Alexander Vinokourov launches an aggressive campaign in the Andalusian mountains to defeat Alejandro Valverde and win in Madrid.

title: Denis Menchov Dominates All Disciplines to Win 2007 Vuelta a Espana
description: Denis Menchov wins the gold jersey, mountains classification, and combined jersey to secure a commanding victory in Madrid.

title: Rest of India Defeats Saurashtra by 8 Wickets to Win 2022 Irani Cup
description: Rest of India defeats Ranji champions Saurashtra by 8 wickets at the Saurashtra Cricket Association Stadium in Rajkot to claim the Irani Cup.

title: Rest of India Defeats Madhya Pradesh to Win 2023 Irani Cup in Gwalior
description: Yashasvi Jaiswal's twin centuries power Rest of India to a 238-run victory over Madhya Pradesh at Captain Roop Singh Stadium in Gwalior.

title: Bill Rodgers Smashes American Record to Win 1975 Boston Marathon
description: Bill Rodgers runs 2:09:55 in a bandana and mesh shirt to break the American marathon record and win his first Boston Marathon.

title: Jack Fultz Wins Infamous Run for the Hoses Boston Marathon in 100-Degree Heat
description: Jack Fultz survives brutal 100-degree Fahrenheit temperatures as spectators hose runners down along Commonwealth Avenue.

title: Jerome Drayton of Canada Battles Headwinds to Win 1977 Boston Marathon
description: Canadian marathoner Jerome Drayton holds off Viren and Rodgers into cold coastal headwinds to win the 81st Boston Marathon.

title: Bill Rodgers Wins Second Boston Marathon Crown on Boylston Street
description: Bill Rodgers runs 2:10:13 to capture his second Boston Marathon victory, kicking off a dominant three-year winning streak.

title: INS Ranvijay Guided Missile Destroyer Commissioned at Sevastopol
description: INS Ranvijay (D55), the fifth and final ship of the Rajput class, is commissioned into the Indian Navy at Sevastopol.

title: INS Talwar Stealth Frigate Commissioned into Indian Navy
description: INS Talwar (F40), lead ship of the advanced stealth guided missile frigates, is commissioned at Baltiysky Zavod in Saint Petersburg, Russia.

title: INS Trishul Guided Missile Frigate Commissioned at Saint Petersburg
description: INS Trishul (F43) is formally inducted into the Indian Navy following sea trials in the Baltic Sea, armed with Shtil air defence missiles.

title: INS Tabar Stealth Frigate Commissioned into Western Naval Command
description: INS Tabar (F44) is commissioned at Saint Petersburg, Russia, later going on to conduct anti-piracy patrols in the Gulf of Aden.

title: Alberto Contador Wins 2008 Vuelta to Complete Grand Tour Career Triple
description: Alberto Contador wins on the Angliru to claim the Vuelta a Espana in Madrid, becoming the fifth rider in cycling history to win all three Grand Tours.

title: Alejandro Valverde Wins Maiden Grand Tour at 2009 Vuelta a Espana in Madrid
description: Alejandro Valverde displays tactical maturity across three weeks to hold off Samuel Sanchez and Cadel Evans and win his first Grand Tour.

title: Vincenzo Nibali Claims Maiden Grand Tour at 2010 Vuelta a Espana in Madrid
description: Twenty-five-year-old Vincenzo Nibali fends off Ezequiel Mosquera in the Bola del Mundo fog to capture his first Grand Tour championship.

title: INS Teg Advanced Stealth Frigate Commissioned at Kaliningrad
description: INS Teg (F45), the first of the follow-on Talwar-class frigates armed with BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles, is commissioned in Kaliningrad, Russia.

title: Alberto Contador Launches Masterpiece Fuente De Ambush to Win 2012 Vuelta
description: Alberto Contador attacks 50 kilometers out on the stage to Fuente De to overturn Joaquim Rodriguez and win his second Vuelta title in Madrid.

title: Chris Horner Becomes Oldest Grand Tour Winner in History at 2013 Vuelta
description: Forty-one-year-old American Chris Horner conquers the Angliru to defeat Vincenzo Nibali and become the oldest Grand Tour winner ever.

title: Alberto Contador Defeats Chris Froome to Win Third Vuelta a Espana in Santiago
description: Returning from a broken leg suffered at the Tour, Alberto Contador defeats Chris Froome on Puerto de Ancares to win his third Vuelta in Santiago.

title: Chris Froome Completes Historic Tour-Vuelta Double in Madrid
description: Chris Froome becomes the first rider in the modern calendar era to win the Tour de France and Vuelta a Espana back-to-back in the same year.

title: Primoz Roglic Wins Maiden Grand Tour Title at 2019 Vuelta a Espana in Madrid
description: Former ski jumper Primoz Roglic dominates the Pau time trial and controls the mountains to become Slovenia's first Grand Tour champion.

title: Primoz Roglic Withstands Carapaz on Covatilla to Defend Vuelta Title in Madrid
description: Primoz Roglic survives a fierce late assault by Richard Carapaz on the Alto de la Covatilla to retain his red jersey in Madrid by 24 seconds.

title: Primoz Roglic Dominates Final Time Trial in Santiago for Vuelta Hat-Trick
description: Primoz Roglic wins four stages, capping off an extraordinary performance with victory in the Santiago time trial to equal Tony Rominger's three-peat.

title: Sepp Kuss Wins 2023 Vuelta a Espana as Jumbo-Visma Sweeps Historic Podium
description: American climber Sepp Kuss wins the red jersey in Madrid as teammates Jonas Vingegaard and Primoz Roglic join him in an unprecedented 1-2-3 podium sweep.

title: Bill Rodgers Sets American Record as Joan Benoit Wins Maiden Boston at 21
description: Bill Rodgers runs 2:09:27 to win his third Boston crown while 21-year-old Bowdoin student Joan Benoit wins the women's title.

title: Jacqueline Gareau Awarded Boston Marathon Victory After Rosie Ruiz Hoax
description: Canadian runner Jacqueline Gareau is crowned rightful women's champion after Rosie Ruiz was exposed for joining the course in the final mile.

title: Toshihiko Seko of Japan Conquers Heartbreak Hill to Win 1981 Boston Marathon
description: Japanese distance star Toshihiko Seko unleashes a devastating surge up Heartbreak Hill to win the 85th Boston Marathon in 2:09:26.

title: Alberto Salazar Edges Dick Beardsley in Epic Duel in the Sun at Boston
description: Alberto Salazar defeats Dick Beardsley by two seconds in 2:08:51 after an unforgettable shoulder-to-shoulder battle on Commonwealth Avenue.

title: Joan Benoit Smashes Women's World Record at 1983 Boston Marathon
description: Joan Benoit demolishes the women's marathon world record by nearly three minutes, clocking an astonishing 2:22:43 from Hopkinton to Boston.

title: Geoff Smith of Great Britain Solos to Victory in 1984 Boston Marathon
description: British Olympian Geoff Smith breaks away early to win the 88th Boston Marathon by over four minutes in 2:10:34.

title: Lisa Rainsberger Wins 1985 Boston Marathon Women's Division
description: Lisa Weidenbach Rainsberger captures the women's title in 2:34:06, the last American woman to win Boston until 2018.

title: Robert de Castella Sets Course Record to Win First Official Prize Money Boston
description: Australian world champion Rob de Castella runs 2:07:51 to break the course record in the first Boston Marathon featuring prize money.

title: Rosa Mota of Portugal Wins Maiden Boston Marathon Women's Crown
description: European champion Rosa Mota dominates the women's field to capture her first Boston Marathon title in 2:25:21.

title: Ibrahim Hussein Becomes First African Winner of Boston Marathon
description: Kenyan pioneer Ibrahim Hussein outsprints Juma Ikangaa by one second on Boylston Street to become the first African to win Boston.

title: Abebe Mekonnen Powers to 1989 Boston Marathon Victory for Ethiopia
description: Abebe Mekonnen breaks away along Beacon Street to win the 93rd Boston Marathon, becoming Ethiopia's first male champion since Bikila.

title: Gelindo Bordin of Italy Wins 1990 Boston Marathon on Newton Hills
description: Reigning Olympic champion Gelindo Bordin catches Juma Ikangaa in the final miles to become the first Italian male winner of Boston.

title: Ibrahim Hussein Captures Second Boston Marathon Victory
description: Kenya's Ibrahim Hussein breaks away over the Newton hills to claim his second Boston Marathon title in 2:11:06.

title: INS Shalki Commissioned as First Submarine Built in India
description: INS Shalki (S46), a Type 209 submarine built by Mazagon Dock in Mumbai, is commissioned, establishing India's indigenous submarine manufacturing capability.

title: Ibrahim Hussein Edges Juma Ikangaa by One Second in Thrilling Boston Repeat
description: Ibrahim Hussein defeats Tanzania's Juma Ikangaa by less than two strides in another breathless Boylston Street sprint.

title: Cosmas Ndeti Sprints to Maiden Boston Marathon Crown for Kenya
description: Cosmas Ndeti breaks clear from Kim Wan-ki in the final miles to win his first Boston Marathon title in 2:09:33.

title: INS Tarkash Stealth Guided Missile Frigate Commissioned in Russia
description: INS Tarkash (F50) is commissioned at the Yantar shipyard in Kaliningrad, joining the Indian Navy's sword arm.

title: INS Trikand Stealth Frigate Commissioned into Indian Navy
description: INS Trikand (F51) is commissioned at Kaliningrad, Russia, completing the second batch of Talwar-class stealth frigates.

title: INS Kochi Guided Missile Destroyer Commissioned in Mumbai
description: Defence Minister Manohar Parrikar commissions INS Kochi (D64) into the Indian Navy, featuring the advanced EL/M-2248 MF-STAR radar.

title: INS Chennai Guided Missile Destroyer Commissioned at Naval Dockyard
description: INS Chennai (D65) is commissioned by Defence Minister Manohar Parrikar in Mumbai, concluding the Project 15A destroyer program.

title: Cosmas Ndeti and Uta Pippig Shatter Course Records in 1994 Boston Marathon
description: Cosmas Ndeti runs 2:07:15 while Germany's Uta Pippig clocks 2:21:45 as both men's and women's course records fall on the same day.

title: INS Shankush Type 209 Submarine Commissioned at Mumbai
description: INS Shankush (S47), the second indigenously assembled Type 209 submarine, is formally inducted into the Indian Navy's submarine arm.

title: Cosmas Ndeti Completes Boston Marathon Hat-Trick with Third Straight Win
description: Cosmas Ndeti defeats Moses Tanui to become only the third man in history to win three consecutive Boston Marathons.

title: Moses Tanui Wins Centenary 100th Boston Marathon as Uta Pippig Repeats
description: Moses Tanui wins the historic 100th Boston Marathon before 38,000 runners while Uta Pippig overcomes stomach bleeding to win her third title.

title: Lameck Aguta and Fatuma Roba Capture 1997 Boston Marathon Crowns
description: Kenya's Lameck Aguta wins the men's race while Olympic champion Fatuma Roba becomes the first African woman to win Boston.

title: Moses Tanui Breaks 2:08 to Win Second Boston Marathon Crown
description: Moses Tanui pulls away from Joseph Chebet on the Newton hills to capture his second Boston Marathon victory in 2:07:34.

title: Joseph Chebet Sprints to 1999 Boston Marathon Victory
description: Joseph Chebet holds off Silvio Guerra by four seconds to claim the 103rd Boston Marathon, completing a Kenyan men's sweep.

title: Elijah Lagat Wins Closest Three-Way Sprint Finish in Boston Marathon History
description: Elijah Lagat edges Gezahegne Abera and Moses Tanui as all three finish within four seconds in an electrifying Boylston Street sprint.

title: Lee Bong-ju Wins 2001 Boston Marathon to End Decade of Kenyan Dominance
description: Olympic silver medalist Lee Bong-ju breaks away at mile 18 to win in 2:09:43, capturing South Korea's first Boston victory in 51 years.

title: Margaret Okayo Smashes Course Record to Win 2002 Boston Marathon
description: Kenya's Margaret Okayo shatters the women's course record by over a minute, running 2:20:43 to take the 106th Boston crown.

title: Robert Kipkoech Cheruiyot Wins Maiden Boston Marathon on Patriots' Day
description: Robert Kipkoech Cheruiyot breaks away from Benjamin Kosgei in Kenmore Square to win his first of four Boston Marathon titles.

title: Catherine Ndereba Captures Third Boston Marathon Crown in 85-Degree Heat
description: Catherine Ndereba battles brutal temperatures to capture her third Boston Marathon title, pacing tactically past Elfenesh Alemu.

title: Catherine Ndereba Becomes First Four-Time Women's Champion at Boston
description: Catherine the Great Ndereba makes history as the first woman to win the Boston Marathon four times, clocking 2:25:12.

title: Robert Kipkoech Cheruiyot Breaks Course Record to Win Second Boston Title
description: Robert Kipkoech Cheruiyot runs 2:07:14 to break Cosmas Ndeti's 12-year-old course record and capture his second Boston Marathon.

title: Robert Kipkoech Cheruiyot Conquers Nor'easter Gales to Defend Boston Crown
description: Robert Kipkoech Cheruiyot battles torrential rain, 30-mph headwind gales, and near-freezing cold to win his third Boston Marathon.

title: INS Jalashwa Amphibious Transport Dock Commissioned at Norfolk
description: India commissions its first amphibious transport dock, INS Jalashwa (L41), at Naval Station Norfolk in Virginia, acquired from the United States Navy.

title: Dire Tune Edges Alevtina Biktimirova by Two Seconds in Boston Thriller
description: Ethiopia's Dire Tune wins the closest women's finish in Boston Marathon history, outsprinting Biktimirova on Boylston Street.

title: New Delhi-Amb Andaura Vande Bharat Express Launched in Himachal Pradesh
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi flags off the fourth Vande Bharat Express from Una in Himachal Pradesh to New Delhi.

title: Howrah-New Jalpaiguri Vande Bharat Express Launched as East India's First
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi virtually flags off West Bengal's first semi-high-speed Vande Bharat train from Howrah to New Jalpaiguri.

title: Mumbai-Solapur and Mumbai-Shirdi Twin Vande Bharat Trains Flagged Off
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi flags off two Vande Bharat trains simultaneously from Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus in Mumbai.

title: Dick Beardsley and Inge Simonsen Cross Line Hand-in-Hand at Inaugural London Marathon
description: American Dick Beardsley and Norwegian Inge Simonsen deliberately cross the finish line holding hands in 2:11:48 to share the inaugural London victory.

title: Hugh Jones Runs 2:09:24 to Win Second London Marathon
description: British distance runner Hugh Jones shatters the course record by over two minutes to take a commanding solo victory in London.

title: Salina Kosgei Edges Dire Tune by One Second in Historic Boston Sprint
description: Kenya's Salina Kosgei and defending champion Dire Tune trade the lead five times on Boylston Street before Kosgei wins by a single second.

title: Robert Kiprono Cheruiyot Smashes Course Record to Win 2010 Boston Marathon
description: Twenty-one-year-old Robert Kiprono Cheruiyot becomes the first runner to break 2:06 in Boston, shattering the course record in 2:05:52.

title: Geoffrey Mutai Runs 2:03:02 in Fastest Marathon in Human History at Boston
description: Geoffrey Mutai runs an unfathomable 2:03:02 aided by tailwinds to destroy the world marathon best and win the 115th Boston Marathon.

title: Wesley Korir Battles 87-Degree Sweltering Heat to Win 2012 Boston Marathon
description: Kenyan scholar-athlete Wesley Korir overtakes Levy Matebo in the Newton hills during a dangerous heatwave to claim the Boston title.

title: Meb Keflezighi Wins Emotional 2014 Boston Marathon for Boston Strong
description: Thirty-eight-year-old Meb Keflezighi breaks away solo to become the first American male winner in 31 years, wearing the names of bombing victims on his bib.

title: Caroline Rotich Sprints Past Mare Dibaba on Boylston for Boston Title
description: Kenya's Caroline Rotich outsprints world champion Mare Dibaba in the final 100 meters to win the 119th Boston Marathon.

title: Atsede Baysa Stages Miraculous 37-Second Deficit Comeback to Win Boston
description: Ethiopia's Atsede Baysa makes up a 37-second gap with five miles remaining to storm to a dramatic victory in the 120th Boston Marathon.

title: Edna Kiplagat Dominates Heartbreak Hill to Win Boston Marathon at Age 37
description: Two-time world champion Edna Kiplagat drops the women's field with a devastating surge on the Newton hills to win Boston on her debut.

title: Des Linden and Yuki Kawauchi Conquer Freezing Deluge to Win 2018 Boston
description: Des Linden becomes the first American woman to win Boston in 33 years while citizen runner Yuki Kawauchi shocks the world in freezing torrential rain.

title: Lawrence Cherono Outsprints Lelisa Desisa by Two Seconds in Boston Thriller
description: Lawrence Cherono catches two-time champion Lelisa Desisa ten yards before the finish line to win the 123rd Boston Marathon by two seconds.

title: Benson Kipruto Wins Landmark Autumn 125th Boston Marathon
description: Benson Kipruto launches a decisive move at mile 22 to win the 125th Boston Marathon, held in October for the first time in race history.

title: Peres Jepchirchir Edges Ababel Yeshaneh in Breathless Boylston Street Duel
description: Olympic champion Peres Jepchirchir and Ababel Yeshaneh trade the lead eight times over the final mile before Jepchirchir wins by four seconds.

title: Bhopal-New Delhi Vande Bharat Express Flagged Off at Rani Kamlapati Station
description: Prime Minister Modi flags off Madhya Pradesh's first Vande Bharat Express from Rani Kamlapati station in Bhopal to Hazrat Nizamuddin in Delhi.

title: Secunderabad-Tirupati Vande Bharat Express Flagged Off by PM Modi
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi flags off the Secunderabad-Tirupati Vande Bharat Express, reducing pilgrim journey time by over three hours.

title: Evans Chebet Defends Boston Title as Hellen Obiri Wins on Debut
description: Evans Chebet pulls away from Gabriel Geay to repeat as champion while Hellen Obiri wins the women's crown in her first Boston Marathon.

title: Puri-Howrah Vande Bharat Express Launched as Odisha's First
description: Prime Minister Modi virtually flags off Odisha's first Vande Bharat Express connecting the holy pilgrimage city of Puri to Howrah in Kolkata.

title: Gorakhpur-Lucknow and Jodhpur-Sabarmati Vande Bharat Trains Flagged Off
description: Prime Minister Modi flags off the Gorakhpur-Lucknow Vande Bharat Express at Gorakhpur railway station, boosting connectivity in Uttar Pradesh.

title: Prime Minister Modi Inaugurates Six Vande Bharat Trains at Ayodhya Dham
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurates the redeveloped Ayodhya Dham railway station and flags off six new Vande Bharat Express trains across India.

title: Paona Brajabasi High School of Manipur Wins 1975 Subroto Cup
description: Paona Brajabasi High School of Imphal defeats Madhyamgram High School of West Bengal in New Delhi to win the prestigious 1975 Subroto Cup.

title: Madhyamgram High School of Bengal Captures 1977 Subroto Cup in Delhi
description: Madhyamgram High School from 24 Parganas in West Bengal claims the Subroto Cup football championship at the Ambedkar Stadium in New Delhi.

title: St. Anthony's High School of Shillong Wins 1980 Subroto Cup
description: St. Anthony's High School from Shillong, Meghalaya, defeats Army Boys Company in New Delhi to lift the 1980 Subroto Cup trophy.

title: Grete Waitz Smashes Women's World Record at 1983 London Marathon
description: Norwegian legend Grete Waitz breaks the women's world marathon record in 2:25:29 as Mike Gratton wins the men's race in 2:09:43.

title: Madhyamgram High School Wins Historic Fourth Subroto Cup Championship
description: Bengal's Madhyamgram High School completes a dominant tournament campaign in New Delhi to secure its fourth Subroto Cup title.

title: Charlie Spedding Sprints Past Favourites to Win 1984 London Marathon
description: Charlie Spedding uses tactical patience to break away in the final two miles and claim victory on Westminster Bridge.

title: Ingrid Kristiansen Smashes World Record in 2:21:06 at London Marathon
description: Norway's Ingrid Kristiansen runs an extraordinary world record of 2:21:06 that stands unbeaten for 13 years, while Steve Jones wins the men's race.

title: Toshihiko Seko of Japan Wins London Marathon on The Mall
description: Toshihiko Seko defeats Hugh Jones and Allister Hutton in 2:10:02 to capture the prestigious London Marathon crown.

title: Hiromi Taniguchi Delivers Japanese Double with 1987 London Marathon Win
description: Hiromi Taniguchi runs 2:09:50 to take the London Marathon title, giving Japan back-to-back victories on the capital's streets.

title: Henrik Jorgensen of Denmark Solos to Victory in 1988 London Marathon
description: Henrik Jorgensen breaks away from the lead pack to win in 2:10:20 while Ingrid Kristiansen claims her fourth women's London crown.

title: Sports School of Gomantak Wins 1988 Subroto Cup Football Title
description: Sports School from Goa defeats Government High School of Mizoram at Ambedkar Stadium to claim the 1988 Subroto Cup crown.

title: Douglas Wakiihuri Becomes First Kenyan Winner of London Marathon
description: World champion Douglas Wakiihuri runs 2:09:03 wearing white gloves to become the first Kenyan runner to win the London Marathon.

title: Allister Hutton of Scotland Powers Through Wind to Win 1990 London Marathon
description: Scottish distance star Allister Hutton breaks away over the final five miles to claim a popular home victory in 2:10:10.

title: Yakov Tolstikov of Soviet Union Wins 1991 London Marathon
description: Soviet marathoner Yakov Tolstikov surprises the field with a dominant 2:09:17 victory while Rosa Mota wins the women's race.

title: Antonio Pinto Sprints to Maiden London Marathon Victory
description: Portuguese runner Antonio Pinto clocks 2:10:02 to capture his first of three London Marathon titles on Westminster Bridge.

title: Eamonn Martin Delivers Fairytale British London Marathon Victory
description: Eamonn Martin defeats Mexican star Isidro Rico in a sprint finish on Westminster Bridge to become the last British male winner of London.

title: Dionicio Ceron of Mexico Wins 1994 London Marathon
description: Mexican distance star Dionicio Ceron runs 2:08:53 to defeat Abebe Mekonnen and capture his first London Marathon title.

title: Liz McColgan Wins London Marathon on Debut Before Home Crowd
description: Scottish world 10,000m champion Liz McColgan dominates the women's field in 2:27:32 to win London on her marathon debut.

title: Dionicio Ceron Completes London Marathon Hat-Trick with Third Straight Win
description: Dionicio Ceron equals the all-time record by winning his third consecutive London Marathon, holding off Vincent Rousseau.

title: Antonio Pinto Breaks Course Record to Win Second London Marathon
description: Antonio Pinto runs 2:07:55 to take his second London Marathon crown while Joyce Chepchumba wins the women's division.

title: Army Boys Company Danapur Wins 1993 Subroto Cup in New Delhi
description: The Army Boys Company from Danapur claims the Subroto Cup junior boys title with an emphatic final performance in New Delhi.

title: Greenwood School of Nagaland Wins 1997 Subroto Cup Championship
description: Greenwood School from Dimapur, Nagaland, edges Bokaro Ispat Vidyalaya in New Delhi to win their maiden Subroto Cup football trophy.

title: Catherina McKiernan of Ireland Wins 1998 London Marathon Women's Title
description: Irish cross-country specialist Catherina McKiernan breaks clear in the rain to win the women's London Marathon in 2:26:26.

title: Abdelkader El Mouaziz of Morocco Solos to 1999 London Marathon Victory
description: Abdelkader El Mouaziz breaks away early and runs alone through central London to win the 19th London Marathon in 2:07:57.

title: Antonio Pinto Smashes European Record to Win Third London Marathon
description: Antonio Pinto clocks a sensational 2:06:36 to claim his third London title while Tegla Loroupe wins the women's race.

title: Abdelkader El Mouaziz Captures Second London Marathon Championship
description: Abdelkader El Mouaziz runs 2:07:11 to claim his second London Marathon title while Derartu Tulu wins the women's crown.

title: Bokaro Steel Plant School Wins 2001 Subroto Cup Junior Boys Title
description: Bokaro Steel Plant School from Jharkhand defeats Army Boys Company to lift the 2001 Subroto Cup football championship in New Delhi.

title: Khalid Khannouchi Smashes World Record as Paula Radcliffe Debuts in London
description: Khalid Khannouchi runs a world-record 2:05:38 while Paula Radcliffe runs the fastest women's debut in history (2:18:56) in a legendary race.

title: Evans Rutto Conquers Rain and Wind to Win 2004 London Marathon
description: Kenyan star Evans Rutto survives torrential downpours to win London in 2:06:18 while Margaret Okayo wins the women's title.

title: Martin Lel Sprints on The Mall to Win Maiden London Marathon
description: Martin Lel outsprints reigning world champion Jaouad Gharib on The Mall while Paula Radcliffe wins her third London title in 2:17:42.

title: St. Ignatius High School Gumla Wins 2006 Subroto Cup in New Delhi
description: St. Ignatius High School from Gumla, Jharkhand, wins the Subroto Cup championship match at the Ambedkar Stadium in New Delhi.

title: Martin Lel Out-Sprints Abderrahim Goumri on The Mall to Win Second London Title
description: Martin Lel unleashes a devastating sprint finish along Birdcage Walk to win the 2007 London Marathon in 2:07:41.

title: Martin Lel Sprints Through Rain for Historic Third London Marathon Crown
description: Martin Lel pulls away from Sammy Wanjiru and Goumri on The Mall to become a three-time London Marathon champion.

title: Samuel Wanjiru Shatters London Course Record in Blistering 2:05:10
description: Olympic champion Sammy Wanjiru runs an aggressive front-running race to smash the course record in 2:05:10.

title: Tsegaye Kebede Solos Through London Rain to Win 2010 Marathon
description: Ethiopia's Tsegaye Kebede runs 2:05:19 to take his first London Marathon title after breaking away along the Embankment.

title: Wilson Kipsang Dominates London Field as Mary Keitany Repeats in 2:18:37
description: Wilson Kipsang breaks clear at mile 15 to win in 2:04:44 while Mary Keitany defends her title in a Kenyan record 2:18:37.

title: Dynamo Kyiv Youth Academy Wins 2012 Subroto Cup International Title
description: The youth academy team of Ukrainian giants FC Dynamo Kyiv defeats MSP Higher Secondary School of Kerala to win the 2012 Subroto Cup in Delhi.

title: Tsegaye Kebede Rallies from 30 Seconds Down to Steal London Marathon Win
description: Tsegaye Kebede chases down Emmanuel Mutai on the final mile along the Thames to win his second London Marathon title.

title: Wilson Kipsang Breaks London Course Record in 2:04:29
description: World record holder Wilson Kipsang drops Stanley Biwott on The Mall to win his second London title in course-record time.

title: Eliud Kipchoge Sprints Past Wilson Kipsang to Win Maiden London Marathon
description: Eliud Kipchoge defeats defending champion Wilson Kipsang by five seconds in 2:04:42, beginning his legendary reign at the London Marathon.

title: Christa Vahlensieck Sets Women's Marathon World Record at Berlin
description: West German distance runner Christa Vahlensieck clocks 2:34:48 in the Grunewald forest to set a new women's marathon world record.

title: Ian Ray of Great Britain Wins First City-Street Berlin Marathon
description: Ian Ray wins the 8th Berlin Marathon, the first edition routed through the streets of West Berlin, finishing at the Kurfuerstendamm.

title: Karel Lismont of Belgium Captures 1983 Berlin Marathon Title
description: Two-time Olympic medalist Karel Lismont of Belgium wins the 10th Berlin Marathon in 2:13:37.

description: Jimmy Ashworth clocks 2:11:43 to take the men's victory at the 12th Berlin Marathon.

title: Suleiman Nyambui of Tanzania Wins 1987 Berlin Marathon

description: PT Usha dominates the sprint events at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in New Delhi, winning four gold medals and two silvers.

description: Australia's Steve Moneghetti clocks 2:08:16 as 25,000 runners run through the opened Brandenburg Gate three days before German reunification.

title: Sisay Lemma and Joyciline Jepkosgei Win Landmark Autumn London Marathon

description: Amos Kipruto solos to victory in 2:04:39 while Yalemzerf Yehualaw recovers from a heavy fall with six miles remaining to win in 2:17:26.

title: TG English School of Manipur Wins 62nd Subroto Cup Under-17 Championship
description: TG English School from Bishnupur, Manipur, defeats Chandigarh in the final at Ambedkar Stadium in New Delhi to lift the 62nd Subroto Cup.

description: Antonio Pinto breaks clear from the lead pack to take his first Berlin Marathon title while Katrin Dorre wins the women's race.

title: Jyotirmoyee Sikdar Wins 800m Gold at Asian Athletics Championships in Fukuoka

description: KM Beenamol clocks 51.41 seconds to win the women's 400m gold medal at the Asian Athletics Championships in Jakarta.

description: Karnataka hosts the 30th National Games of India, inaugurated at the Sree Kanteerava Stadium in Bangalore.

description: Brazilian underdog Marilson Gomes dos Santos attacks on the Queensboro Bridge to stun favourites in Central Park and claim victory.

title: Khalid Khannouchi Smashes Marathon World Record in 2:05:42 at Chicago
description: Khalid Khannouchi lowers Ronaldo da Costa's world record by 23 seconds, becoming the first runner to break 2:06 on American soil.

title: 31st Punjab National Games Inaugurated at Guru Nanak Stadium in Ludhiana
description: Punjab hosts the 2001 National Games across five cities, featuring premier sporting facilities at Ludhiana, Patiala, and Jalandhar.

title: 32nd National Games of India Inaugurated at Gachibowli Stadium in Hyderabad

title: 33rd National Games Inaugurated at Sarusajai Complex in Guwahati

title: 34th National Games Inaugurated at Birsa Munda Stadium in Ranchi
description: Jharkhand hosts the 34th National Games of India, inaugurated at the Birsa Munda Athletics Stadium in Ranchi.

title: Prime Minister Modi Inaugurates 37th National Games in Fatorda, Goa

description: Chris Froome beats Tony Martin by one second in the Neuchatel time trial to successfully defend his Tour de Romandie general classification.

description: Russian climber Ilnur Zakarin surprises the peloton with a formidable mountain performance to win the 2015 Tour de Romandie in Lausanne.

description: Colombian Nairo Quintana defends his overall lead through the Swiss mountains to capture the 2016 Tour de Romandie title in Geneva.

description: Australian Richie Porte overcomes a nineteen-second deficit in the final Lausanne time trial to capture the 2017 Tour de Romandie.

title: Primoz Roglic Defends Yellow Jersey in Geneva to Win 2018 Romandie
description: Former ski jumper Primoz Roglic defends his overall lead across the final mountain stages to capture his maiden WorldTour title at Romandie.

title: Primoz Roglic Sweeps Three Stages to Retain Tour de Romandie Title
description: Primoz Roglic wins the concluding Geneva time trial to seal his third stage win and become the first repeat Romandie champion in five years.

title: Richie Porte Holds Off Late Attacks on Les Gets to Win 2021 Dauphine
description: Australian veteran Richie Porte defends his yellow jersey on the descent into Les Gets to capture the 2021 Criterium du Dauphine.

title: Aleksandr Vlasov Dominates Villars Time Trial to Win 2022 Romandie
description: Aleksandr Vlasov wins the brutal final mountain time trial up to Villars to snatch the yellow jersey and capture the 2022 Tour de Romandie.

title: Primoz Roglic and Jonas Vingegaard Celebrate One-Two Dauphine Triumph
description: Jumbo-Visma teammates Primoz Roglic and Jonas Vingegaard cross the Plateau de Solaison hand-in-hand as Roglic wins the 2022 Dauphine.

title: Adam Yates Defends Lead in Geneva to Win 2023 Tour de Romandie
description: British rider Adam Yates protects his yellow jersey after a decisive climb to Thyon 2000 to win the 2023 Tour de Romandie in Geneva.

title: Jonas Vingegaard Crushes Rivals on Bastille to Win 2023 Dauphine
description: Reigning Tour de France champion Jonas Vingegaard climbs the Grenoble Bastille to seal the 2023 Criterium du Dauphine by over two minutes.

title: CSIR Foundation Day Announces 1999 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Awards
description: CSIR marks its foundation day by announcing the 1999 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prizes honoring visionary work by Indian scientists under forty-five.

description: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research declares the 2000 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize winners in New Delhi across core disciplines.

title: CSIR Announces 2001 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners
description: On its foundation day, CSIR announces the 2001 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prizes recognizing exemplary research across scientific disciplines.
