description: Celebrating its diamond jubilee, CSIR declares the 2002 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize laureates in engineering, medical, and physical sciences.

title: CSIR Foundation Day Announces 2003 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Laureates
description: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research names the 2003 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize recipients during its foundation day session.

title: Oscar Freire Sprints on Avenue de Grammont to Win 2010 Paris-Tours
description: Three-time world champion Oscar Freire unleashes an unstoppable sprint to win his second career Paris-Tours classic on the Avenue de Grammont.

title: Tom Boonen Outkicks Daniele Bennati to Win Second Gent-Wevelgem
description: Belgian cycling hero Tom Boonen sprints to his second career Gent-Wevelgem classic victory, seven years after his first triumph in 2004.

title: Greg Van Avermaet Outkicks Marco Marcato to Win 2011 Paris-Tours
description: Belgian rider Greg Van Avermaet attacks late alongside Marco Marcato, outsprinting the Italian to claim his first major classic at Paris-Tours.

title: Tom Boonen Sprints to Record-Equaling Third Gent-Wevelgem Title
description: Tom Boonen outpaces Peter Sagan in Wevelgem to win his second classic in three days and equal the record of three Gent-Wevelgem victories.

title: Peter Sagan Solos in Freezing Rain to Win Maiden Gent-Wevelgem
description: Twenty-three-year-old Peter Sagan breaks clear four kilometers out in freezing Flemish winds to solo to his first Gent-Wevelgem classic victory.

title: John Degenkolb Outkicks Arnaud Demare to Win 2014 Gent-Wevelgem
description: German powerhouse John Degenkolb wins a mass field sprint in Wevelgem to capture his first career Belgian cobbled classic.

title: Jelle Wallays Survives from Early Breakaway to Win 2014 Paris-Tours
description: Topsport Vlaanderen rider Jelle Wallays holds off Thomas Voeckler in a two-man sprint to win Paris-Tours from the day-long breakaway.

title: Luca Paolini Attacks Through Gale-Force Winds to Win Gent-Wevelgem
description: Thirty-eight-year-old Italian veteran Luca Paolini attacks five kilometers from the finish amidst hurricane-force winds to win an epic race.

title: World Champion Peter Sagan Sprints Past Vanmarcke to Win Gent-Wevelgem
description: Peter Sagan wears the rainbow jersey as he outkicks Sep Vanmarcke and Vyacheslav Kuznetsov to take his second Gent-Wevelgem title.

title: Peter Sagan Sprints Past Elia Viviani to Equal Record Third Gent-Wevelgem
description: Peter Sagan launches a blistering sprint from two hundred meters out to beat Elia Viviani and claim his record-equaling third Gent-Wevelgem.

title: Alexander Kristoff Overwhelms Sprinters to Win 2019 Gent-Wevelgem
description: Norwegian powerhouse Alexander Kristoff launches a long-range sprint to defeat John Degenkolb and win the 2019 Gent-Wevelgem classic.

title: Mads Pedersen Sprints from Four-Man Breakaway to Win Gent-Wevelgem
description: Former world champion Mads Pedersen times his move perfectly from a late breakaway to capture the rescheduled autumn Gent-Wevelgem.

title: Wout van Aert Sprints to Maiden Gent-Wevelgem Victory for Jumbo-Visma
description: Belgian superstar Wout van Aert dominates a seven-man breakaway sprint in Wevelgem to capture his first Gent-Wevelgem championship.

title: Biniam Girmay Makes History as First African Winner of Gent-Wevelgem
description: Twenty-one-year-old Eritrean Biniam Girmay shocks the cycling world by outsprinting Christophe Laporte to become the first African classic champion.

title: Christophe Laporte Handed Gent-Wevelgem Win by Teammate Wout van Aert
description: Jumbo-Visma teammates Wout van Aert and Christophe Laporte complete a dominant 52-kilometer two-man breakaway, with Van Aert gifting Laporte the win.

title: 2004 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Laureates Named on CSIR Day
description: CSIR announces the 2004 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize winners in New Delhi, honoring cutting-edge breakthroughs in Indian science.

title: CSIR Celebrates Foundation Day with 2005 Bhatnagar Prize Declarations
description: On CSIR Foundation Day, the prestigious 2005 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prizes are announced across biological, chemical, and physical sciences.

title: CSIR Announces 2006 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Laureates in Delhi
description: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research reveals the 2006 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize recipients on its 64th foundation day.

title: 2007 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners Announced on CSIR Day
description: CSIR marks its foundation day by announcing the 2007 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prizes honoring nine exceptional young Indian scientists.

title: CSIR Foundation Day Declares 2008 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Laureates
description: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research announces the 2008 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize winners in New Delhi.

title: Juan Antonio Flecha Solos Over Molenberg to Win 2010 Omloop
description: Team Sky rider Juan Antonio Flecha launches a decisive solo attack on the Molenberg to capture the 2010 Omloop Het Nieuwsblad.

title: Sebastian Langeveld Edges Juan Antonio Flecha in Photo Finish at Omloop
description: Dutch rider Sebastian Langeveld defeats Juan Antonio Flecha by mere millimeters in a breathless two-man sprint to win Omloop.

title: Sep Vanmarcke Stuns Tom Boonen to Win Maiden Omloop Het Nieuwsblad
description: Twenty-three-year-old Sep Vanmarcke outsprints Tom Boonen and Juan Antonio Flecha in Ghent to claim a sensational maiden classic triumph.

title: Luca Paolini Outwits Stannard and Vandenbergh to Win 2013 Omloop
description: Italian veteran Luca Paolini times his sprint perfectly from a small lead group to capture the 2013 Omloop Het Nieuwsblad in Ghent.

title: Ian Stannard Outkicks Greg Van Avermaet to Win 2014 Omloop
description: British powerhouse Ian Stannard rides through heavy Belgian drizzle to defeat Greg Van Avermaet in a two-man sprint for the Omloop title.

title: Ian Stannard Defeats Three Etixx-QuickStep Riders in Miraculous Omloop Win
description: Ian Stannard executes one of modern cycling's most famous tactical rides, single-handedly outfoxing three Etixx riders to retain Omloop.

title: Matteo Trentin Breaks Yellow Ribbon Record to Win 2015 Paris-Tours
description: Matteo Trentin wins Paris-Tours at an astonishing average speed of 49.64 km/h, earning the prestigious Ruban Jaune for the fastest classic.

title: Greg Van Avermaet Outkicks Peter Sagan to Win 2016 Omloop Het Nieuwsblad
description: Greg Van Avermaet defeats world champion Peter Sagan in a five-man sprint on the Emile Clauslaan to claim his first Omloop victory.

title: Fernando Gaviria Surprises Bunch with Long Sprint to Win Paris-Tours
description: Twenty-two-year-old Colombian Fernando Gaviria attacks from 600 meters out, catching the entire peloton off guard to win Paris-Tours.

title: Greg Van Avermaet Outpaces Sagan and Vanmarcke to Retain Omloop Title
description: Olympic champion Greg Van Avermaet beats Peter Sagan and Sep Vanmarcke to become the first back-to-back Omloop champion in thirty years.

title: Matteo Trentin Outkicks Soren Kragh Andersen to Win Second Paris-Tours
description: Italian rider Matteo Trentin caps a sensational late season by defeating Soren Kragh Andersen to capture his second Paris-Tours title.

title: Soren Kragh Andersen Conquers Vineyard Gravel to Win 2018 Paris-Tours
description: Danish rider Soren Kragh Andersen thrives on the newly introduced vineyard gravel sectors to solo into Tours for classic victory.

title: Jelle Wallays Solos Past Gravel Sectors to Win Second Paris-Tours
description: Lotto Soudal rider Jelle Wallays launches a solo raid over the chalk gravel roads to capture his second career Paris-Tours championship.

title: Arnaud Demare Sprints to Back-to-Back Paris-Tours Championships
description: Arnaud Demare outpaces Edward Teuns in a small group sprint to become the first rider in twenty-four years to win consecutive Paris-Tours titles.

title: Riley Sheehan Stuns Favorites as Neo-Pro to Win 2023 Paris-Tours
description: American stagiaire Riley Sheehan shocks the peloton by winning Paris-Tours from a five-man sprint, becoming the first American winner.

title: South Korean President Kim Dae-jung Awarded 2000 Nobel Peace Prize
description: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awards the 2000 Nobel Peace Prize to Kim Dae-jung for his Sunshine Policy and historic reconciliation with North Korea.

title: United Nations and Kofi Annan Awarded 2001 Nobel Peace Prize
description: The Norwegian Nobel Committee honors the United Nations and Secretary-General Kofi Annan on the UN's centenary for work toward a more organized and peaceful world.

title: Former US President Jimmy Carter Awarded 2002 Nobel Peace Prize
description: Jimmy Carter receives the Nobel Peace Prize for decades of untiring effort to find peaceful solutions to international conflicts and advance democracy.

title: Iranian Human Rights Lawyer Shirin Ebadi Awarded 2003 Nobel Peace Prize
description: Shirin Ebadi becomes the first Muslim woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize, honored for her courageous advocacy for democracy and human rights.

title: Kenyan Environmentalist Wangari Maathai Awarded 2004 Nobel Peace Prize
description: Green Belt Movement founder Wangari Maathai becomes the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize for her contribution to sustainable development.

title: IAEA and Director Mohamed ElBaradei Win 2005 Nobel Peace Prize
description: The International Atomic Energy Agency and Director General Mohamed ElBaradei are awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for preventing military nuclear proliferation.

title: Muhammad Yunus and Grameen Bank Awarded 2006 Nobel Peace Prize
description: Bangladeshi economist Muhammad Yunus and Grameen Bank receive the Nobel Peace Prize for pioneering microcredit to advance social and economic development.

title: IPCC and Al Gore Awarded 2007 Nobel Peace Prize for Climate Action
description: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change and former US Vice President Al Gore win the Nobel Peace Prize for disseminating knowledge about man-made climate change.

title: Finnish Diplomat Martti Ahtisaari Awarded 2008 Nobel Peace Prize
description: Former Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for his mediation efforts resolving conflicts in Namibia, Kosovo, and Aceh.

title: CSIR Announces Eleven 2009 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners
description: On its 67th foundation day, CSIR declares eleven young researchers as winners of the 2009 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize.

title: Nine Scientists Named 2010 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Laureates by CSIR
description: CSIR announces nine scientists as recipients of the prestigious 2010 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize during CSIR Foundation Day celebrations.

title: CSIR Declares Eleven Winners of 2011 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize
description: On its foundation day, CSIR announces eleven researchers as winners of the 2011 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology.

title: Platinum Jubilee CSIR Foundation Day Declares 2012 Bhatnagar Prizes
description: CSIR announces the 2012 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prizes during its 70th foundation day celebrations inaugurated by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.

title: Eight Scientists Win 2013 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize on CSIR Day
description: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research announces eight scientists as winners of the 2013 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize.

title: Michael Valgren Solos Over Muur van Geraardsbergen to Win Omloop
description: Danish rider Michael Valgren attacks two kilometers from the line in Ninove to capture his first WorldTour classic victory at Omloop.

title: Zdenek Stybar Attacks on Ninove Approach to Win 2019 Omloop Het Nieuwsblad
description: Former cyclocross world champion Zdenek Stybar launches a late solo counterattack to win Omloop Het Nieuwsblad for Deceuninck-Quick-Step.

title: Jasper Stuyven Solos into Ninove to Win 2020 Omloop Het Nieuwsblad
description: Belgian rider Jasper Stuyven outkicks Yves Lampaert in a two-man dash to capture the opening classic of the season at Omloop.

title: Davide Ballerini Sprints to Victory in 2021 Omloop Het Nieuwsblad
description: Italian sprinter Davide Ballerini wins an uncharacteristically large bunch sprint in Ninove to give Deceuninck-Quick-Step victory at Omloop.

title: Wout van Aert Solos from Bosberg to Win Maiden Omloop Het Nieuwsblad
description: Belgian champion Wout van Aert launches an explosive attack over the Bosberg cobbled climb to solo into Ninove for a dominant Omloop win.

title: Dylan van Baarle Solos to 2023 Omloop Het Nieuwsblad on Jumbo Debut
description: Paris-Roubaix champion Dylan van Baarle attacks sixteen kilometers from the finish to win Omloop Het Nieuwsblad on his debut for Jumbo-Visma.

title: Chinese Dissident Gao Xingjian Awarded 2000 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: The Swedish Academy awards the 2000 Nobel Prize in Literature to Gao Xingjian for an oeuvre of universal validity, bitter insights and linguistic ingenuity.

title: Trinidad-Born Author V.S. Naipaul Awarded 2001 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: V.S. Naipaul is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for having united perceptive narrative and incorruptible scrutiny in works that compel us to see suppressed histories.

title: Imprisoned Chinese Dissident Liu Xiaobo Awarded 2010 Nobel Peace Prize
description: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awards the Nobel Peace Prize to Liu Xiaobo for his long and non-violent struggle for fundamental human rights in China.

title: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, Leymah Gbowee, and Tawakkol Karman Win Nobel Peace Prize
description: Three women leaders from Liberia and Yemen are awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for their non-violent struggle for women's safety and rights in peace-building.

title: European Union Awarded 2012 Nobel Peace Prize for Continent-Wide Peace
description: The Norwegian Nobel Committee honors the European Union for over six decades of advancing peace, reconciliation, democracy, and human rights in Europe.

title: Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons Wins Nobel Peace Prize
description: The OPCW is awarded the 2013 Nobel Peace Prize for its extensive efforts to eliminate chemical weapons arsenals globally under international law.

title: Ten Researchers Win 2014 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize on CSIR Day
description: CSIR declares ten scientists as recipients of the 2014 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize during its 72nd foundation day event in New Delhi.

title: Eleven Scientists Named 2015 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Laureates
description: On CSIR Foundation Day, eleven prominent young researchers are named winners of the 2015 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology.

title: Tunisian National Dialogue Quartet Awarded 2015 Nobel Peace Prize
description: The civil society coalition Tunisian National Dialogue Quartet is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for building a pluralistic democracy following the Jasmine Revolution.

title: CSIR Platinum Jubilee Celebrations Announce 2016 Bhatnagar Prizes
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi kicks off CSIR's platinum jubilee as the 2016 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize winners are announced in New Delhi.

title: Colombian President Juan Manuel Santos Awarded 2016 Nobel Peace Prize
description: President Juan Manuel Santos receives the Nobel Peace Prize for his resolute efforts to negotiate a peace agreement ending Colombia's fifty-year civil war.

title: Ten Scientists Selected for 2017 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize by CSIR
description: On its foundation day, CSIR declares ten young researchers as recipients of the 2017 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize across seven categories.

title: International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons Wins 2017 Nobel Peace Prize
description: ICAN is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for drawing attention to catastrophic humanitarian consequences and achieving a treaty-based ban on nuclear weapons.

title: Thirteen Scientists Named 2018 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Laureates
description: CSIR announces thirteen scientists as winners of the 2018 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize during its 76th foundation day celebrations.

title: Denis Mukwege and Nadia Murad Awarded 2018 Nobel Peace Prize
description: Congolese physician Denis Mukwege and Yazidi activist Nadia Murad receive the Nobel Peace Prize for their courageous efforts to end sexual violence in armed conflict.

title: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Awarded 2019 Nobel Peace Prize
description: Abiy Ahmed receives the Nobel Peace Prize for his initiative to resolve the border conflict with neighboring Eritrea and promote regional peace.

title: World Food Programme Awarded 2020 Nobel Peace Prize
description: The United Nations World Food Programme receives the Nobel Peace Prize for combating global hunger and preventing the use of starvation as a weapon of war.

title: Journalists Maria Ressa and Dmitry Muratov Awarded 2021 Nobel Peace Prize
description: Maria Ressa of the Philippines and Dmitry Muratov of Russia win the Nobel Peace Prize for safeguarding freedom of expression in defense of democracy.

title: Ales Bialiatski, Memorial, and Center for Civil Liberties Win Nobel Peace Prize
description: Human rights advocates from Belarus, Russia, and Ukraine receive the Nobel Peace Prize for documenting war crimes and human rights abuses.

title: Imprisoned Iranian Activist Narges Mohammadi Awarded 2023 Nobel Peace Prize
description: Narges Mohammadi is awarded the Nobel Peace Prize from Evin Prison for her courageous fight against the oppression of women in Iran.

title: Punjab Hosts 31st National Games Across Five Cities
description: The 31st National Games of India open in Punjab with competitions staged in Ludhiana, Patiala, Jalandhar, and Anandpur Sahib.

title: Hungarian Holocaust Survivor Imre Kertesz Wins Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Imre Kertesz receives the 2002 Nobel Prize in Literature for writing that upholds the fragile experience of the individual against the barbaric arbitrariness of history.

title: South African Novelist J.M. Coetzee Awarded 2003 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: The Swedish Academy honors J.M. Coetzee, author of Disgrace and Waiting for the Barbarians, for portraying the surprising involvement of the outsider in countless guises.

title: Austrian Playwright Elfriede Jelinek Awarded 2004 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Elfriede Jelinek receives the Nobel Prize in Literature for her musical flow of voices and counter-voices in novels and plays that reveal the absurdity of society's clichés.

title: British Dramatist Harold Pinter Awarded 2005 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Harold Pinter is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for his plays that uncover the precipice under everyday prattle and force entry into oppression's closed rooms.

title: Turkish Novelist Orhan Pamuk Awarded 2006 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Orhan Pamuk receives the Nobel Prize in Literature for discovering new symbols for the clash and interlacing of cultures in the quest for the melancholic soul of his native city.

title: British Author Doris Lessing Named Oldest Literature Nobel Laureate
description: At age 87, Doris Lessing is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature as that epicist of the female experience, who with scepticism, fire and visionary power subjected a divided civilization to scrutiny.

title: French Author J.M.G. Le Clezio Awarded 2008 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: J.M.G. Le Clezio is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature as an author of new departures, poetic adventure and sensual ecstasy, explorer of a humanity beyond reigning civilization.

title: Romanian-Born German Author Herta Muller Wins Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Herta Muller receives the 2009 Nobel Prize in Literature for depicting the landscape of the dispossessed with the concentration of poetry and the frankness of prose.

title: Peruvian Novelist Mario Vargas Llosa Awarded 2010 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Mario Vargas Llosa receives the Nobel Prize in Literature for his cartography of structures of power and his trenchant images of the individual's resistance, revolt, and defeat.

title: Swedish Poet Tomas Transtromer Awarded 2011 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Tomas Transtromer is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature because, through his condensed, translucent images, he gives us fresh access to reality.

title: Chinese Novelist Mo Yan Awarded 2012 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Mo Yan receives the Nobel Prize in Literature for merging folk tales, history, and the contemporary with hallucinatory realism in works such as Red Sorghum.

title: Canadian Short Story Master Alice Munro Wins 2013 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: The Swedish Academy honors Alice Munro as master of the contemporary short story, making her the first Canadian woman to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

title: French Novelist Patrick Modiano Awarded 2014 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Patrick Modiano receives the Nobel Prize in Literature for the art of memory with which he has evoked the most ungraspable human destinies and uncovered the life-world of the Occupation.

title: Belarusian Investigative Journalist Svetlana Alexievich Wins Nobel Prize
description: Svetlana Alexievich is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for her polyphonic writings, a monument to suffering and courage in our time, documenting Chernobyl and Soviet wars.

title: British-Japanese Author Kazuo Ishiguro Awarded 2017 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Kazuo Ishiguro receives the Nobel Prize in Literature for novels of great emotional force that uncover the abyss beneath our illusory sense of connection with the world.

title: Fourteen Researchers Awarded 2019 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize
description: President Ram Nath Kovind attends CSIR Foundation Day where fourteen scientists are announced as winners of the 2019 Bhatnagar Prize.

title: Fourteen Scientists Win 2020 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize on CSIR Day
description: Science and Technology Minister Harsh Vardhan announces fourteen young researchers as recipients of the 2020 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize.

title: Eleven Scientists Named 2021 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Recipients
description: On the 80th CSIR Foundation Day, eleven researchers under forty-five are declared winners of the 2021 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize.

title: Twelve Scientists Named 2022 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners
description: CSIR announces the long-awaited 2022 Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prizes honoring twelve exceptional young researchers across physical and life sciences.

title: President Zail Singh Confers Inaugural Dronacharya Awards at Rashtrapati Bhavan
description: President Giani Zail Singh presents the inaugural Dronacharya Awards for coaching excellence to O.M. Nambiar, Om Prakash Bhardwaj, and B.B. Bhagwat.

title: Desh Prem Azad and R.V. Gokhale Conferred 1986 Dronacharya Awards
description: Kapil Dev's mentor Desh Prem Azad and chess trainer R.V. Gokhale receive the prestigious Dronacharya Award at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

title: Guru Hanuman and Gurcharan Singh Receive 1987 Dronacharya Awards
description: Legendary wrestling guru Hanuman and boxing pioneer Gurcharan Singh are honored with the Dronacharya Award in New Delhi.

title: Syed Nayeemuddin and A. Ramana Rao Receive 1990 Dronacharya Awards
description: Football coach Syed Nayeemuddin and volleyball coach A. Ramana Rao receive the Dronacharya Award for stellar contributions to Indian sports.

title: Karan Singh and Shyam Sunder Rao Conferred 1995 Dronacharya Awards
description: Athletics coach Karan Singh and volleyball maestro Shyam Sunder Rao receive the Dronacharya Award from the President of India.

title: Alferov, Kroemer, and Kilby Awarded 2000 Nobel Prize in Physics
description: Zhores Alferov, Herbert Kroemer, and Jack Kilby share the Nobel Prize in Physics for developing semiconductor heterostructures and the integrated circuit, founding modern information technology.

title: Cornell, Ketterle, and Wieman Win Nobel Prize for Bose-Einstein Condensate
description: Eric Cornell, Wolfgang Ketterle, and Carl Wieman receive the Nobel Prize in Physics for achieving Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute gases of alkali atoms.

title: Davis, Koshiba, and Giacconi Awarded 2002 Nobel Prize in Physics
description: Raymond Davis Jr. and Masatoshi Koshiba share the Nobel Prize in Physics for detecting cosmic neutrinos, alongside Riccardo Giacconi for discovering cosmic X-ray sources.

title: Abrikosov, Ginzburg, and Leggett Win Nobel Prize for Superconductivity
description: Alexei Abrikosov, Vitaly Ginzburg, and Anthony Leggett are awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for pioneering contributions to the theory of superconductors and superfluids.

title: Gross, Politzer, and Wilczek Win Nobel Prize for Asymptotic Freedom
description: David Gross, David Politzer, and Frank Wilczek receive the Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering asymptotic freedom in the theory of the strong interaction.

title: Glauber, Hall, and Hansch Win Nobel Prize for Quantum Optics
description: Roy Glauber wins half the Nobel Prize in Physics for the quantum theory of optical coherence, with John Hall and Theodor Hansch sharing half for laser-based precision spectroscopy.

title: Mather and Smoot Awarded Nobel Prize for COBE Cosmic Microwave Discovery
description: John Mather and George Smoot receive the Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering the blackbody form and anisotropy of the cosmic microwave background radiation.

title: Albert Fert and Peter Grunberg Win Nobel Prize for Giant Magnetoresistance
description: Albert Fert and Peter Grunberg receive the Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering giant magnetoresistance, enabling high-density computer hard disk drives.

title: Nambu, Kobayashi, and Maskawa Awarded Nobel Prize for Broken Symmetry
description: Yoichiro Nambu wins half the Nobel Prize in Physics for spontaneous broken symmetry, with Makoto Kobayashi and Toshihide Maskawa sharing half for predicting three quark families.

title: Kao, Boyle, and Smith Win Nobel Prize for Fiber Optics and CCD Sensor
description: Charles Kao receives half the Nobel Prize in Physics for fiber optic communications, while Willard Boyle and George Smith share half for inventing the CCD imaging sensor.

title: Olga Tokarczuk and Peter Handke Awarded Nobel Prizes in Literature
description: The Swedish Academy announces Polish novelist Olga Tokarczuk as the 2018 laureate and Austrian writer Peter Handke as the 2019 Nobel Prize in Literature recipient.

title: American Poet Louise Gluck Awarded 2020 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Louise Gluck receives the Nobel Prize in Literature for her unmistakable poetic voice that with austere beauty makes individual existence universal.

title: Zanzibar-Born Novelist Abdulrazak Gurnah Awarded 2021 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Abdulrazak Gurnah is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for his uncompromising and compassionate penetration of the effects of colonialism and refugee fate.

title: French Memoirist Annie Ernaux Awarded 2022 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Annie Ernaux receives the Nobel Prize in Literature for the courage and clinical acuity with which she uncovers the roots, estrangements, and collective restraints of personal memory.

title: Norwegian Playwright Jon Fosse Awarded 2023 Nobel Prize in Literature
description: Jon Fosse is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for his innovative plays and prose which give voice to the unsayable in contemporary theatre and fiction.

title: Wilson Jones Conferred 1996 Dronacharya Award for Billiards Coaching
description: Former world billiards champion Wilson Jones is honored with the Dronacharya Award for mentoring generations of Indian cueists.

title: Gurdial Singh Bhangu Conferred 2000 Dronacharya Award for Hockey Coaching
description: Women's hockey coach Gurdial Singh Bhangu receives the Dronacharya Award at Rashtrapati Bhavan on National Sports Day.

title: Sunny Thomas Conferred 2001 Dronacharya Award for Shooting Coaching
description: National shooting coach Sunny Thomas receives the Dronacharya Award after guiding Indian marksmanship onto the world stage.

title: Sarah Hughes Skates Flawless Long Program to Win Olympic Figure Skating Gold
description: Sixteen-year-old American Sarah Hughes lands seven triple jumps to rally from fourth place and capture Olympic women's figure skating gold in Salt Lake City.

title: Canada Defeats United States 5-2 to End 50-Year Men's Olympic Hockey Drought
description: Canada defeats the United States 5-2 in Salt Lake City to capture their first men's Olympic ice hockey gold medal in fifty years, led by Joe Sakic.

title: M.K. Kaushik Conferred 2005 Dronacharya Award for Women's Hockey
description: Olympic gold medalist M.K. Kaushik receives the Dronacharya Award after coaching the Indian women's hockey team to Commonwealth and Afro-Asian titles.

title: Shaun White Captures Maiden Olympic Halfpipe Gold in Bardonecchia
description: Nineteen-year-old Shaun White puts down a 46.8-point run in Bardonecchia to win his first Olympic snowboard halfpipe gold medal in Turin.

title: Shizuka Arakawa Becomes First Japanese Figure Skating Olympic Champion
description: Shizuka Arakawa lands an iconic Ina Bauer sequence in Turin to win the ladies' singles gold medal, becoming Japan's first Olympic figure skating champion.

title: Sweden Edges Finland 3-2 to Win Men's Ice Hockey Olympic Gold in Turin
description: Nicklas Lidstrom scores early in the third period as Sweden defeats rival Finland 3-2 to win the men's Olympic ice hockey tournament.

title: R.D. Singh Conferred 2006 Dronacharya Award for Paralympic Athletics
description: Paralympic athletics coach R.D. Singh, mentor of gold medalist Devendra Jhajharia, receives the Dronacharya Award at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

title: Shaun White Unveils Double McTwist 1260 to Retain Olympic Halfpipe Crown
description: Having already secured gold, Shaun White executes the revolutionary Double McTwist 1260 on his victory lap to defend his Olympic halfpipe title in Vancouver.

title: Kim Yuna Shatters World Record Score to Win Olympic Figure Skating Gold
description: South Korea's Kim Yuna delivers an unforgettable, technically sublime free skate to score a record 228.56 points and win Olympic gold in Vancouver.

title: Sidney Crosby Scores Golden Goal in Overtime for Canada at Vancouver Games
description: Sidney Crosby scores at 7:40 of sudden-death overtime to beat the United States 3-2 and deliver Olympic men's hockey gold for host nation Canada.

title: Yuzuru Hanyu Becomes First Asian Man to Win Olympic Figure Skating Gold
description: Nineteen-year-old Japanese star Yuzuru Hanyu overcomes two falls in his free skate to become Japan's first men's singles Olympic figure skating champion in Sochi.

title: Mikaela Shiffrin Becomes Youngest Slalom Champion in Olympic History
description: Eighteen-year-old American Mikaela Shiffrin masters the Rosa Khutor course to win Olympic slalom gold, becoming the youngest slalom champion in history.

title: Canada Blanks Sweden 3-0 to Defend Men's Olympic Ice Hockey Gold in Sochi
description: Carey Price stops all 24 shots as Canada shuts out Sweden 3-0 in the men's hockey final, completing an undefeated tournament run in Sochi.

title: Chloe Kim Dominates Snowboard Halfpipe at Age Seventeen in PyeongChang
description: Seventeen-year-old American Chloe Kim scores 98.25 points on her final run to capture Olympic snowboard halfpipe gold near her family's homeland.

title: Shaun White Captures Third Halfpipe Gold with Dramatic Final-Run 97.75
description: Shaun White lands back-to-back 1440s on the final run of the competition to score 97.75 and win a historic third Olympic snowboard halfpipe gold medal.

title: Yuzuru Hanyu Becomes First Man in 66 Years to Retain Olympic Figure Skating Title
description: Yuzuru Hanyu skates to Seimei in PyeongChang to defend his Olympic men's singles figure skating title, the first repeat champion since Dick Button in 1952.

title: Ester Ledecka Stuns Alpine Skiing World to Win Olympic Super-G by 0.01 Seconds
description: Czech snowboarder Ester Ledecka borrows skis to shock defending champion Anna Veith by one-hundredth of a second in the greatest upset in Winter Olympic history.

title: Oxford Ends Seven-Year Cambridge Dominance in 146th Boat Race
description: Oxford pulls clear through Barnes to win the 146th Boat Race on the River Thames by three lengths, ending Cambridge's seven-year streak.

title: Cambridge Recovers from Clash of Blades to Win 147th Boat Race
description: Cambridge survives an early clash of oars near the Mile Post to pull away and defeat Oxford by two-and-a-half lengths.

title: Oxford Overcomes Cambridge by Two-Thirds of a Length in Boat Race
description: Oxford holds off Cambridge in a grueling side-by-side battle along the Championship Course to win the 148th Boat Race.

title: FR Yugoslavia Defeats Argentina in Overtime to Retain FIBA World Championship
description: Dejan Bodiroga scores nine consecutive points late in regulation as Yugoslavia rallies to defeat Argentina 84-77 in overtime in Indianapolis.

title: Oxford Edges Cambridge by One Foot in Closest Boat Race in History
description: In the closest finish in modern Boat Race history, Oxford cox Acer Nethercott steers the Dark Blues to victory by just one foot over Cambridge.

title: Cambridge Capitalizes on Oxford Oar Clash to Win 150th Boat Race
description: Cambridge takes advantage of a catastrophic clash of blades near Hammersmith Bridge to win the historic 150th Boat Race.

title: Oxford Overwhelms Heaviest Crew in Boat Race History
description: Oxford defeats the heaviest Cambridge crew in history by two lengths to capture the 151st Boat Race along the River Thames.

title: Oxford Dominates Rain-Lashed 152nd Boat Race by Five Lengths
description: Oxford handles blustery wind and choppy waters with technical mastery to defeat Cambridge by five lengths on the Championship Course.

title: Cambridge Survives Brave Oxford Challenge to Win 153rd Boat Race
description: Cambridge pulls away past Chiswick Eyot to defeat Oxford by one-and-a-quarter lengths, securing their 79th victory in the series.

title: Sanjeeva Kumar Singh Receives 2007 Dronacharya Award for Archery
description: Chief archery coach Sanjeeva Kumar Singh is conferred the Dronacharya Award for mentoring India's recurve archers to international success.

title: Satpal Singh Conferred 2009 Dronacharya Award at Rashtrapati Bhavan
description: Wrestling guru Satpal Singh receives the Dronacharya Award from President Pratibha Patil for mentoring Olympic medalist Sushil Kumar.

title: A.K. Bansal Conferred 2010 Dronacharya Award for Junior Hockey
description: Hockey tactician A.K. Bansal receives the Dronacharya Award for steering India's junior men's team to continental championship victories.

title: Kevin Durant Powers United States Past Host Turkey to Win 2010 FIBA World Title
description: Kevin Durant scores 28 points in Istanbul as the United States defeats Turkey 81-64 to capture their first world championship since 1994.

title: Poornima Mahato Conferred 2013 Dronacharya Award for Archery
description: Former international archer Poornima Mahato receives the Dronacharya Award from President Pranab Mukherjee for training Deepika Kumari.

title: Mahabir Prasad Conferred 2014 Dronacharya Award for Wrestling
description: Wrestling coach Mahabir Prasad receives the Dronacharya Award at Rashtrapati Bhavan on National Sports Day in New Delhi.

title: Poland Stuns Brazil 3-1 in Front of Ecstatic Home Crowd in Katowice
description: Mariusz Wlazly leads host nation Poland to an emotional 3-1 victory over three-time defending champion Brazil at the Spodek arena.

title: United States Women's Hockey Team Beats Canada in Shootout for Olympic Gold
description: Jocelyne Lamoureux-Davidson scores a dazzling shootout goal to end Canada's 16-year Olympic reign and win women's hockey gold for the United States.

title: Eileen Gu Lands Historic Double Cork 1620 to Win Big Air Olympic Gold
description: Eighteen-year-old Eileen Gu stomps a left-side double cork 1620 on her final jump to win the inaugural freestyle skiing Big Air gold for host China.

title: Nathan Chen Shatters World Record to Win Men's Olympic Figure Skating Gold
description: American Nathan Chen lands five clean quadruple jumps to Elton John's Rocket Man, winning men's Olympic singles gold by more than 22 points in Beijing.

title: Finland Defeats Russian Olympic Committee to Win Maiden Men's Olympic Hockey Gold
description: Hannes Bjorninen scores the winning goal as Finland defeats the ROC 2-1 in Beijing to capture their first ever men's Olympic ice hockey gold medal.

title: Mumbai-Pune Expressway Becomes Fully Operational as India's First Access-Controlled Highway
description: The 93-kilometer Mumbai-Pune Expressway becomes fully operational, slashing travel time between Maharashtra's two economic hubs to two hours.

title: Oxford Conquers Terrible Weather to Win 154th Boat Race
description: In freezing rain and fierce crosswinds, Oxford outlasts Cambridge along the Championship Course to win by six lengths.

title: Oxford Breaks Early to Secure Emphatic 155th Boat Race Victory
description: Oxford breaks clear before Hammersmith Bridge to defeat Cambridge by three-and-a-half lengths on the Tideway.

title: Cambridge Overturns Weight Deficit to Win 156th Boat Race
description: Lighter Cambridge crew produces an astonishing comeback from nearly a length down to pass Oxford and win by one-and-a-third lengths.

title: Oxford Powers to Four-Length Victory in 157th Boat Race
description: Oxford dominates the Surrey station bend to establish an insurmountable lead and beat Cambridge by four lengths.

title: Cambridge Wins Dramatic 158th Boat Race Halted by River Swimmer
description: The 158th Boat Race is dramatically stopped halfway due to a protester in the water, with Cambridge winning after an oar-snapping restart.

title: Yamuna Expressway Inaugurated Connecting Greater Noida and Agra
description: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav inaugurates the 165-kilometer six-lane Yamuna Expressway, reducing travel time to Agra to under two hours.

title: Oxford Cruises to One-and-a-Half Length Boat Race Victory
description: Olympic bronze medalist Constantine Louloudis strokes Oxford to a controlled one-and-a-half length win over Cambridge.

title: Oxford Dominates 160th Boat Race After Early Cambridge Clash
description: Oxford pulls away after an early clash of blades knocks Cambridge five-man off his seat, securing an eleven-length victory.

title: Oxford Completes Historic Boat Race Clean Sweep on Tideway
description: Oxford wins the men's race by six-and-a-half lengths on the same day the Women's Boat Race is held on the Championship Course for the first time.

title: Cambridge Men End Oxford Streak in Rough Tideway Waters
description: Cambridge ends a three-year Oxford winning streak with a commanding two-and-a-half length victory through turbulent Thames water.

title: Bishweshwar Nandi Conferred 2016 Dronacharya Award for Gymnastics
description: Gymnastics coach Bishweshwar Nandi receives the Dronacharya Award after guiding Dipa Karmakar to fourth place in vault at the Rio Olympics.

title: Oxford Smashes Course Record to Win 163rd Boat Race
description: Oxford clocks sixteen minutes and 59 seconds to break the Tideway course record and claim their fourth win in five years.

title: Cambridge Dominates 164th Boat Race by Three Lengths
description: Cambridge takes control early and pulls away along the Surrey bend to defeat Oxford by three lengths on the Championship Course.

title: Chenanda Achaiah Kuttappa Receives 2018 Dronacharya Award for Boxing
description: Chief boxing coach C.A. Kuttappa is presented the Dronacharya Award by President Ram Nath Kovind at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

title: Double Olympic Champion James Cracknell Wins Boat Race for Cambridge at Age 46
description: Forty-six-year-old double Olympic champion James Cracknell becomes the oldest competitor in Boat Race history, rowing Cambridge to victory.

title: Sanjay Bhardwaj Conferred 2019 Dronacharya Award for Cricket Coaching
description: Prominent cricket coach Sanjay Bhardwaj receives the Dronacharya Award at Rashtrapati Bhavan for mentoring Gautam Gambhir and Amit Mishra.

title: Cambridge Edges Oxford in Closed-Door Boat Race at River Great Ouse
description: Relocated to Ely due to structural concerns over Hammersmith Bridge, Cambridge holds off Oxford by three-quarters of a length.

title: Oxford Breaks Five-Year Cambridge Reign in 167th Boat Race
description: Oxford sets a new course record of sixteen minutes and 42 seconds to defeat Cambridge and win their first Boat Race in five years.

title: Cambridge Overcomes Aggressive Steering Warning to Win 168th Boat Race
description: Cambridge survives multiple umpire warnings for aggressive line steering along the Championship Course to defeat Oxford by one-and-a-third lengths.

title: Phil Taylor Claims Record Fifteenth World Darts Championship
description: The Power Phil Taylor crushes Simon Whitlock 7-3 at Alexandra Palace to capture an unprecedented 15th world darts title.

title: Adrian Lewis Hits Nine-Dart Finish on Way to Maiden World Darts Title
description: Adrian Lewis hits a historic nine-darter in the opening set and defeats Gary Anderson 7-5 to become PDC world champion at age twenty-five.

title: Adrian Lewis Retains World Darts Championship Over Andy Hamilton
description: Adrian Lewis defeats Stoke-on-Trent rival Andy Hamilton 7-3 to become only the third player to successfully defend a PDC world title.

title: Phil Taylor Rallies from Behind to Win Sixteenth World Darts Crown
description: Phil Taylor overcomes a 4-2 deficit against Michael van Gerwen to win five consecutive sets and capture his 16th and final world title.

title: Ronnie O'Sullivan Retains World Snooker Championship After Year-Long Sabbatical
description: The Rocket Ronnie O'Sullivan defeats Barry Hawkins 18-12 at the Crucible Theatre to win his fifth world championship after playing just one match all season.

title: Twenty-Four-Year-Old Michael van Gerwen Becomes Youngest PDC World Champion
description: Michael van Gerwen defeats Peter Wright 7-4 to become the youngest PDC World Darts Champion in history at Alexandra Palace.

title: Gary Anderson Outlasts Phil Taylor in Thrilling Deciding Sets for World Title
description: Flying Scotsman Gary Anderson survives two bounce-outs and defeats 16-time champion Phil Taylor 7-6 to claim his maiden world title.

title: Gary Anderson Hits Nine-Darter and Defends World Darts Crown Over Lewis
description: Gary Anderson defeats Adrian Lewis 7-5 in the Alexandra Palace final to become only the fourth player to retain the PDC World Championship.

title: Agra-Lucknow Expressway Inaugurated with Mirage 2000 Fighter Jet Landings
description: The 302-kilometer Agra-Lucknow Expressway opens with Indian Air Force fighter jets landing on a dedicated runway strip in Unnao.

title: Michael van Gerwen Sets Record Tournament Average in Second World Title Win
description: Michael van Gerwen defeats defending champion Gary Anderson 7-3 with an average of 107.79 to capture his second PDC world crown.

title: Former Electrician Rob Cross Stuns Phil Taylor in World Final Fairytale
description: In his debut professional year, Rob Cross routs retiring legend Phil Taylor 7-2 to win the PDC World Championship at Alexandra Palace.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Inaugurates 135-Kilometer Eastern Peripheral Expressway
description: The Kundli-Ghaziabad-Palwal expressway opens in Baghpat, diverting non-destined commercial traffic away from the National Capital Region.

title: Western Peripheral Expressway Fully Opened by Prime Minister Narendra Modi
description: The 83-kilometer Kundli-Manesar stretch of the Western Peripheral Expressway is inaugurated, completing the mega ring road encircling Delhi.

title: Michael van Gerwen Overwhelms Michael Smith to Win Third World Darts Title
description: Michael van Gerwen cruises to a 7-3 victory over Michael Smith to capture his third career PDC World Darts Championship.

title: Peter Wright Topples Michael van Gerwen to Win Maiden World Darts Title
description: Snakebite Peter Wright defeats defending champion Michael van Gerwen 7-3 to claim an emotional first PDC world title at age forty-nine.

title: Durgam Cheruvu Cable-Stayed Bridge Inaugurated in Hyderabad
description: Minister K.T. Rama Rao inaugurates the 238-meter cable-stayed bridge over Durgam Cheruvu, easing connectivity to Hitec City in Hyderabad.

title: Gerwyn Price Becomes First Welsh World Darts Champion in Behind-Closed-Doors Final
description: Former rugby player Gerwyn Price defeats Gary Anderson 7-3 to become the first Welsh PDC world champion and new world number one.

title: Delhi-Meerut Expressway Dedicated to Nation Reducing Travel Time to 45 Minutes
description: Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari formally dedicates the 82-kilometer fourteen-lane Delhi-Meerut Expressway to the nation.

title: Peter Wright Clinches Second World Darts Championship Over Michael Smith
description: Peter Wright wins nine of the final ten legs to defeat Michael Smith 7-5 and capture his second PDC World Darts Championship.

title: Michael Smith Hits Greatest Leg in Darts History on Way to Maiden World Title
description: Michael Smith hits a sensational nine-darter right after Van Gerwen misses double 12, going on to win 7-4 for his first PDC world championship.

title: Eric Bristow Captures First World Darts Championship Title
description: Eric Bristow defeats Bobby George 5-3 in sets at the Jollees Club in Stoke-on-Trent to claim his maiden World Darts Championship.

title: Cambridge Breaks Oxford Ten-Year Streak in 132nd Boat Race
description: Cambridge University ends Oxford's historic ten-year winning run, crossing the finish line at Mortlake seven lengths ahead.

title: Oxford Wins 133rd Boat Race Following Infamous Mutiny Dispute
description: Oxford's reserve-laden crew defeats Cambridge in rough water after American rowers walked out over training selections.

title: Cambridge Rows to Record-Breaking Triumph in 139th Boat Race
description: Cambridge sets a new course record of 17 minutes flat, smashing Oxford by 3.5 lengths to begin a new dynasty.

title: Cambridge Rallies to Capture 142nd University Boat Race
description: Cambridge overcomes an early Oxford advantage along the Surrey bend to win by two-and-three-quarter lengths.

title: Cambridge Wins 143rd Boat Race over Dark Blues
description: Cambridge maintains its unbeaten run of the 1990s, winning by two lengths over Oxford on the Thames.

title: Cambridge Smashes Course Record Winning 144th Boat Race
description: Cambridge shatters the course record, clocking 16 minutes 19 seconds to win by three lengths over Oxford.

title: Cambridge Completes Seven-in-a-Row in 145th Boat Race
description: Cambridge University beats Oxford by three-and-a-half lengths to complete a run of seven straight victories.

title: John Walton Wins 2001 World Professional Darts Championship
description: John Walton defeats Ted Hankey 6-2 at Lakeside Country Club to capture his maiden world darts title.

title: Foundation Stone Laid for Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad
description: The Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad is officially founded as one of eight new IITs established by the Ministry of Human Resource Development.

title: Stuart Bingham Defeats Shaun Murphy to Win Maiden World Snooker Championship
description: Thirty-eight-year-old Stuart Bingham defeats Shaun Murphy 18-15 at the Crucible Theatre to become the oldest first-time world snooker champion since 1978.

title: Indian Institute of Technology Palakkad Inaugurates First Academic Batch
description: IIT Palakkad begins functioning from the Ahalia Integrated Campus in Kozhippara, establishing Kerala's first Indian Institute of Technology.

title: Mark Selby Defeats Ding Junhui to Win Second World Snooker Championship
description: Mark Selby fends off Ding Junhui 18-14 in Sheffield to win his second world title on the same night his hometown club Leicester City wins the Premier League.

title: Indian Institute of Technology Dharwad Formally Inaugurated in Karnataka
description: Union ministers and state dignitaries officially inaugurate IIT Dharwad at its transit campus on the WALMI campus in Belur industrial area.

title: Mark Selby Rallies Past John Higgins to Retain World Snooker Championship
description: Mark Selby overcomes a 10-4 deficit to defeat four-time champion John Higgins 18-15, becoming only the fourth player to defend a world title at the Crucible.

title: Mark Williams Defeats John Higgins 18-16 in Epic Crucible World Final
description: Forty-three-year-old Mark Williams holds off John Higgins in a dramatic 18-16 thriller to win his third World Snooker Championship, 15 years after his second.

title: Mark Selby Outlasts Shaun Murphy to Win Fourth World Snooker Championship
description: Mark Selby controls the tactical exchanges to defeat Shaun Murphy 18-15 before a capacity Crucible crowd and capture his fourth world title.

title: Ronnie O'Sullivan Equals Stephen Hendry Record with Seventh World Snooker Title
description: At age forty-six, Ronnie O'Sullivan defeats Judd Trump 18-13 at the Crucible Theatre to equal Stephen Hendry's modern record of seven world championships.

title: Sohna-Dausa Stretch of Delhi-Mumbai Expressway Inaugurated by PM Modi
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurates the 246-kilometer first section of the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway in Dausa, cutting Delhi-Jaipur travel time.

title: Bengaluru-Mysuru Access-Controlled Expressway Dedicated to Nation by PM Modi
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi dedicates the 118-kilometer 10-lane Bengaluru-Mysuru Expressway in Mandya, cutting travel time to 75 minutes.

title: Eric Bristow Retains World Darts Championship at Jollees
description: The 'Crafty Cockney' Eric Bristow beats John Lowe 5-3 in the final to retain his world professional darts title.

title: Jocky Wilson Wins Emotional First World Darts Championship
description: Scotland's Jocky Wilson overcomes John Lowe 5-3 in a classic final to become world darts champion.

title: Keith Deller Becomes Youngest Qualifier to Win World Darts Championship
description: Unseeded 23-year-old qualifier Keith Deller checks out 138 against Eric Bristow to win the World Darts Championship 6-5.

title: Eric Bristow Crushes Dave Whitcombe to Win Third World Darts Title
description: Eric Bristow produces a masterful display, whitewashing Dave Whitcombe 7-0 at the Lakeside Country Club in Frimley Green.

title: Eric Bristow Clinches Fourth World Darts Championship at Lakeside
description: Eric Bristow defeats John Lowe 6-2 in the final to claim his fourth World Professional Darts crown.

title: Eric Bristow Defeats Dave Whitcombe for Fifth World Darts Title
description: Eric Bristow beats Dave Whitcombe 6-0 to secure his fifth BDO World Professional Darts Championship.

title: John Lowe Defeats Eric Bristow to Claim Second World Darts Title
description: John Lowe defeats his perennial rival Eric Bristow 6-4 in an unforgettable final at Lakeside Country Club.

title: Bob Anderson Clinches World Darts Championship at Lakeside
description: Bob 'The Limestone Cowboy' Anderson defeats John Lowe 6-4 in sets to become the world professional darts champion.

title: Jocky Wilson Defeats Eric Bristow to Win Second World Darts Crown
description: Scotland's Jocky Wilson wins an epic 6-4 contest against Eric Bristow to claim his second World Darts Championship.

title: Phil Taylor Stuns Eric Bristow to Win Maiden World Darts Title
description: Protege Phil Taylor shocks his mentor Eric Bristow with a 6-1 thrashing at Lakeside to win his first World Darts Championship.

title: Dennis Priestley Captures World Darts Championship on Debut
description: Dennis 'The Menace' Priestley whitewashes five-time champion Eric Bristow 6-0 in the final at Lakeside.

title: Phil Taylor Pips Mike Gregory in Sudden-Death World Darts Final
description: Phil Taylor defeats Mike Gregory 6-5 in a sudden-death leg after Gregory misses six darts to win the world championship.

title: John Lowe Wins Third World Darts Title in Three Different Decades
description: John Lowe beats Alan Warriner 6-3 to become the first player to win world titles in the 1970s, 1980s, and 1990s.

title: John Part Becomes First Non-UK Player to Win BDO World Darts Championship
description: Canada's John Part defeats Bobby George 6-0 at Lakeside, becoming the first player from North America to win a world darts title.

title: Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar Commences Academic Operations
description: IIT Gandhinagar begins its first academic session operating temporarily from the Vishwakarma Government Engineering College campus in Chandkheda.

title: Christian Kist Wins BDO World Darts Championship as Qualifier
description: Dutch qualifier Christian Kist defeats Tony O'Shea 7-5 in a gripping final to become world darts champion.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Lays Foundation Stone for AIIMS Gorakhpur
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi lays the foundation stone for the All India Institute of Medical Sciences at Gorakhpur to serve eastern Uttar Pradesh.

title: Indian Institute of Technology Jammu Commences Classes for Founding Batch
description: IIT Jammu begins its academic journey at its temporary campus in Paloura, Jammu, mentored by IIT Delhi.

title: Indian Institute of Technology Bhilai Inaugurates First Academic Session
description: IIT Bhilai commences operations in Chhattisgarh, mentored by IIT Hyderabad, expanding advanced technical education in central India.

title: Foundation Stone Laid for AIIMS Bathinda by Prime Minister Narendra Modi
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi lays the foundation stone of AIIMS Bathinda in Punjab, expanding tertiary medical education under PMSSY.

title: Richie Burnett Clinches World Darts Championship on Debut
description: Welshman Richie Burnett defeats Raymond van Barneveld 6-3 at Lakeside to claim the BDO World Darts title.

title: Steve Beaton Defeats Richie Burnett to Win World Darts Championship
description: Steve 'The Bronzed Adonis' Beaton defeats defending champion Richie Burnett 6-3 to win the world title.

title: Les Wallace Becomes First Left-Hander to Win World Darts Championship
description: Scotland's Les Wallace, wearing a traditional kilt, beats Marshall James 6-3 to become world darts champion.

title: Raymond van Barneveld Wins Thrilling Sudden-Death World Darts Final
description: Raymond van Barneveld edges Richie Burnett 6-5 in a sudden-death leg to become the first Dutchman to win the World Darts Championship.

title: Raymond van Barneveld Retains World Darts Championship at Lakeside
description: Raymond van Barneveld defeats Ronnie Baxter 6-5 in another gripping final to capture back-to-back world crowns.

title: Ted Hankey Routs Ronnie Baxter to Win Maiden World Darts Crown
description: 'The Count' Ted Hankey sweeps Ronnie Baxter 6-0 in sets at Lakeside, averaging a then-record 104 in the final.

title: Tony David Becomes First Australian to Win World Darts Championship
description: Tony David defeats Mervyn King 6-4 at Lakeside, making history as the first Australian to lift a world darts championship.

title: Raymond van Barneveld Captures Third World Darts Title at Lakeside
description: Raymond van Barneveld beats Ritchie Davies 6-3 to secure his third BDO World Darts Championship trophy.

title: Andy Fordham Wins Emotional World Darts Championship Final
description: 'The Viking' Andy Fordham rallies from 3-0 down to beat Mervyn King 6-3 in front of a thunderous Lakeside crowd.

title: Raymond van Barneveld Clinches Fourth Lakeside World Darts Championship
description: Raymond van Barneveld defeats Martin Adams 6-2 in the final to claim his fourth BDO World title.

title: Jelle Klaasen Becomes Youngest Ever World Darts Champion
description: At age 21, Dutch unseeded qualifier Jelle Klaasen upsets Raymond van Barneveld 7-5 to become the youngest world darts champion.

title: Martin Adams Wins Maiden World Darts Championship in Lakeside Thriller
description: 'Wolfie' Martin Adams survives an improbable comeback by Phill Nixon to win 7-6 in sets and claim his first world title.

title: Mark Webster Clinches BDO World Darts Championship for Wales
description: Welsh plumber Mark Webster defeats Simon Whitlock 7-5 in the final at Lakeside to win the world professional darts title.

title: Indian Institute of Technology Ropar Begins First Academic Session
description: IIT Ropar welcomes its inaugural batch of undergraduate engineering students at its transit campus in Rupnagar, Punjab.

title: Ted Hankey Captures Second World Darts Title Hitting 170 Checkout
description: Ted Hankey defeats Tony O'Shea 7-6 in an electric final featuring a maximum 170 checkout to win his second world crown.

title: Indian Institute of Management Rohtak Commences First Academic Session
description: IIM Rohtak begins classes as the eighth IIM and the first central management institute in the National Capital Region.

title: Scott Waites Stages Stunning Comeback to Win World Darts Title
description: Scott Waites roars back from 0-2 down in sets to defeat Tony O'Shea 7-1 at Lakeside to claim the BDO world championship.

title: Indian Institute of Technology Goa Welcomes Inaugural Student Batch
description: IIT Goa is inaugurated at the Goa Engineering College campus in Farmagudi, under the direct mentorship of IIT Bombay.

title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Lays Foundation Stone for AIIMS Bilaspur
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi lays the foundation stone for the 750-bed AIIMS Bilaspur in Himachal Pradesh to bolster healthcare in the hill state.

title: Foundation Stone Laid for AIIMS Deoghar in Jharkhand by Prime Minister Modi
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi lays the foundation stone for AIIMS Deoghar, bringing super-speciality medical care to Santhal Parganas.

title: Cliff Thorburn Becomes First Overseas World Snooker Champion in Modern Era
description: Canada's Cliff 'The Grinder' Thorburn defeats Alex Higgins 18-16 at the Crucible to become the first non-British world snooker champion.

title: Steve Davis Wins First World Snooker Championship at the Crucible
description: Steve Davis defeats Doug Mountjoy 18-12 at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield to claim his first world snooker crown.

title: Alex Higgins Wins Emotional Second World Snooker Title at Crucible
description: Alex 'Hurricane' Higgins defeats Ray Reardon 18-15 and sheds tears with his daughter in one of the most emotional moments in sport.

title: Steve Davis Routs Cliff Thorburn to Win Second World Snooker Crown
description: Steve Davis defeats Cliff Thorburn 18-6 in the final at the Crucible to win his second world snooker title.

title: Steve Davis Fends Off Jimmy White to Win Third World Snooker Title
description: Steve Davis resists a courageous comeback by Jimmy White to win 18-16 and secure his third World Snooker Championship.

title: Dennis Taylor Stuns Steve Davis on Final Black in 1985 Crucible Final
description: Dennis Taylor pots the final black ball past midnight to beat Steve Davis 18-17 in front of 18.5 million British TV viewers.

title: Indian Institute of Technology Bhubaneswar Holds Inaugural Classes
description: IIT Bhubaneswar initiates its first academic session under the mentorship of IIT Kharagpur, fostering higher technical education in Odisha.

title: Martin Adams Wins Second BDO World Darts Championship
description: Martin Adams defeats Dave Chisnall 7-5 in the final at Lakeside Country Club to capture his second world darts crown.

title: Indian Institute of Management Ranchi Commences Inaugural Academic Program
description: IIM Ranchi starts its first academic year, mentored by IIM Calcutta, bringing premier management education to Jharkhand.

title: Indian Institute of Management Raipur Formally Inaugurated in Chhattisgarh
description: IIM Raipur is officially inaugurated at the Government Engineering College Sejbahar transit campus.

title: Martin Adams Retains Lakeside World Darts Championship
description: Martin Adams edges Dean Winstanley 7-5 to become only the fourth player in history to successfully defend the BDO world title.

title: Stephen Bunting Dominates Alan Norris to Win World Darts Crown
description: Number one seed Stephen Bunting defeats Alan Norris 7-4 in the final at Frimley Green to capture the BDO world title.

title: Scott Mitchell Wins BDO World Darts Championship in Deciding Set
description: Dorset farmer Scott Mitchell beats Martin Adams 7-6 in a pulsating final set to lift his maiden world darts title.

title: Scott Waites Clinches Second BDO World Darts Title

title: Leo Bergere Wins Dramatic World Triathlon Championship Finals
description: French triathlete Leo Bergere wins the Championship Finals in Abu Dhabi, unexpectedly leaping to the overall world title.

title: Dorian Coninx Wins 2023 World Triathlon Championship in Pontevedra
description: French triathlete Dorian Coninx wins the Championship Finals in Pontevedra, Spain, to claim his first World Triathlon Championship.

title: Aurora Cunha Wins 1988 Tokyo Women's Marathon
description: Portugal's Aurora Cunha clocks 2:31:26 through Tokyo to win the 10th anniversary Tokyo International Women's Marathon.

title: India Senior Captures Third Challenger Trophy in Mohali
description: India Senior defeats India A by 12 runs at the PCA Stadium in Mohali to win the 1996-97 NKP Salve Challenger Trophy.

title: India Senior Completes Four-in-a-Row Challenger Trophy Wins
description: Sachin Tendulkar's India Senior defeats India B by 19 runs in Bangalore to claim their fourth consecutive Challenger Trophy title.

title: India B Halts Senior Streak to Win 1998 Challenger Trophy
description: VVS Laxman leads India B to an exciting five-wicket victory over India Senior at M. A. Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai to win the Challenger Trophy.

title: Hadi Saei Wins Maiden World Taekwondo Championship in Garmisch
description: Iranian taekwondo legend Hadi Saei captures his first lightweight world championship in Garmisch-Partenkirchen, Germany.

title: Avant-Garde Choreographer Chandralekha Conferred Akademi Ratna
description: Revolutionary dancer-choreographer Chandralekha is conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship for transforming modern Indian classical dance.

title: Steven Lopez Wins Third World Taekwondo Championship in Madrid
description: Steven Lopez captures the welterweight gold medal at the World Taekwondo Championships at the Palacio de Deportes in Madrid.

title: Steven Lopez Wins Historic Fourth World Taekwondo Title in Beijing
description: Steven Lopez becomes the first male practitioner to win four consecutive world titles at the World Taekwondo Championships in Beijing.

title: Lee Chang-hwan Wins 2009 World Archery Championship in Ulsan
description: South Korean archer Lee Chang-hwan wins the men's individual recurve world title at Munsu Archery Field in Ulsan, South Korea.

title: Brigitte Yague Wins Third World Taekwondo Title in Copenhagen
description: Spanish flyweight Brigitte Yague wins her third career gold medal at the World Taekwondo Championships in Copenhagen.

title: Servet Tazegul Wins 2011 World Taekwondo Championship
description: Turkish dynamic fighter Servet Tazegul captures the featherweight gold medal at the World Taekwondo Championships in Gyeongju.

title: Carnatic Flute Virtuoso N Ramani Conferred Akademi Ratna
description: Flute maestro N. Ramani is conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship at Rashtrapati Bhavan by President Pranab Mukherjee.

title: Lee Dae-hoon Retains World Taekwondo Championship in Puebla
description: Lee Dae-hoon of South Korea successfully defends his bantamweight world title at the Exhibition Center in Puebla, Mexico.

title: Servet Tazegul Wins Second World Taekwondo Championship
description: Olympic champion Servet Tazegul captures his second featherweight world title at the Traktor Ice Arena in Chelyabinsk, Russia.

title: Lee Dae-hoon Wins Third World Taekwondo Championship in Muju
description: Lee Dae-hoon captures his third world championship gold medal at the Taekwondowon arena in Muju, South Korea.

title: Jade Jones Wins Long-Awaited Maiden World Taekwondo Championship
description: Two-time Olympic champion Jade Jones completes her medal collection by winning her first world championship in Manchester.

title: Bradly Sinden Wins Great Britain's First Men's World Taekwondo Title
description: Bradly Sinden wins Great Britain's first-ever men's world taekwondo championship title at Manchester Arena.

title: Brady Ellison Wins Maiden World Archery Championship in 's-Hertogenbosch
description: American archer Brady Ellison captures his first individual recurve world championship in 's-Hertogenbosch, Netherlands.

title: Kim Woo-jin Wins Historic Triple Gold at World Archery Championships
description: Kim Woo-jin wins men's individual, team, and mixed team titles at the World Archery Championships in Yankton, South Dakota.

title: Mete Gazoz Wins 2023 World Archery Championship in Berlin
description: Olympic champion Mete Gazoz of Turkey wins the men's individual recurve world title at the Olympic Stadium in Berlin.

title: Liubov Klochko Wins 1989 Tokyo Women's Marathon
description: Soviet runner Liubov Klochko handles damp conditions to win the 1989 Tokyo International Women's Marathon in 2:31:33.

title: Kim Je-kyoung Wins Third World Taekwondo Title in Edmonton
description: South Korean heavyweight Kim Je-kyoung wins his third career gold medal at the World Taekwondo Championships in Edmonton, Canada.

title: India Senior Reclaims Challenger Trophy Title in Bangalore
description: India Senior captures the 1999-2000 NKP Salve Challenger Trophy with a dominant performance at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bangalore.

title: India Senior Wins Millennium 2000 Challenger Trophy
description: Sourav Ganguly's India Senior defeats India A by 25 runs at Chepauk in Chennai to win the 2000-01 Challenger Trophy championship.

title: India A Captures Maiden Challenger Trophy in Bangalore
description: Yuvraj Singh's India A pulls off a thrilling six-wicket victory over India Senior at the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium to lift their maiden Challenger Trophy.

title: Matthew Emmons Wins 2002 ISSF World Prone Rifle Championship
description: American marksman Matthew Emmons wins the men's 50m rifle prone gold medal at the ISSF World Shooting Championships in Lahti, Finland.

title: Abhinav Bindra Wins India's First ISSF World Shooting Championship
description: Abhinav Bindra wins the men's 10m air rifle gold medal at the ISSF World Shooting Championships in Zagreb, Croatia, a historic first for India.

title: Vincent Hancock Wins 2006 ISSF World Skeet Championship
description: Seventeen-year-old American prodigy Vincent Hancock wins the men's skeet title at the ISSF World Shooting Championships in Zagreb.

title: Jin Jong-oh Wins Double Gold at 2010 ISSF World Championships
description: South Korean shooting maestro Jin Jong-oh wins individual and team 50m pistol golds at the ISSF World Shooting Championships in Munich.

title: Carnatic Patriarch RK Srikantan Conferred Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship
description: Centenarian Carnatic vocalist R. K. Srikantan is honored with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship for eighty years of devotion to classicism.

title: Jin Jong-oh Smashes 50m Pistol World Record in Granada
description: South Korea's Jin Jong-oh scores 583 to smash a 34-year-old world record and win 50m pistol gold at the ISSF World Championships in Granada.

title: Bharatanatyam Master CV Chandrasekhar Conferred Akademi Ratna
description: Veteran Bharatanatyam dancer and guru C. V. Chandrasekhar is conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in New Delhi.

title: Sergey Kamenskiy Wins 2018 ISSF 10m Air Rifle World Title
description: Russian marksman Sergey Kamenskiy captures the men's 10m air rifle gold medal at the ISSF World Shooting Championships in Changwon.

title: Vincent Hancock Wins Fourth ISSF World Skeet Title in Changwon
description: Vincent Hancock hits a perfect final round to win his fourth men's skeet world title at the ISSF World Championships in Changwon.

title: Panipak Wongpattanakit Wins Second World Taekwondo Championship
description: Thailand's Panipak Wongpattanakit dominates the women's flyweight final to win her second world title in Manchester.

title: Daniela Souza Wins 2022 World Taekwondo Championship
description: Daniela Souza wins the women's flyweight gold medal at the World Taekwondo Championships in Guadalajara, Mexico.

title: Carlos Sansores Wins World Taekwondo Heavyweight Gold in Guadalajara
description: Mexican heavyweight Carlos Sansores wins the world taekwondo championship on home soil at the Centro Acuatico in Guadalajara.

title: Merve Dincel Wins 2023 World Taekwondo Championship in Baku
description: Turkish flyweight Merve Dincel captures the women's flyweight gold medal at the Baku Crystal Hall in Azerbaijan.

title: Cheick Sallah Cisse Wins World Taekwondo Heavyweight Title in Baku
description: Olympic champion Cheick Sallah Cisse of Ivory Coast wins the men's heavyweight title at the World Taekwondo Championships in Baku.

title: Victor Lindgren Wins 2023 ISSF 10m Air Rifle World Championship
description: Swedish teenager Victor Lindgren wins the men's 10m air rifle gold medal at the ISSF World Shooting Championships in Baku, Azerbaijan.
